Medical management corrects the underlying hormonal disturbance in the majority of cases without the mortality, morbidity, and cost of surgery. A complete understanding of the menstrual cycle and hormonal mechanisms enables successful medical management of almost all DUB cases.
options: The first-line treatment in all women with DUB over 40 years
Offered to all women who complete their family, regardless of medical therapy response
Last-line therapy for failed medical treatment or confirmed pelvic pathology
Performed before medical therapy in perimenopausal women with irregular bleeding
The treatment of choice in adolescents with severe anovulatory DUB

questions.explanation: A threatened abortion is characterised by vaginal bleeding in early pregnancy with a closed cervical os and a viable fetus confirmed on ultrasound, distinguishing it from inevitable abortion where the cervix is open. Many threatened abortions proceed to a normal continuing pregnancy with conservative management. Close follow-up with repeat ultrasound and clinical review is appropriate.
questions.question: A 10-week pregnant patient presents with light vaginal bleeding and mild cramping. Ultrasound shows a viable intrauterine pregnancy with fetal cardiac activity and a closed cervix. What is the most appropriate classification of this presentation?

questions.explanation: An inadvertent cystotomy during gynaecological surgery requires immediate recognition and formal closure in two layers (mucosa and muscularis) with an absorbable suture. The repair may be performed laparoscopically or via open surgery. Prolonged urinary catheter drainage (7–14 days) is maintained to allow bladder healing and reduce fistula risk.
questions.question: The management of an inadvertent cystotomy (bladder entry) during laparoscopic hysterectomy requires:
options: Immediate open conversion and formal repair of the bladder
Venous thromboembolism in the early postpartum period
questions.question: A woman is prescribed combined oral contraceptives 3 weeks postpartum but is not breastfeeding. The MOST important reason for delaying initiation until this time is the increased risk of:
questions.explanation: The early postpartum period is associated with a physiologically hypercoagulable state, and combined oral contraceptives further increase venous thromboembolism risk, so their initiation is typically delayed until at least three weeks postpartum in non-breastfeeding women to reduce this compounded risk.

Kallmann syndrome results from failure of GnRH neuron migration during development, which is anatomically linked to olfactory bulb development, causing the combination of anosmia and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with low FSH, LH, and testosterone. This central cause of infertility differs from primary testicular failure, where FSH and LH would typically be elevated. Treatment involves gonadotropin or pulsatile GnRH therapy to induce fertility.
questions.question: A 21-year-old male presents to an infertility clinic unable to smell, with low testosterone and low FSH and LH. Which diagnosis links his anosmia to his hypogonadism?

questions.explanation: Endometrioid ovarian carcinoma shows histological similarity to endometrial carcinoma and has a documented association with it. It relates mainly to endometrioid ovarian tumour and thecal cysts, and women with endometrial cancer have an increased risk of developing endometrioid-type ovarian malignancy.
questions.question: Endometrioid ovarian carcinoma is MOST closely related pathologically to which other malignancy?

options: Dependence on time of blood sampling
Wide fluctuation across the cycle daily
Rapid changes with acute illness states
Stable levels throughout the menstrual cycle
questions.explanation: Anti-Mullerian hormone, secreted by small antral follicles, remains relatively stable throughout the menstrual cycle, unlike FSH which fluctuates and must be measured on a specific cycle day, making AMH a more convenient and reliable marker of ovarian reserve that can be tested at any time. This stability is a key practical advantage in fertility assessment. Low AMH suggests diminished ovarian reserve, though it does not predict natural conception probability precisely.
questions.question: A woman undergoing fertility assessment has anti-Mullerian hormone measured to estimate ovarian reserve. Which characteristic of AMH makes it MOST useful for this purpose compared with FSH?

options: Permanent sterilization after 5 years of continuous use
Enhancement of erection quality through sustained penile pressure
Protection against cervical cancer by blocking all carcinogens
Significant protection against sexually transmitted infections including HIV
Increasing sperm quality by keeping the scrotum at body temperature
questions.explanation: Male latex condoms, when used correctly and consistently (every time, from start to finish of intercourse), provide significant protection against STIs including HIV, gonorrhoea, chlamydia, and trichomoniasis. They are the only contraceptive method that simultaneously prevents both pregnancy and STI transmission. This dual protection makes them essential in high-risk populations.
questions.question: Male latex condoms, when used correctly and consistently, have an additional benefit beyond contraception. This benefit is BEST described as:
The dominant follicle of a menstrual cycle is selected because it is MOST sensitive to:
questions.explanation: During follicular recruitment, multiple follicles begin to grow, but only the most FSH-sensitive follicle — the one with the highest density of FSH receptors and greatest ability to aromatize androgens to oestrogens — becomes the dominant follicle. As FSH levels fall (due to oestrogen and inhibin negative feedback), only the dominant follicle, with its superior FSH sensitivity, continues to develop, while others undergo atresia.
options: LH at the time of ovulation
Inhibin produced by the corpus luteum
Oestradiol secreted by the adrenal gland

questions.explanation: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumours secrete androgens, initially causing defeminisation with secondary amenorrhoea, then progressive virilisation including hirsutism, clitoral enlargement, and deepening of the voice. These tumours are classified in the Sertoli-Leydig cell group of sex cord stromal tumours.
questions.question: A Sertoli-Leydig cell tumour (androblastoma) characteristically produces which hormonal effect?

questions.explanation: Under the revised FIGO staging, Stage IB1 cervical cancer is a clinically visible lesion confined to the cervix measuring up to 2 cm in greatest dimension. Larger confined lesions are staged IB2 and IB3, while parametrial extension defines Stage IIB.
questions.question: FIGO Stage IB1 cervical cancer is defined as invasive carcinoma confined to the cervix with a greatest dimension of:
Vanishing testis syndrome in an XY fetus, where the testis develops normally and then undergoes atrophy in utero, most likely results in which phenotypic outcome at birth?
options: Ambiguous genitalia with rudimentary Müllerian structures
Complete female phenotype with uterus and vagina
questions.explanation: Vanishing testis syndrome occurs when the fetal testis (XY) develops initially (so AMH is produced, causing Müllerian regression) and then undergoes atrophy (from torsion, thrombosis, or viral infection). If atrophy occurs after AMH secretion but before testosterone production is sufficient, the result is a female external phenotype (default) with absent Müllerian structures (because AMH was produced). The degree of male internal structure development depends on timing of the atrophy.

options: Cord prolapse from small uterine cavity
Shoulder dystocia from excessive fetal weight
questions.question: A 16-year-old girl presents to a GOPD with confirmed pregnancy at 18 weeks. Her pelvis is clinically assessed as contracted. Which specific obstetric outcome is she MOST at risk for due to her immature pelvic anatomy?
questions.explanation: Adolescent females whose pelvic growth is incomplete face cephalopelvic disproportion (CPD) when the fetal head is too large to negotiate the underdeveloped bony pelvis, leading to obstructed labour. CPD is the primary mechanical complication driving increased operative delivery rates, prolonged labour, obstetric fistula, and peripheral nerve injuries in teenage mothers. It is the anatomical basis for most adverse adolescent birth outcomes.

GnRH analogues suppress pituitary gonadotrophin secretion, lowering serum oestradiol to menopausal levels and causing cessation of menstruation. They are highly effective but their use is limited to 6 months due to the hypo-oestrogenic side effects (bone mass loss, hot flushes, vaginal dryness). Long-term therapy requires oestrogen/progestin add-back to prevent bone loss, though this adds cost and complexity. Expense is also a formidable obstacle.
options: Limited to 6 months from bone loss
They cause hyper-oestrogenism with increased endometrial proliferation
They increase LH surges causing menorrhagia
They are not effective in ovulatory DUB
questions.question: GnRH analogues (e.g., Depot Leuprolide) are used in DUB with which MAJOR limitation?

options: Tumour shrinks the tube by fibrosis
Tumour distends lumen and protrudes through fimbria
Tumour replaces the tube entirely with solid mass
questions.explanation: In fallopian tube cancer, the tumour usually distends the lumen of the tube and may protrude through the fimbrial end, giving the tube a retort-shaped appearance resembling a hydrosalpinx. This gross morphological characteristic often causes the preoperative diagnosis to be missed as the mass may be interpreted as a benign tubal condition.
questions.question: The fallopian tube in cancer may become retort-shaped or resemble a hydrosalpinx because:

options: Start directly with the pelvic examination
Ask a nurse to take all the history
Defer examination to a female colleague
Begin with family and medical history first
Perform only abdominal examination without pelvic assessment
questions.explanation: For shy or introverted patients, beginning with non-intimate past medical and family history gives the patient time to build confidence and rapport before sensitive questions are asked. This approach is endorsed in standard gynaecological teaching to facilitate more complete and accurate disclosure. Skipping history undermines diagnosis.
questions.question: A male gynaecologist is about to examine a shy, introverted patient. The MOST appropriate approach to put her at ease is to:

options: Dense calcification within the cyst wall
Sebaceous material within a dermoid cyst
Old degenerated blood products within the cyst
Serous fluid within a simple cyst
questions.explanation: The ground-glass appearance of an endometrioma reflects accumulated old degenerated menstrual blood products within the cyst, often described as a chocolate cyst on gross pathology. This distinguishes it from simple serous cysts, which appear anechoic, and dermoid cysts, which show characteristic fat-fluid levels or calcification. Recognising this pattern aids preoperative diagnosis and surgical planning.
questions.question: An endometrioma is identified on ultrasound as a homogeneous, low-level, ground-glass echogenic cyst. What is the underlying pathological basis for this classic ultrasound appearance?

options: Hormonal disruption from chronic pelvic inflammation after the procedure
Psychological suggestion causing women to believe intercourse is impossible
Chronic infection converting the vaginal epithelium into scar tissue preventing lubrication
Destruction of clitoral tissue and nerve supply impairing arousal, lubrication, orgasmic response
FGM has no proven effect on sexual function in adequately counselled women
questions.explanation: FGM Types I–IV cause variable degrees of clitoral excision, destruction, or infibulation. The clitoris is the primary organ of female sexual arousal and orgasm, containing approximately 8,000 sensory nerve endings. Its partial or complete removal directly impairs arousal, lubrication, and orgasmic capacity. Infibulation (Type III) additionally causes dyspareunia from introital stenosis. Psychological trauma from the procedure compounds organic dysfunction.
questions.question: Female genital mutilation (FGM) is clinically associated with long-term sexual dysfunction through which PRIMARY mechanism?

A patient with 46,XY karyotype has testes, but presents with a completely female phenotype including normal breast development, absent pubic and axillary hair, and primary amenorrhoea. This is MOST consistent with:
questions.explanation: CAIS is caused by a mutation in the androgen receptor gene, causing complete inability of target tissues to respond to androgens despite normal or elevated testosterone. The fetus develops in the female phenotype (no androgen effect on cloaca), while AMH from testes causes Müllerian regression (no uterus). Breast development occurs from testosterone being converted to oestrogen peripherally. Absent pubic/axillary hair is characteristic because hair follicles require androgen.

questions.question: A urinary diary in a patient with suspected detrusor instability characteristically shows which pattern?
options: Large volume voids at infrequent intervals
Consistent voiding volumes with predictable timing
Leakage only with physical activity and coughing
Single episode of nocturnal enuresis only
questions.explanation: A urinary diary in detrusor instability characteristically shows: high frequency of voiding (more than 8 per day), multiple small void volumes, frequent episodes of nocturia (more than once per night), and urgency episodes. This pattern contrasts with stress incontinence (where leakage correlates with physical activity and void volumes are normal) and overflow incontinence (where there are frequent small voids with high residual urine).

questions.question: The MOST important advantage of DMPA over combined injectable contraceptives (CICs) in breastfeeding women is:
options: DMPA as a progestogen-only method does not suppress lactation, unlike estrogen-containing CICs
DMPA is cheaper and more widely available in Nigeria
DMPA provides contraceptive protection for 12 months with one injection
DMPA has no effect on bone mineral density during breastfeeding
DMPA eliminates the need for STI screening before administration
questions.explanation: DMPA contains no estrogen; it is a progestogen-only injectable. Estrogen (as found in combined injectables) inhibits prolactin action and reduces milk production, making estrogen-containing methods unsuitable for breastfeeding women. Progestogen-only methods do not adversely affect lactation quantity or infant growth. WHO recommends DMPA be delayed until 6 weeks postpartum as a precaution against any theoretical effect on the breastfed newborn's immature liver.

Bacterial vaginosis in pregnancy, even when asymptomatic, is associated with increased risk of preterm labour, preterm premature rupture of membranes, and late miscarriage, justifying treatment with agents such as oral metronidazole despite the absence of symptoms. It is not linked to congenital anomalies, cervical cancer, or postpartum haemorrhage risk. This obstetric-specific risk differentiates management in pregnancy from the non-pregnant state.
questions.question: A pregnant woman at 32 weeks has confirmed bacterial vaginosis on high vaginal swab but is asymptomatic. Why is treatment MOST strongly recommended despite absence of symptoms in this context?
options: Reduces risk of preterm labour and rupture
Reduces risk of fetal congenital anomaly

questions.question: Radiotherapy in DUB is reserved SPECIFICALLY for which subset of patients?
questions.explanation: Radiotherapy has a small but defined place in DUB management — it is reserved for patients who are not fit for surgery (severe co-morbidities making surgical risk prohibitive). Methods include external irradiation of the ovaries. It results in amenorrhoea in 95% of cases but carries serious complications including gynaeatresia, pyometra, haematometra, and metaplastic transformation of genital cells. It is therefore a last resort for patients in whom surgical options carry unacceptable risk.
options: All perimenopausal women with heavy periods
Women who have failed medical therapy only
Patients unfit for surgery needing definitive treatment

questions.question: Fine needle aspiration biopsy (FNAB) is listed among cytological techniques used in gynaecology. For which type of lesion is FNAB specifically most useful as a diagnostic sampling method?
questions.explanation: Fine needle aspiration biopsy is specifically useful for sampling palpable solid masses, such as a breast lump or enlarged lymph node, obtaining cells for cytological diagnosis with a minimally invasive technique. It differs from the exfoliative technique used for cervical smears, which relies on naturally shed surface cells rather than direct needle sampling. FNAB findings often need histological confirmation if malignancy is suspected.
options: A palpable lump or enlarged lymph node
Discard the rest of the pack and wait for menstruation before starting a new pack
Take all 3 missed pills together immediately and continue normally
Stop the pack, allow a natural cycle, and restart at the next period

Take the most recently missed pill immediately, discard earlier missed pills, continue the pack, use barrier contraception for 7 days, consider emergency contraception if unprotected intercourse occurred
No action needed as efficacy is maintained if fewer than 5 pills are missed in one pack
questions.question: A 25-year-old woman misses 3 consecutive combined oral contraceptive pills in week 2 of her pack. According to standard missed pill guidance, she should:
questions.explanation: Standard guidance for more than 2 consecutive missed COC pills: take the most recently missed pill as soon as remembered (discard earlier missed pills), continue taking the remaining pills daily, use additional barrier contraception for 7 days, and consider emergency contraception if unprotected intercourse occurred during or up to 7 days before missing the pills. If the missed pills fall in the final week (week 3), skip the pill-free interval and start the next pack immediately.

options: Falling hCG and other pregnancy hormone levels following fetal demise
questions.question: A woman describes the early disappearance of nausea, breast tenderness, and fatigue before being told her pregnancy has failed. What is the physiological explanation for the resolution of these symptoms preceding diagnosis of pregnancy loss?
questions.explanation: Early pregnancy symptoms such as nausea and breast tenderness are driven by rising hCG and other placental hormones; when the fetus dies, hormone production declines, causing these symptoms to resolve even before clinical or ultrasound confirmation of pregnancy loss. This symptom resolution can be an early clinical clue prompting further investigation. It underlies why some missed abortions are first suspected based on symptom regression rather than bleeding.

An unsatisfactory smear provides no diagnostic information and should be repeated, typically after an interval of about three months to allow cervical epithelium to recover from any inflammation affecting sampling adequacy. Proceeding directly to colposcopy or biopsy is not indicated without cytological abnormality driving that decision. Waiting the standard three-year screening interval would inappropriately delay detection of any underlying abnormality.
options: Repeat the smear in three months
Reassure and repeat in three years
questions.question: A 32-year-old has an unsatisfactory Pap smear result due to inadequate cellular sampling. What is the MOST appropriate next step in her management?

questions.explanation: Residual and recurrence rates are at least 5% for all treatment techniques (cryotherapy, electrocautery, cold coagulation, laser) except hysterectomy. Hysterectomy has recurrence of intraepithelial or invasive neoplasia of less than 1%, making it the most definitive treatment. The 5% threshold applies even to laser therapy, which offers rapid healing of 10-12 days and no requirement for anaesthesia.
questions.question: Residual and recurrence rates for all CIN treatment techniques except hysterectomy are at least:

questions.explanation: Vomiting or severe diarrhoea occurring shortly after taking a combined oral contraceptive pill can impair absorption of the hormone, so the same guidance used for missed pills should be followed, including additional contraceptive precautions, until reliable pill absorption resumes.
questions.question: A woman with severe vomiting and diarrhoea two hours after taking her combined oral contraceptive pill should be advised that:
options: She should immediately switch to emergency contraception instead
She should stop the pill permanently after any illness
Diarrhoea has no effect on oral contraceptive absorption
The pill is definitely still fully effective regardless of vomiting
Absorption may be impaired, so the missed pill rules should be followed
Providing pharmacological stimulation of the pelvic floor
Applying electrical current to stimulate involuntary contraction
Visualising subconscious pelvic floor activity to patient
questions.explanation: Biofeedback is a behavioural therapy that uses visual or auditory signals to make subconscious pelvic floor muscle activity perceptible to the patient. By seeing or hearing muscle activity in real time (via EMG or pressure sensors), patients learn to improve voluntary pelvic floor muscle contraction and relaxation. It is listed in the SUI treatment continuum between Kegel exercises and electrical stimulation as a progressive step in conservative management.
questions.question: Biofeedback in the treatment of pelvic floor dysfunction works by:

questions.explanation: A clinically inadequate pelvis identified in an adolescent pregnancy warrants planning for caesarean delivery to avoid the serious risks of obstructed labour, including uterine rupture and obstetric fistula. Early identification allows appropriate antenatal counselling and delivery planning at a facility equipped for surgical delivery. This proactive approach reduces adolescent maternal morbidity and mortality.
options: Planned delivery by caesarean section given anticipated cephalopelvic disproportion
Home delivery with a traditional birth attendant
Induction of labour at 34 weeks regardless of fetal maturity
Routine expectant management for spontaneous vaginal delivery
questions.question: A 16-year-old girl presents at 18 weeks gestation with a clinically inadequate pelvis on examination. Her obstetrician plans her delivery accordingly. What is the most appropriate management plan based on this finding?

options: SRY gene mutation causing gonadal agenesis
Leydig cell hypoplasia with absent testosterone
questions.explanation: Persistent Müllerian duct syndrome (Müllerian inhibitory factor deficiency) is an XY condition where the testes are functional and testosterone production is normal, but AMH (MIF) is absent or its receptor is defective. Without AMH signalling, the Müllerian ducts persist alongside normal male Wolffian-derived structures. Affected individuals are phenotypically male with cryptorchid testes and may present when uterus and tubes are found incidentally during hernia repair.
questions.question: The condition in which an XY male has persistent Müllerian structures co-existing with normal male internal structures is caused by:

questions.explanation: The progestogen-only pill is a suitable initial postnatal option for breastfeeding women who are uncertain about longer-term commitment, since it can be started early after delivery, does not affect lactation, and allows the woman time to decide on a longer-acting method later if desired.
questions.question: Which progestogen-only preparation is MOST appropriate for immediate postnatal use in a breastfeeding woman who is uncertain about long-term commitment to a method?
The FEMALE condom differs from the male condom most significantly in that it:
questions.explanation: The female condom (polyurethane or nitrile sheath) can be inserted up to 8 hours before intercourse, unlike the male condom which must be applied at erection. Its placement is entirely controlled by the woman, regardless of partner cooperation. It provides comparable STI protection to the male condom, requires no prescription, and is suitable for latex-allergic individuals since it is latex-free.
options: Is made only of natural sheep membrane
Provides inferior STI protection compared to the male condom
Requires prescription from a healthcare provider
Can be inserted well before intercourse and is controlled by the woman
Cannot be used by women with latex allergy

questions.question: In the investigation of intersex conditions, which investigation provides information about both chromosomal sex AND the internal organs simultaneously?
questions.explanation: Karyotype determines the genetic sex (XX, XY, XO, etc.), while pelvic ultrasound identifies internal organs (presence/absence of uterus, ovaries, or testes). Together, they provide complementary information about genetic sex and internal genitalia simultaneously, which is essential in intersex evaluation. MRI is more detailed but not as immediately accessible. Hormone levels are also needed but do not provide information about internal anatomy.

PSTT is derived from intermediate trophoblast at the placental site, produces low levels of hCG but higher levels of human placental lactogen (hPL), and is relatively resistant to chemotherapy. Hysterectomy is the treatment of choice. It is a rare form of GTD representing approximately 1% of all cases.
questions.question: Placental site trophoblastic tumour (PSTT) is BEST characterised by:
options: High hCG production and sensitivity to chemotherapy
Rapid haematogenous spread to the brain

questions.explanation: Current guidelines recommend that the IUCD may be left in place in PID if the patient is responding well to antibiotic therapy, as routine removal does not improve short-term outcomes and increases pregnancy risk in women relying on it for contraception. However, if there is no clinical improvement within 24–72 hours of antibiotics, removal of the IUCD is recommended. The decision must balance infection control against unintended pregnancy risk.
questions.question: A 25-year-old with lower abdominal pain, fever, and cervical excitation is diagnosed with PID. She has an IUCD in situ. What is the appropriate management of the IUCD?
options: Leave the IUCD in place as removal worsens PID
Remove the IUCD immediately before starting antibiotics
The IUCD must remain in place for all PID cases
Remove IUCD after 24–48 hours if no clinical improvement
Replace with a hormone-releasing IUCD immediately
History of allergic reaction to latex or spermicide
Current use of combined oral contraceptive pills
History of one prior vaginal delivery
questions.explanation: A documented allergy or sensitivity to rubber (latex) or spermicide is an absolute contraindication to diaphragm use because the combination of a latex device and spermicide directly contacts genital mucosa. Exposure could precipitate anaphylaxis, severe contact dermatitis, or toxic epidermal reactions. In such cases, alternative non-latex barrier methods (female condom, cervical cap) or entirely different contraceptive methods should be offered.
questions.question: Which of the following is an ABSOLUTE contraindication (WHO MEC Category 4) to the use of a diaphragm?

questions.explanation: Molar pregnancy patients are at highest risk for developing choriocarcinoma when serum HCG exceeds 100,000 mIU/ml (or urinary HCG exceeds 100,000 IU/24h). Additionally, excessive uterine enlargement and theca-lutein cysts greater than 6 cm are high-risk features of marked trophoblastic proliferation.
questions.question: The beta-HCG level in a molar pregnancy that is MOST associated with increased risk of malignant sequelae is:

questions.explanation: In cervical elongation, the fundus of the uterus stays at a relatively normal intrapelvic level while only the cervix descends and protrudes, whereas in true procidentia the entire uterus including the fundus has descended. Bimanual assessment of fundal position is key to this distinction. This differentiation guides whether a Manchester operation or vaginal hysterectomy is more appropriate.
questions.question: A woman with a large third-degree prolapse and a hypertrophied, elongated cervix is being worked up for possible Manchester repair. On bimanual examination, how would the surgeon differentiate cervical elongation from complete uterine descent?
options: Fundus stays normal in position while cervix descends
The adnexa cannot be palpated at all
The cervix retracts fully on traction
The fundus is also palpable at the introitus

questions.explanation: Yolk sac tumours, also known as endodermal sinus tumours, characteristically secrete alpha-fetoprotein, which serves as a sensitive marker for diagnosis and monitoring of treatment response in this aggressive but chemosensitive germ cell malignancy of young women.
questions.question: Yolk sac tumour of the ovary is characteristically associated with elevation of which serum marker?

options: Young, fit adults with no comorbidities
Women with mild stress incontinence only
Elderly patients at risk of cognitive impairment and urinary retention
questions.explanation: Anticholinergic drugs used for detrusor instability can cause confusion, cognitive impairment, and urinary retention, particularly in elderly patients, who are more susceptible to these central and peripheral side effects. Careful risk-benefit assessment and consideration of alternative agents or non-drug therapy is warranted in this group. Regular review for side effects is important throughout treatment.
questions.question: A woman on long-term anticholinergic therapy for detrusor instability is reviewed. Which patient group would require the most caution before starting this class of medication?

questions.explanation: Colpomicroscopy uses in-vivo staining, typically with toluidine blue and haematoxylin-based stains, combined with much higher magnification than standard colposcopy, allowing near-histological assessment of nuclear detail directly on the cervix. This technique is less widely used than standard colposcopy with biopsy but can provide immediate cellular-level information. It requires specialised equipment and expertise.
options: Toluidine blue and haematoxylin-based stains applied in vivo
questions.question: Colpomicroscopy is described as achieving higher magnification than standard colposcopy. Which combination of special stains is applied to the cervix to enhance visualisation during this technique?
The primary mechanism by which the copper intrauterine device prevents pregnancy is:
questions.explanation: The copper IUD works primarily by inducing a local sterile inflammatory reaction within the uterine cavity that is toxic to sperm and ova, impairing fertilisation, rather than through any systemic hormonal mechanism, distinguishing it from the levonorgestrel intrauterine system.
options: Thickening of cervical mucus preventing sperm entry
A local inflammatory reaction toxic to sperm and ova
Thinning of the endometrium through progestogen action
Mechanical occlusion of the fallopian tubes
Suppression of ovulation through systemic hormone release

questions.question: A 38-year-old woman with endometriosis has an endometrioma of 6cm on her right ovary. Her anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH) is low at 0.8 ng/mL. Her surgeon is discussing surgery. What is the KEY surgical concern when operating on this endometrioma?
options: Ovarian reserve loss removing cortex with cyst wall
Damage to the right ureter during ovarian mobilization
Risk of triggering premature ovulation during anaesthesia
Endometrioma content causing chemical peritonitis if spillage occurs
questions.explanation: The critical surgical concern in operating on an endometrioma with already diminished ovarian reserve (low AMH) is inadvertent removal of normal ovarian primordial follicles that are adherent to or incorporated within the endometrioma cyst wall during cyst excision. This can further and irreversibly reduce ovarian reserve. Careful surgical technique — including hydrodissection to develop a cleavage plane and minimizing normal ovarian tissue excision — is essential. Ovarian reserve should be discussed extensively pre-operatively.

Effective contraceptive counselling is client-centered, assessing individual health conditions, reproductive intentions, relationship dynamics, and personal preferences. The goal is informed autonomous choice, not prescribing any single 'best' method universally. Method effectiveness must be balanced with acceptability, because a perfect method unused provides no protection.
options: Directing patients to the most modern available method
Informing patients of the risks of all methods without recommendation
Recommending the method with the lowest Pearl Index regardless of patient factors
Helping clients choose a method that suits their health, lifestyle, reproductive goals
Obtaining formal written consent before any discussion
questions.question: Counselling for contraception should ideally be MOST focused on:
During a difficult forceps delivery, the operator palpates the ischial spines to assess station. Which nerve travelling close to this bony landmark is at risk during a pudendal block?
questions.explanation: The pudendal nerve passes just posterior to the ischial spine before entering the pudendal (Alcock's) canal, making this landmark the target for pudendal nerve block. Injury or inadequate block here explains failure of perineal anaesthesia. The nerve supplies the external anal sphincter and perineal skin.

questions.question: The composition of a standard low-dose combined oral contraceptive commonly prescribed in Nigeria typically includes ethinylestradiol combined with which progestogen?
questions.explanation: Many widely used low-dose combined oral contraceptives combine a small dose of ethinylestradiol with the second generation progestogen levonorgestrel, a combination favoured for its established safety profile and lower relative thrombotic risk compared with newer progestogens.

Menarche in the United States has been reported at a mean age of 12.8 years, with the normal range extending from 9.1 to 17.7 years. A mean age of 11–14 years is broadly cited for various populations. Menarche before age 9 or absence by age 17 in the US constitutes precocious or delayed puberty respectively. Environmental, nutritional, and genetic factors influence the age of menarche.
questions.question: Menarche in the USA has been reported to occur at a mean age of:

A 29-year-old with stage IV endometriosis is undergoing IVF. Her gynaecologist discusses the impact of endometriomas on oocyte quality. How does an endometrioma (ovarian chocolate cyst) affect adjacent ovarian follicles?
options: It stimulates adjacent follicle maturation through local oestrogen release
It destroys ovarian reserve by direct toxic effect and surgical dissection
It has no effect on adjacent follicles as cysts are encapsulated
It increases FSH production to compensate for cyst formation
It converts androgen to oestrogen more efficiently than normal ovary
questions.explanation: Endometriomas reduce ovarian reserve through direct toxic effects of the cyst contents (reactive oxygen species from degraded haemoglobin) on adjacent primordial follicles, and through surgical removal of normal ovarian cortex adherent to the cyst wall. Repeated endometrioma cyst drainage and surgery further diminishes ovarian reserve. This is why careful surgical technique minimizing removal of normal ovarian tissue is essential in fertility-sparing endometriosis surgery.

At the onset of puberty, GnRH pulsatility initially increases during sleep, producing high amplitude nocturnal pulsatile LH (and FSH) releases detectable in blood samples taken during sleep. These nocturnal gonadotrophin surges are the first hormonal evidence of pubertal hypothalamic activation, preceding visible physical signs. Daytime sampling may miss this early pubertal hormonal signature.
options: Daytime LH and FSH levels in a single morning sample
Nocturnal oestradiol surges from the ovary
High amplitude nocturnal pulsatile LH releases during sleep
questions.question: At puberty, pulsatile GnRH release from the hypothalamus initially occurs predominantly at night. This is MOST reliably detected by measuring which parameter?
In ovarian development, the maximum follicle count peaks in utero and declines irreversibly. The approximate oocyte count at birth after reduction from the fetal peak is:
questions.explanation: After peaking at approximately 7 million oocytes at around 5 months in utero, the number reduces to approximately 2 million (with about 50% being atretic) by the time of birth. This reduction continues until puberty (approximately 300,000 remain at menarche) and throughout reproductive life, with none remaining at menopause. This irreversible decline in ovarian reserve is the biological basis of the female reproductive lifespan.

options: Parasympathetic from sacral roots S2, S3, S4
Somatic nervous system via pudendal nerve
Both sympathetic from thoracolumbar and parasympathetic from cranial nerves
questions.question: The smooth detrusor muscle is richly innervated by which component of the autonomic nervous system?
questions.explanation: The smooth detrusor muscle of the bladder is richly innervated by the parasympathetic nervous system outflow from sacral roots S2, S3, and S4. At the onset of micturition, the pelvic floor striated muscle voluntarily relaxes, reducing intraurethral pressure. Background inhibition of the sacral reflex arc is suppressed, and efferent impulses cause a rise in intravesical pressure exceeding intraurethral pressure.

Infertility is generally defined as failure to conceive after 12 months or more of regular unprotected intercourse, at which point formal investigation of both partners is warranted. Earlier investigation may be justified in women over 35 or with known risk factors. This standard definition guides the timing of referral for fertility workup.
questions.question: A couple presents after 14 months of unprotected intercourse without achieving pregnancy. Which duration of unprotected intercourse is generally used to define infertility warranting formal investigation?
options: 6 months without conception in all couples

questions.explanation: Cervical leiomyomas (fibroids) arise from smooth muscle of the cervix and must be distinguished from endocervical polyps (which are pedunculated adenomatous growths). Cervical fibroids can cause pressure symptoms and are associated with surgical complications involving the ureter and bladder, requiring careful surgical technique. They are also associated with complications in pregnancy and labour.
options: Is most common in women aged 20-30
questions.question: A leiomyoma in a cervical fibroid differs from an endocervical polyp primarily in that it:

questions.explanation: Sarcoma botryoides (embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma) is characteristically seen in infants and young children. It presents with blood-stained watery discharge and grape-like masses of soft growth arising from the cervix. Histologically, it contains primitive striped muscle cells (rhabdomyoblasts) among myxomatous cells.
questions.question: Sarcoma botryoides (embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma) characteristically presents in:
options: Women in their 40s with rapid fibroid growth

questions.question: The pubovesical ligament is important during micturition because it inserts into which anatomical junction?
questions.explanation: The pubovesical ligament is the most anterior group of levator ani fibres. It arises from the back of the pubic bone and inserts into the junction between the bladder and the urethra. Because of this insertion, it plays an important role during micturition by modulating bladder neck dynamics.

options: Firm, solid consistency arising from the cervical stroma
Attachment by a thin vascular pedicle only
questions.question: A cervical mass is found on speculum examination. Which feature would favour a diagnosis of leiomyoma of the cervix rather than an endocervical polyp?
questions.explanation: A cervical leiomyoma is a firm, solid smooth-muscle tumour arising within the cervical stroma, unlike an endocervical polyp which is typically soft, friable, and arises from glandular endocervical tissue on a thin pedicle. This distinction guides management, since fibroids require surgical excision while polyps can often be avulsed. Histology confirms the diagnosis when uncertain.

questions.question: Masters and Johnson's human sexual response cycle describes four phases in order as:
questions.explanation: Masters and Johnson (1966) described four phases: Excitement (initial arousal with vasocongestion and myotonia), Plateau (sustained arousal before orgasm), Orgasm (peak reflex muscular contraction), and Resolution (return to baseline). Desire was added by Kaplan as a precursor phase (Triphasic Model). The original Masters and Johnson model has four, not five, phases.

questions.question: In FIGO staging of ovarian cancer, retroperitoneal lymph node metastasis would classify the disease as at least:
questions.explanation: FIGO Stage IIIC ovarian cancer includes macroscopic peritoneal metastases beyond the pelvis with greatest dimension greater than 2 cm and/or regional lymph node metastasis. Retroperitoneal (pelvic or para-aortic) lymph node involvement classifies disease as Stage IIIC.

questions.question: Dual protection in the context of contraception specifically refers to:
questions.explanation: Dual protection describes strategies, most commonly consistent condom use alongside another contraceptive method, that simultaneously reduce the risk of unintended pregnancy and the transmission of sexually transmitted infections, addressing both reproductive health goals together.
options: Combining two barrier methods for pregnancy prevention alone
Doubling the dose of a single contraceptive method
Simultaneous protection against pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections
Using two hormonal methods together for extra efficacy
Using contraception with a backup method only during high fertility days

questions.explanation: Hyperinsulinaemia in PCOD acts synergistically with LH to stimulate ovarian theca cell androgen (testosterone, androstenedione) overproduction and simultaneously reduces hepatic sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) synthesis, increasing free testosterone. Elevated free androgens cause hirsutism, acne, and further suppress folliculogenesis. Insulin-sensitizing agents (metformin) address this mechanism and can restore ovulation in some PCOD patients.
questions.question: PCOD is associated with insulin resistance and compensatory hyperinsulinaemia. How does hyperinsulinaemia contribute to the hormonal derangement in PCOD?
options: Directly suppressing LH secretion from the pituitary
Stimulating hepatic SHBG production to bind excess androgens
Ovarian theca androgen stimulation and hepatic SHBG reduction
Increasing peripheral oestrogen conversion from androgens

questions.question: A 35-year-old presents with her first episode of spontaneous abortion. Her physician explains the baseline population risk. What is the risk of a FIRST spontaneous abortion in the general pregnant population?
questions.explanation: The incidence of spontaneous abortion is approximately 15% of clinically evident pregnancies, though it rises to 60% when chemical pregnancies (biochemical losses) are included. This 15% figure for clinically recognized pregnancies is the standard teaching statistic. Women should be counselled that a single miscarriage does not necessarily indicate a recurring problem.

Radiation endarteritis causes progressive obliteration of small blood vessels in irradiated tissues. When gynaecological surgery is performed in a previously irradiated field, the ischaemic tissues are prone to avascular necrosis, leading to weakening of the bladder wall or ureteric wall and subsequent development of ureteric or vesico-vaginal fistula. This is why VVF is particularly likely after surgery in previously irradiated tissues.
questions.question: Which of the following urinary tract injury complications is specifically mentioned as a risk when performing gynaecological surgery in the presence of previous radiation endarteritis?
A woman with severe incontinence has failed both conservative pelvic floor therapy and pharmacological treatment. Which broad category of management is next appropriately considered?
options: Repeating the same failed pharmacological regimen at a lower dose
Surgical intervention guided by urodynamic findings
questions.explanation: When conservative and pharmacological measures fail to adequately control incontinence, surgical options tailored to the underlying urodynamic diagnosis, such as a mid-urethral sling for stress incontinence or neuromodulation for refractory overactive bladder, become appropriate next steps. Accurate diagnosis via urodynamics before surgery ensures the correct procedure is chosen. This stepwise escalation avoids premature or inappropriate surgical intervention.

questions.question: A woman with prolapse is noted to have difficulty voiding, needing to push the bulge back manually before urine flows. Which mechanism accounts for this obstructive symptom?
questions.explanation: A large cystocele or uterine descent can kink or compress the urethra, creating a functional outflow obstruction. Manually reducing the prolapse straightens the urethral axis and permits voiding. This mechanical obstruction is a recognised indication for surgical correction of prolapse.
options: Anterior wall prolapse kinking the urethra

questions.question: A woman presents 4 weeks after an apparently complete abortion. She is still amenorrhoeic and hCG is still elevated. Uterine size is unchanged. This picture is MOST consistent with which complication requiring urgent evaluation?
questions.explanation: Persistently elevated hCG following apparently complete abortion should raise immediate suspicion for gestational trophoblastic disease (GTD), including hydatidiform mole or choriocarcinoma. GTD requires urgent investigation with serial hCG monitoring, pelvic ultrasound, and chest X-ray. Early diagnosis enables curative chemotherapy and prevents the potentially fatal complications of metastatic GTD.
options: Resumption of pregnancy from retained products

questions.explanation: Sensate focus therapy is structured in graduated stages, typically beginning with non-genital touching exercises focused on sensation rather than performance, before progressively introducing genital touching and eventually intercourse, allowing anxiety to reduce gradually as intimacy is rebuilt.
questions.question: Sensate focus therapy is typically structured in which sequential order?
options: A single session covering all stages at once
Random order determined solely by the couple without structure
Progressing from non-genital touching to genital touching and eventually intercourse
Beginning with genital touching before non-genital touching

questions.explanation: Secondary infertility describes difficulty conceiving in a woman who has previously achieved at least one pregnancy, in contrast to primary infertility, which describes an inability to conceive despite regular unprotected intercourse in a woman who has never previously conceived, a distinction relevant when infection-related tubal damage is suspected.
questions.question: A woman asks about the difference between primary and secondary infertility related to sexually transmitted infection. The MOST accurate distinction is that secondary infertility refers to:
options: Inability to ever conceive despite regular unprotected intercourse
Infertility resulting exclusively from male factors
Infertility occurring only in women over forty
Inability to conceive after a previous successful pregnancy

questions.explanation: Menstruation ceases because rising oestrogen levels from newly developing follicles in the next cycle cause vasoconstriction of the spiral arterioles (stopping blood loss), stimulate rapid tissue repair of the shed endometrium, and promote clot formation at the capillary level. This oestrogen-driven healing mechanism is so rapid that the endometrium begins to re-epithelialize even while shedding of the upper layers continues.
options: Endometrial proliferation restarting from the basalis
Vasoconstriction, tissue repair, and clot formation
AMH release from the regenerating endometrium
questions.question: Menstruation ceases at the end of the period because of oestrogen-mediated:

questions.explanation: SSRI-induced sexual dysfunction should be addressed collaboratively with the prescribing psychiatrist since discontinuing antidepressants without psychiatric guidance risks relapse of depression. Management options include dose reduction, timed 'drug holiday', switching to antidepressants with lower sexual side effect profiles (bupropion, mirtazapine, agomelatine), or adding sildenafil/tadalafil adjunctively. Patient education about this common side effect improves retention on treatment.
options: Immediately discontinuing sertraline and substituting a tricyclic antidepressant
Reassuring her that SSRI-induced anorgasmia always resolves spontaneously within 3 months
Prescribing testosterone gel regardless of her baseline androgen levels
Discussing the side effect with her psychiatrist with options including dose reduction, adding PDE5 inhibitor, or switching to bupropion
Referring for intensive psychotherapy as anorgasmia is primarily psychogenic on SSRIs
questions.question: Anorgasmia developing in a woman after starting sertraline (SSRI) is MOST appropriately managed initially by:

questions.explanation: Post-menopausal bleeding is endometrial carcinoma until proven otherwise. An endometrial thickness >4mm on ultrasound in post-menopausal women (or any PMB regardless of thickness) requires endometrial sampling/biopsy to histologically exclude malignancy. Pipelle endometrial biopsy (sensitivity ~90% for endometrial carcinoma) is first-line; hysteroscopy with directed biopsy is performed if pipelle is inconclusive or fails. Early investigation is life-saving as endometrial carcinoma detected early has >90% 5-year survival.
options: Start HRT to restore endometrial cycling
questions.question: A woman presents with post-menopausal bleeding 5 years after her last period. Endometrial thickness on ultrasound is 8mm. What is the MOST important next step?

A patient at 10 weeks reports her nausea and vomiting have been more severe than in a previous uncomplicated pregnancy. On ultrasound, a 'snowstorm' pattern is seen with no identifiable fetus. Which diagnosis does this combination suggest?
options: Missed abortion of a normal singleton
questions.explanation: Exaggerated pregnancy symptoms such as severe nausea and vomiting, combined with a 'snowstorm' ultrasound appearance and absence of a fetus, are classic features of a hydatidiform mole, resulting from abnormal trophoblastic proliferation and very high hCG levels. This must be distinguished from other causes of early pregnancy failure because molar pregnancy requires specific evacuation and hCG surveillance for malignant transformation. Early recognition prevents complications such as choriocarcinoma.

A transverse colostomy diverts the faecal stream from a point proximal to the fistula, providing more complete faecal diversion and protection of the distal repair site during healing compared with some other diversion options. This reduces contamination risk at the repair site during the critical healing period. It is later reversed once healing is confirmed, typically with a dye test.
options: It avoids the need for bowel preparation
Diverts the faecal stream proximally, protecting the repair
It never requires a stoma appliance
It is easier to reverse without any surgery
questions.question: Transverse colostomy is generally preferred over an iliac (sigmoid) colostomy for preliminary faecal diversion before repair of a high recto-vaginal fistula. What is the main advantage of the transverse colostomy in this context?

questions.explanation: Transdermal delivery of ethinylestradiol and norelgestromin bypasses the gastrointestinal tract and hepatic first-pass metabolism, delivering hormones directly into the systemic circulation. This achieves steadier plasma levels without the peak-trough fluctuations of daily oral dosing. However, total weekly estrogen exposure from the patch is approximately 60% higher than from a 35mcg EE pill, which may contribute to slightly higher VTE risk compared to some oral COC formulations.
options: The patch releases progesterone only, eliminating estrogen-related VTE risk entirely
Transdermal delivery bypasses hepatic first-pass metabolism, achieving steadier plasma hormone levels with lower peak concentrations
The patch delivers lower total estrogen exposure than equivalent oral COC formulations
Transdermal absorption completely prevents nausea and headache side effects
The patch requires daily replacement unlike weekly OCP pill packs
questions.question: The contraceptive patch (transdermal) differs from combined oral contraceptives in its pharmacokinetics PRIMARILY because:
Stenosis of the vulval orifice and lower vagina after reconstruction of a complete perineal tear is managed by which of the following procedures?
questions.explanation: Sequelae of extensive reconstruction of a complete perineal tear include stenosis of the vulval orifice and lower vagina. Management options for this stenosis include: division of stricture with simple suture, dissection and reconstruction (with simple suture or split skin graft on a mould), and Frank's procedure. Another sequela is dehiscence of the midline scar, managed by adequate posterior lateral episiotomy and hospital confinement.

questions.question: A 38-year-old woman presents with increasingly irregular heavy periods over the last 8 months after years of regular cycles. The MOST important investigation to perform FIRST is:
questions.explanation: A woman aged 35 years or older with abnormal uterine bleeding must have endometrial sampling performed as the priority investigation to exclude endometrial hyperplasia or carcinoma. In the perimenopausal period, organic disease (including malignancy) is common and must be excluded before attributing bleeding to anovulatory changes. The principle is 'biopsy first' in this age group. Ultrasound and FBC are also important but endometrial sampling to exclude malignancy takes priority.

questions.question: A 35-year-old presents with her second ectopic pregnancy managed medically. She is concerned about her future fertility. What is the OVERALL intrauterine pregnancy rate following conservative management of ectopic pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Approximately 60–70% of women achieve a subsequent intrauterine pregnancy following conservative management of ectopic pregnancy, depending on the management method and underlying tubal status. However, the recurrence rate of ectopic pregnancy is 15% after one and 25% after two ectopics, emphasizing the importance of early ultrasound in all future pregnancies. Women with risk factors like bilateral tubal disease have significantly lower intrauterine pregnancy rates.

options: Assessment of musculoskeletal and psychosocial factors
Repeat pelvic ultrasound in one week only
questions.explanation: When gynaecological structural causes have been thoroughly excluded, chronic pelvic pain assessment should broaden to consider musculoskeletal, gastrointestinal, urological, and psychosocial contributors, since chronic pain conditions are frequently multifactorial and central sensitisation may play a role. Repeating the same negative investigations is unlikely to yield new information. A multidisciplinary approach often provides more effective symptom management than further isolated gynaecological intervention.
questions.question: A 34-year-old with chronic pelvic pain for six months has had a normal pelvic examination, ultrasound, and laparoscopy. Which broader assessment is MOST important to include in her ongoing evaluation?

options: Both follicular and luteal phases equally
The menstrual phase of shedding only
The late follicular phase just before the LH surge
questions.explanation: In ovulatory polymenorrhoea (short cycles), the preovulatory (follicular) phase is shortened, while the postovulatory (luteal) phase remains relatively constant at 14 days. This is because the luteal phase duration is fixed by the lifespan of the corpus luteum, independent of the time taken for follicular maturation. Ovulatory failure (anovulation) is another cause of polymenorrhoea where cycles are shortened irregularly.
questions.question: In polymenorrhoea (shortened cycle length), when ovulatory cycles are preserved, which phase is most commonly shortened?

questions.explanation: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome results from spread of infection from the pelvis to the liver capsule, classically associated with ascending chlamydial or gonococcal pelvic inflammatory disease, producing violin-string adhesions between the liver capsule and abdominal wall visible at laparoscopy.
questions.question: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome, characterised by right upper quadrant pain from perihepatic inflammation, is MOST classically associated with which sexually transmitted infections?
options: Herpes simplex virus and human papillomavirus

questions.question: A uterine fibroid of FIGO type 0 is entirely contained within the endometrial cavity on a stalk. Which treatment approach is most appropriate for this specific fibroid type given its location?
questions.explanation: A FIGO type 0 fibroid, being entirely intracavitary on a stalk, is well-suited to minimally invasive hysteroscopic resection, avoiding the need for more invasive abdominal surgery, and this approach also preserves the uterus and fertility potential. This differs from intramural or subserosal fibroids, which typically require a different surgical approach such as abdominal or laparoscopic myomectomy. Hysteroscopic resection also allows direct histological confirmation of the excised tissue.
options: GnRH analogue therapy alone as definitive treatment
Total abdominal hysterectomy as the only option

questions.explanation: Because the neonate showed signs of life at expulsion before dying, it is classified as a neonatal death rather than an abortion or stillbirth by Nigerian definition. The standard definition of abortion specifically excludes cases where signs of life are present at expulsion. In Nigeria, viability is set at 28 weeks (=1,000g), below which a delivery without signs of life would be classified as abortion.
questions.question: In Nigeria, the gestational age threshold for defining viability and thus abortion is 28 weeks, corresponding to a fetal weight of =1,000g. A patient at 26 weeks delivers a live neonate who subsequently dies. How should this event be classified according to Nigerian legal standards?

options: Postmenopausal women with no menstrual flow
Women who have had a hysterectomy
Reproductive-age women with retained menstrual flow
questions.question: A woman with dysmenorrhoea is found to have narrowing of the cervical canal following previous cervical surgery. In which group of patients is cervical stenosis most likely to cause significant dysmenorrhoea?
questions.explanation: Cervical stenosis causes dysmenorrhoea primarily in menstruating women of reproductive age, where outflow obstruction leads to retained blood and increased intrauterine pressure with painful contractions. Postmenopausal or hysterectomised women, lacking menstrual flow, are not similarly affected by stenosis-related pain. Treatment involves cervical dilatation to relieve obstruction.

options: No anaesthesia as repair is minor
questions.question: The anaesthesia of choice for immediate primary repair of a 3rd degree perineal tear is:
questions.explanation: Immediate primary repair of a 3rd degree perineal tear requires the patient to be placed in the lithotomy position under general (GA), spinal, or caudal anaesthesia. This is because repair must be performed layer by layer in a properly equipped theatre by an experienced surgeon. Good anaesthesia ensures muscle relaxation for adequate exposure and precise identification and apposition of the torn anal sphincter ends.

options: Good prognosis and high sensitivity to chemotherapy
questions.explanation: Clear cell carcinoma of the ovary is associated with a poor prognosis and relative resistance to standard platinum-based chemotherapy. Together with papillary serous histotype, it confers a worse outcome than other epithelial ovarian cancers and accounts for a disproportionate number of chemotherapy failures.
questions.question: Clear cell (mesonephroid) ovarian carcinoma is associated with:

A 62-year-old woman not on HRT presents with progressive vaginal dryness, dyspareunia, and recurrent urinary symptoms. Which localised treatment specifically targets these urogenital atrophy symptoms with minimal systemic absorption?
questions.explanation: Low-dose vaginal oestrogen, delivered locally as cream, tablet, or ring, effectively treats urogenital atrophy symptoms such as dryness, dyspareunia, and some urinary symptoms with minimal systemic absorption, making it a suitable option even in some women where systemic HRT is contraindicated. This targeted approach addresses the local tissue effects of oestrogen deficiency without the broader systemic exposure of oral or transdermal HRT. It can often be used long-term with appropriate monitoring.

In suspected placenta praevia, digital vaginal examination should be avoided until the placental location is confirmed by ultrasound, since it can dislodge the low-lying placenta and provoke severe, potentially catastrophic haemorrhage. Abdominal palpation and fetal monitoring can be safely performed while awaiting ultrasound confirmation. This principle, often summarised as 'no digital vaginal examination until praevia is excluded,' is a fundamental safety rule in managing antepartum haemorrhage.
questions.question: A woman at 38 weeks with known placenta praevia presents with painless bright red vaginal bleeding. Which examination should specifically be avoided until placental location is confirmed, given the risk of provoking catastrophic haemorrhage?

A woman with a singleton pregnancy at 36 weeks is found to have severe fetal growth restriction with abnormal umbilical artery Doppler showing absent end-diastolic flow. What does this Doppler finding indicate about placental function?
questions.explanation: Absent end-diastolic flow in the umbilical artery on Doppler ultrasound indicates significantly increased placental vascular resistance, reflecting placental insufficiency severe enough to compromise fetal oxygen and nutrient delivery, and is associated with a high risk of stillbirth if not appropriately managed with close monitoring and considered timing of delivery. This is a more severe finding than simply reduced but still present end-diastolic flow. It often prompts intensified surveillance or expedited delivery depending on gestational age and overall clinical picture.
options: Significantly increased placental vascular resistance reflecting placental insufficiency
Fetal cardiac arrhythmia as the primary abnormality
Normal variation requiring no further monitoring
Reduced maternal blood pressure only, unrelated to the placenta

questions.question: The incidence of MRKH syndrome (uterovaginal agenesis) is approximately:
questions.explanation: MRKH syndrome has an estimated incidence of 1 in 4,000 to 1 in 6,000 females. It is the second most common cause of primary amenorrhoea (after Turner's syndrome at 1:2000). The rarity of the condition means it is often diagnosed late — at puberty when primary amenorrhoea brings the patient to clinical attention. Renal tract imaging is indicated due to the 30–40% incidence of associated renal anomalies.

questions.question: The Interstim therapy success rate at 3-5 years is quoted as 50-80%. Compared to TVT/TOT (80%), which statement is most accurate?
options: Interstim is superior to TVT for all types of incontinence
Interstim is indicated only for overflow incontinence
TVT is used for overactive bladder while Interstim is for SUI
Interstim for OAB; TVT/TOT for stress incontinence
Both are equally effective for stress and urge incontinence
questions.explanation: Interstim (sacral neuromodulation) with 50-80% success rate is specifically indicated for overactive bladder (detrusor instability/urgency incontinence). TVT/TOT with 80% success rate is specifically indicated for stress urinary incontinence. These two types of incontinence have fundamentally different pathophysiology and therefore require different treatment approaches. Using the wrong surgical intervention would be ineffective or harmful.

questions.question: Loss of tone in the levator ani results in which of the following specific changes?
options: Elongation of the cervix without uterine descent
Hypertrophy of the bladder detrusor muscle
questions.explanation: With loss of tone in the levator ani, the pelvic floor support diminishes, resulting in a change in the vaginal axis, sagging of the levator plate, and enlargement of the urogenital hiatus. This contrasts with the normal state where there is acute anorectal angle and a horizontal levator plate maintaining pelvic organ positions.

questions.question: Transverse colostomy is preferred over iliac colostomy for preliminary diversion before high RVF repair. The key advantage is:
questions.explanation: Transverse colostomy is preferred because it leaves the abdominal wall below the umbilicus clear for approach to the pelvis (important if abdominal repair is needed or if ureterocolic anastomoses are required for an associated difficult VVF). Iliac colostomy leaves the pelvic colon tethered to the anterior abdominal wall, making transplantation of the ureters difficult if urinary diversion is subsequently needed.

questions.question: Cryptomenorrhoea is best defined as:
questions.explanation: Cryptomenorrhoea (hidden menstruation) is defined as cyclical lower abdominal pain caused by obstruction of menstrual outflow, with blood accumulating behind the obstruction. Causes include an imperforate hymen, vaginal atresia, transverse vaginal septum, or cervical obstruction. Haematocolpos (blood in the vagina) and haematometra (blood in the uterus) develop as complications if untreated.
options: Absence of menstruation for six months or more
Cyclical pain with obstruction of menstrual outflow

questions.explanation: Migraine with aura is classified as WHO MEC Category 4 for combined hormonal contraceptives because of a significantly increased risk of ischaemic stroke when oestrogen-containing methods are combined with this specific type of migraine, making progestogen-only or non-hormonal methods more appropriate.
questions.question: A woman with migraine with aura requesting combined oral contraceptives should be classified under which WHO MEC category due to increased stroke risk?

questions.explanation: Frequent childbearing with short inter-pregnancy intervals repeatedly stresses pelvic floor musculature and connective tissue support without sufficient time for recovery between deliveries, cumulatively increasing the risk of pelvic organ prolapse. This is compounded when postnatal pelvic floor rehabilitation, such as physiotherapy, is not practised. Public health interventions addressing birth spacing and postnatal care can help reduce this risk.
questions.question: A cultural practice involving early, frequent childbearing with inadequate spacing between pregnancies and minimal postnatal pelvic floor rehabilitation is identified as a determinant of prolapse incidence in a community. What is the primary mechanism linking this practice to increased prolapse rates?
options: Reduced overall parity in the community
Repeated obstetric trauma without adequate recovery time
Increased maternal age at first pregnancy

questions.explanation: Aggressive uterine curettage (D&C), particularly when performed for retained products of conception or in the postpartum period when the endometrium is vulnerable, most frequently causes Asherman's syndrome. The trauma and subsequent healing leads to intrauterine adhesion formation. It is also listed as a cause of secondary amenorrhoea after tuberculosis and suppurative endometritis in the teaching materials.
questions.question: Asherman's syndrome (uterine synechia) is listed as a cause of primary amenorrhoea when it occurs in utero. However, it more commonly causes secondary amenorrhoea. Which common gynaecological procedure MOST frequently causes Asherman's syndrome?

questions.explanation: Faradism (intermittent electrical stimulation of pelvic floor muscles) is a conservative physiotherapy option that applies electrical current to the pelvic floor muscles to make them contract. It is particularly useful in patients with poor voluntary contraction ability. It is used alongside pelvic floor exercises in post-natal and minor degree prolapse management.
options: Delivering antibiotics trans-dermally to the pelvic floor
questions.question: Faradism in the management of prolapse works by:

options: Gram stain of cervical discharge showing intracellular diplococci
Culture of cervical swab on Thayer-Martin medium
Direct immunofluorescence of cervical scrape for elementary bodies
Nucleic acid amplification test on endocervical swab or first-void urine
questions.question: The MOST sensitive test for diagnosing active chlamydial infection in a symptomatic woman is:
questions.explanation: Nucleic acid amplification tests (NAAT) — including PCR and strand displacement amplification — are the most sensitive (>95%) and specific (>99%) tests for detecting Chlamydia trachomatis. They can detect very low organism loads and can be performed on endocervical swabs, self-collected vaginal swabs, or first-void urine. Culture is less sensitive (60–80%) and technically demanding. Serology (IgG) indicates past exposure, not active infection.

questions.question: A Rhesus-negative woman delivers a Rhesus-positive baby. Why is anti-D immunoglobulin administered to her within 72 hours of delivery?
questions.explanation: Anti-D immunoglobulin given after delivery of a Rhesus-positive infant to a Rhesus-negative mother works by clearing fetal Rhesus-positive red cells from the maternal circulation before her immune system can form anti-D antibodies, preventing sensitisation that would otherwise risk haemolytic disease of the newborn in a future Rhesus-positive pregnancy. Timely administration within 72 hours of delivery, or after any sensitising event during pregnancy, is essential for effectiveness. This prophylactic principle has substantially reduced the incidence of severe Rhesus isoimmunisation disease.
options: To treat existing fetal anaemia in this pregnancy
To prevent gestational diabetes in future pregnancies
To prevent maternal sensitisation from fetal cells

questions.question: Return of bowel sounds and passage of flatus after major abdominal surgery typically occurs by:
questions.explanation: Return of bowel sounds and passage of flatus after major abdominal surgery typically occurs within 24–72 hours (small bowel motility recovers by 24 hours, stomach by 24–48 hours, colon by 48–72 hours). Prolonged ileus beyond 72 hours warrants investigation for electrolyte imbalance, intra-abdominal collections, or other complications.

questions.question: HIV transmission efficiency per act of unprotected intercourse is HIGHEST during which type of sexual contact?
questions.explanation: Receptive anal intercourse carries the highest per-act risk of HIV transmission among sexual practices, largely because the rectal mucosa is thinner and more easily traumatised than vaginal mucosa, facilitating viral entry, whereas oral sex carries comparatively low transmission risk.

The EMA-CO regimen, comprising etoposide, methotrexate, actinomycin D, cyclophosphamide, and vincristine, is the standard multi-agent chemotherapy protocol for high-risk gestational trophoblastic neoplasia, achieving high cure rates even in metastatic disease.
questions.question: High-risk gestational trophoblastic neoplasia is typically managed with which multi-agent chemotherapy regimen?

questions.explanation: Bladder exstrophy is a congenital condition listed under the congenital aetiology of vaginal prolapse, alongside collagen disorders, racial factors, and anatomical variations. The midline fusion defect in bladder exstrophy disrupts the pelvic floor architecture from birth, predisposing to prolapse. This illustrates that prolapse does not exclusively occur in the context of parity or ageing.
questions.question: Which congenital condition most clearly illustrates a structural aetiology for vaginal prolapse from birth?

A 33-year-old with fibroids and menorrhagia has a haemoglobin of 6.5g/dL from chronic iron deficiency. She has completed her family. Her surgeon plans pre-operative optimization. Which combination of treatments is MOST effective for pre-operative preparation in this scenario?
options: GnRH analogue 3 months plus iron supplementation
Combined OCP plus iron for 6 months
Progesterone alone to stop menstrual loss
questions.explanation: The optimal pre-operative preparation for fibroid-related severe anaemia combines GnRH analogue therapy (3 months) to induce amenorrhoea and shrink fibroids (reducing surgical blood loss), with concurrent IV or oral iron supplementation to restore haemoglobin. GnRH analogues stop menstrual blood loss immediately while iron repletes stores. This combination achieves maximal haemoglobin restoration and fibroid shrinkage, minimizing intraoperative and transfusion requirements.

options: Cervical cancer with persistent high-risk HPV infection
Liver cancer in women without pre-existing hepatic disease
questions.question: Combined oral contraceptive use is associated with a STATISTICALLY SIGNIFICANT increased risk of which cancer?
questions.explanation: COC use is associated with a small but statistically significant increased risk of cervical cancer, but this risk is confined to women with persistent high-risk HPV infection. COC appears to act as a co-factor rather than as an independent carcinogen. The absolute risk increase is small and offset by COC's protective effects on ovarian and endometrial cancer. Regular cervical screening provides effective surveillance.

options: The tape is placed entirely intra-abdominally
Tape passes laterally through the obturator foramen
The tape bypasses the urethra completely
The tape is anchored to the sacrum
The tape is placed subcutaneously in the thigh only
questions.question: A woman with stress incontinence and marked urethral hypermobility is treated with a Trans Obturator Tape (TOT). Compared with a retropubic TVT, what is the key anatomical difference in tape placement for a TOT?
questions.explanation: The transobturator tape (TOT) is passed laterally through the obturator foramen from the groin rather than behind the pubic bone as with the retropubic TVT, reducing the risk of bladder perforation and major vessel injury associated with the retropubic route. Both achieve a similar tension-free hammock effect beneath the urethra. Choice between routes depends on patient anatomy and surgeon preference.

Prolonged menstruation with prolonged days of bleeding at a normal flow rate is characteristically caused by irregular shedding of the endometrium due to prolonged corpus luteum activity (corpus luteum hyperfunction). The endometrium fails to shed completely on schedule because progesterone support continues longer than normal. Diagnosis is by endometrial biopsy on the 4th–5th day of menstruation, which shows mixed secretory and proliferative endometrium. Anovulatory cycles cause prolonged irregular bleeding rather than regularly prolonged menstruation.
questions.question: Prolonged menstruation (prolonged bleeding with normal flow amount) as a variation of the menstrual cycle has which MOST common cause?
Polyamines such as spermine, spermidine, and putrescine are used as tumour markers in which malignancies?
questions.explanation: Polyamines including spermine, spermidine, and putrescine serve as tumour markers in leukaemia, lymphoma, and colorectal carcinoma. They are categorised among the nature of tumour antigens as polyamine markers, distinct from oncofetal antigens, proteins, enzymes, receptors, cell markers, and ectopic hormones in the classification of tumour marker types. Subtopic 6: Vulval Lesions (Benign and Malignant)

Hyperosmolar agents (hypertonic saline 20%, urea 30%, concentrated glucose) are administered by intra-amniotic instillation, causing direct fetal death through osmotic injury and subsequently triggering uterine contractions leading to expulsion. These methods are used for second-trimester induced abortion. They have largely been replaced by prostaglandin analogues and combination mifepristone-misoprostol regimens, which are safer and more effective.
options: Competing with oxytocin receptors in myometrium
Inhibiting progesterone synthesis from the placenta
Stimulating cervical ripening without uterine contractions
questions.question: Hyperosmolar glucose (30% urea and 20% saline) is listed among medical methods for induced abortion. These agents work by which shared mechanism?

questions.explanation: Pipelle biopsy obtains an endometrial tissue sample for histological analysis, allowing detection of hyperplasia or carcinoma, and is typically performed as an outpatient procedure following an ultrasound finding of a thickened or irregular endometrium in postmenopausal bleeding.
questions.question: A pipelle endometrial biopsy in a woman with postmenopausal bleeding is primarily performed to:
options: Obtain histological sampling of the endometrium
Replace the need for ultrasound entirely

questions.explanation: Meigs syndrome consists of ovarian fibroma (or occasionally other benign pelvic tumours), ascites, and a right-sided pleural effusion. The pleural effusion is predominantly right-sided and resolves completely after removal of the tumour.
questions.question: Meigs syndrome, associated with ovarian fibroma, is characterised by the triad of ovarian tumour, ascites, and:

questions.explanation: Combined injectable contraceptives, containing both oestrogen and progestogen, tend to produce more regular, predictable withdrawal bleeding compared with the irregular bleeding or amenorrhoea commonly seen with progestogen-only DMPA, though they require more frequent monthly injections.
options: Complete absence of any hormonal side effects
A more predictable regular bleeding pattern
A longer duration of action between injections
questions.question: A woman using combined injectable contraceptives compared with DMPA should be counselled that the main advantage of the combined formulation is:

questions.explanation: Cervicography is a diagnostic technique that involves taking a photograph of the cervix using a hand-held, fixed-focus 35mm camera after application of acetic acid. The image is projected onto a screen for evaluation.
