questions.explanation: The Manchester (Fothergill) operation involves shortening of the cervix, which can lead to cervical incompetence as a complication with direct obstetric consequences. Cervical incompetence causes painless mid-trimester abortions and premature deliveries. This is why informed consent and careful patient selection (preferring women who have already completed their family, unless fertility preservation is required) are essential. SUBTOPIC 3: UTERINE FIBROIDS AND ENDOMETRIOSIS

Androgen levels (testosterone, DHEA-S, androstenedione) are measured in DUB investigations to help diagnose PCOS — the most common endocrine cause of anovulatory DUB. PCOS is characterised by elevated androgens (hyperandrogenaemia), polycystic ovaries on ultrasound, oligomenorrhoea or amenorrhoea, and often elevated LH:FSH ratio. Identifying PCOS guides management toward insulin sensitisers (metformin), ovulation induction, or OCPs with an anti-androgenic progestin.
questions.question: Androgen levels are measured in DUB evaluation specifically to diagnose:
options: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia causing uterine bleeding
Endometrial carcinoma from androgen receptor activation
Turner's syndrome presenting late in the reproductive years
Polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) in anovulatory DUB

questions.question: A postmenopausal woman presenting with an ovarian mass and CA-125 of 400 u/ml, together with a normal chest X-ray, is MOST appropriately managed by which initial approach?
options: Needle aspiration of the cyst for cytology
Referral for staging laparotomy by a gynaecological oncologist
questions.explanation: A markedly elevated CA-125 in a postmenopausal woman with an adnexal mass strongly suggests malignancy, and the appropriate management is prompt referral for staging laparotomy performed by a gynaecological oncologist, since accurate surgical staging determines prognosis and subsequent treatment.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains the anorectal angle maintained in a normal, continent individual?
options: Puborectalis anterior pull on the anorectal junction
Passive tension of the uterosacral ligaments
Tone of the internal anal sphincter alone
questions.explanation: The puborectalis is a U-shaped, medially located levator ani muscle that runs from the back of the pubic bone and inserts into the anorectal junction. Its tonic contraction pulls the anorectal junction anteriorly, creating the anorectal angle that is central to gross faecal continence by relieving pressure from the sphincter complex.

Colposcopy uses two sequential solutions to highlight abnormal cervical epithelium: 3–5% acetic acid (which causes acetowhitening of dysplastic cells with high nuclear density) and Lugol's iodine (which stains glycogen-containing normal squamous cells dark brown/black while dysplastic, glycogen-poor cells remain unstained — iodine-negative areas). These two solutions together help identify and direct biopsy to most suspicious areas.
questions.question: A colposcope is used to visualize the cervix in gynaecological practice. The two solutions used to facilitate colposcopic visualization of abnormal cervical cells are:

options: Increases FSH by removing ovarian inhibin; replaced by exogenous FSH
Removes luteinized cysts, restoring progesterone balance; replaced by progestin therapy
Destroys all follicles preventing anovulation; replaced by GnRH analogues
Stimulates oestrogen production; replaced by clomiphene citrate
Reduces ovarian androgen mass; replaced by laparoscopic ovarian drilling
questions.explanation: Wedge resection of the ovaries reduces the total androgen-producing ovarian mass, lowering androgen levels and restoring the LH:FSH ratio to allow follicular maturation and ovulation. This has been replaced by laparoscopic ovarian drilling (LOD) using electrocautery or laser, which achieves the same goal through multiple ovarian surface punctures with equivalent efficacy and lower adhesion risk. Clomiphene citrate is first-line pharmacological ovulation induction in PCOD.
questions.question: Wedge resection of the ovaries was historically used for PCOD. Which hormonal response does wedge resection achieve and which modern treatment has replaced it?

questions.explanation: Return of menstrual bleeding indicates that one of the essential criteria for LAM effectiveness is no longer met, signalling probable return of ovulation, so an additional contraceptive method should be started promptly to avoid unintended pregnancy while breastfeeding can safely continue.
options: Start an additional contraceptive method promptly
Continue relying on LAM alone since breastfeeding continues
Assume fertility has not yet returned
Wait until 6 months before adding contraception
questions.question: A breastfeeding woman relying on LAM notices the return of menstrual bleeding at 4 months postpartum. The MOST appropriate advice is:

questions.explanation: Adolescents are characterized by impressionable minds, adventurousness, sexual awareness that may be misguided, and being in conflict with themselves and society — all while still mentally and emotionally developing. These qualities make contraceptive counselling challenging: adolescents may understand risk intellectually yet make impulsive decisions inconsistent with their stated intentions. Non-judgmental, confidential, and practical approaches are essential for effective adolescent sexual health services.
options: Her impressionable mind and adventurous attitude combined with emotional immaturity
Her excellent understanding of long-term health consequences
Her stable emotional responses and full cognitive maturity
Her complete dependence on parental guidance for all decisions
Her reduced susceptibility to peer pressure compared to older teens
questions.question: A 13-year-old female presents to a school health clinic seeking contraceptive advice. She has been sexually active for 3 months. She is concerned about privacy. Which aspect of the adolescent disposition described in teaching texts is MOST relevant to her contraceptive counselling challenge?
The Gellhorn pessary is one type used for prolapse management. What distinguishes pessaries used for prolapse management from those for stress incontinence?
questions.explanation: Pessaries for prolapse (ring, shelf, doughnut, inflatable, Gellhorn) are designed to support the pelvic structures and keep prolapsing organs within the pelvis. Incontinence pessaries specifically support the bladder neck and urethra to prevent the downswing that causes leakage with stress. Both are removable devices placed in the vagina, but their shape, placement, and mechanism of action differ based on the condition being treated.
options: Prolapse pessaries are made of metal while incontinence pessaries are silicone
Prolapse pessaries are always rigid while incontinence pessaries are always soft
Prolapse pessaries support organs; incontinence pessaries support bladder neck
Prolapse pessaries are permanent while incontinence pessaries are temporary
There is no difference; all pessaries serve the same purpose

questions.question: A 14-year-old girl has had no signs of puberty. Investigations show low FSH, low LH, and normal bone age. The MOST likely diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Low FSH and LH (hypogonadotrophic hypogonadism) in the setting of delayed puberty with normal bone age (distinguishing it from constitutional delay which typically has advanced bone age relative to maturation) points to a central (hypothalamic or pituitary) cause — such as a CNS tumour, Kallmann's syndrome, or empty sella syndrome. Turner's syndrome causes hypergonadotrophic hypogonadism (elevated FSH/LH). Normal bone age distinguishes this from constitutional delay.

questions.question: Adenomyosis is defined pathologically as the presence of endometrial glands and stroma within which structure?
questions.explanation: Adenomyosis is characterised by ectopic endometrial glands and stroma embedded within the myometrium, causing uterine enlargement, dysmenorrhoea, and menorrhagia. It differs from endometriosis, where ectopic tissue is found outside the uterus, typically on pelvic peritoneum or ovaries.

questions.question: Which of the following women would be LEAST suitable for using periodic abstinence as her SOLE contraceptive method?
options: A 35-year-old with polycystic ovary syndrome and irregular cycles
A 25-year-old exclusively breastfeeding at 3 months postpartum
A perimenopausal woman with cycle lengths varying between 23 and 45 days
questions.explanation: Periodic abstinence methods including the calendar and BBT methods are unreliable for women with irregular cycles, because the fertile window cannot be predicted accurately. Women with PCOS characteristically have irregular, anovulatory cycles with unpredictable ovulation timing. Perimenopausal women also experience highly variable cycle lengths. Both are poor candidates for period-based NFP methods.

questions.question: A 60-year-old with endometrial carcinoma confirmed on biopsy is being staged. Which imaging modality MOST accurately assesses myometrial invasion depth prior to surgery?
questions.explanation: Pelvic MRI provides superior soft tissue contrast for assessing depth of myometrial invasion and cervical stromal involvement in endometrial cancer, information that guides surgical planning including extent of lymphadenectomy. Transabdominal ultrasound and plain radiographs lack the resolution needed for accurate local staging. Accurate preoperative staging helps tailor the surgical approach to the individual risk profile.

The uterus, cervix, and upper two-thirds of the vagina develop from fusion and canalisation of the paired paramesonephric (Mullerian) ducts. The mesonephric ducts instead regress in females without functioning testosterone. Failure of fusion produces uterine anomalies such as bicornuate or septate uterus, while failure of duct formation causes Mullerian agenesis.
questions.question: A female fetus fails to develop a uterus and upper vagina due to failed fusion of the paired embryonic ducts. Which structure is primarily responsible for forming these organs?
Prior to buccal smear collection for Barr body analysis, the patient is instructed to thoroughly rinse the mouth. What is the primary reason for this preparatory step?
questions.explanation: Thorough mouth rinsing before buccal smear collection removes food debris, excess mucus, and bacterial contamination that could obscure the epithelial cells or interfere with accurate identification and counting of Barr bodies under the microscope. A clean sample improves the reliability of the test. This simple preparatory step is essential for accurate cytogenetic screening.
options: Removes debris and bacteria contaminating the sample
To reduce the patient's anxiety before the procedure
To stimulate additional saliva production for the test
To numb the buccal mucosa before scraping

questions.question: Helen Singer Kaplan's contribution to the understanding of human sexual response was to introduce which additional phase to the Masters and Johnson model?
questions.explanation: Kaplan proposed a triphasic model of desire, excitement, and orgasm, adding a distinct desire phase preceding the excitement, plateau, orgasm, and resolution phases originally described by Masters and Johnson, recognising the importance of psychological desire in sexual response.

questions.question: The Stamey procedure is a type of which surgical approach for stress incontinence?
questions.explanation: The Stamey procedure is a type of needle suspension (retropubic sling) operation for stress incontinence, where insertion is by blind directed needles through the retropubic space. Sling operations use multiple materials including synthetic substances (nylon, prolene, Teflon, mersilene mesh) or natural tissues (round ligament or external oblique aponeurosis). This is distinct from open retropubic colposuspension (Burch) and vaginal approaches.

questions.question: Retrograde urography is specifically indicated to demonstrate which pathological findings in urinary fistula assessment?
questions.explanation: Retrograde urography is used to demonstrate ureteric and vesico-vaginal fistulae by injecting contrast medium retrogradely through ureteric catheters or cystoscopically. Ultrasound urograms outline defects of the bladder and upper urinary tract. Together, these investigations delineate the anatomy of urinary fistulae and guide surgical planning, including identifying concomitant ureteric injuries.

questions.question: Which first-line chemotherapy combination is considered standard of care for epithelial ovarian cancer after optimal cytoreductive surgery?
questions.explanation: Carboplatin and paclitaxel (taxane-platinum combination) is the standard first-line chemotherapy for epithelial ovarian cancer following optimal surgical debulking. This combination has demonstrated superior survival compared to older regimens and is well-tolerated in most patients.

In adolescents, DUB is almost always due to anovulatory cycles from hypothalamic-pituitary axis immaturity. It usually resolves spontaneously as the axis matures over 2–5 years. Initial management is expectant: iron therapy to treat anaemia from menorrhagia, keeping a menstrual calendar, and conservative hormonal management with OCPs or progestins if needed. Curettage is often delayed. Organic disease (especially coagulopathy) must be excluded before labelling it DUB.
options: Expectant management with iron; DUB resolves spontaneously
questions.question: In the adolescent with DUB, which approach is the MOST appropriate initial management?

options: It has a characteristic offensive odour distinguishing it from infective causes
Normal discharge with no pathological features but excessive patient concern
It is indistinguishable from infective discharge on clinical examination alone
It produces a frothy yellow discharge similar to trichomoniasis
It causes marked vulval inflammation and excoriation
questions.question: Vaginal discharge of psychogenic origin is listed among the causes of abnormal vaginal discharge. A 24-year-old presents with profuse clear vaginal discharge but all microbiological investigations are negative and pH is normal. How does psychogenic vaginal discharge present clinically compared to infective discharge?
questions.explanation: Psychogenic vaginal discharge represents a patient's perception of excessive discharge in the context of anxiety or somatization, where the discharge is objectively normal (normal pH, normal flora, no pathological organisms) but the patient experiences it as abnormal or excessive. This falls within the psychiatric category of causes of abnormal vaginal discharge. Management requires reassurance, explanation of normal vaginal physiology, and addressing any underlying psychological issues.

options: It always presents as postmenopausal bleeding
It has identical appearance to hydatidiform mole on ultrasound
Presents in any organ via haematogenous spread
It responds identically to all antibiotics
questions.explanation: Choriocarcinoma is called 'the great imitator' because circulating trophoblast cells can settle in virtually any organ, producing metastatic disease with diverse presentations including haemoptysis (lung), neurological deficits (brain), GI haemorrhage, and liver disease. This protean presentation frequently delays diagnosis.
questions.question: Choriocarcinoma is described as 'the great imitator' because:
Endometrial carcinoma has the highest incidence among which population?
questions.explanation: Endometrial carcinoma has the highest incidence among white North American women, though the reasons for this racial disparity are not fully clear. Interestingly, while incidence is higher in white women, mortality from endometrial carcinoma is higher in black women, possibly reflecting differences in tumour type and access to treatment.

options: Minimal or absent symptoms with haemodynamic stability
hCG greater than 5000 mIU/mL and rising
Rising hCG with visible fetal cardiac activity
A large adnexal mass with free fluid
questions.question: Expectant management is being considered for a woman with a small, unruptured ectopic pregnancy and a very low, falling serum hCG. Which additional criterion would most strongly support this conservative approach rather than active treatment?
questions.explanation: Expectant management of ectopic pregnancy is reserved for women who are asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic, haemodynamically stable, with a small mass, low and declining hCG, and no evidence of rupture, since these features predict spontaneous resolution without intervention. Close follow-up with serial hCG and clinical review is mandatory during this approach to detect early signs of failure or rupture. Any deterioration warrants prompt escalation to medical or surgical treatment.

Vulval carcinoma confined to the vulva or perineum with stromal invasion greater than 1 mm is classified as Stage IB, distinguishing it from Stage IA disease where invasion is 1 mm or less and the risk of nodal spread is minimal.
questions.question: A 70-year-old woman with vulval carcinoma has a 3 cm lesion with stromal invasion of 1.5 mm confined to the vulva and no palpable groin nodes. This is MOST consistent with which FIGO stage?

questions.explanation: Major medical and psychiatric organizations worldwide (APA, WHO, RCPSYCH, WMA) have concluded that sexual orientation cannot be reliably changed through any therapeutic intervention. Conversion therapy causes severe psychological harm including depression, anxiety, self-harm, and suicidality — particularly in adolescents. It is based on the false premise that non-heterosexual orientations are disorders requiring treatment.
questions.question: Which statement MOST accurately reflects the current scientific consensus on sexual orientation change efforts (conversion therapy)?
options: Conversion therapy reliably changes sexual orientation in approximately 40% of participants
Conversion therapy is most effective when initiated before puberty
Conversion therapy is acceptable if requested voluntarily by the individual
Conversion therapy is ineffective, causes significant psychological harm, is ethically condemned
Hormonal conversion therapy reliably alters sexual orientation in women
Mechanical dilation of the cervical canal
Direct surgical excision of the fibroid
Inducing ischaemic infarction of fibroid tissue
questions.explanation: Uterine artery embolisation occludes the blood supply to fibroids using embolic particles, causing ischaemic infarction and subsequent shrinkage, while sparing the patient a surgical procedure. It is generally avoided in women who strongly desire future fertility due to uncertain effects on ovarian reserve.
questions.question: Uterine artery embolisation as treatment for symptomatic fibroids works by which mechanism?

options: It reverses easily if pregnancy is desired later
The procedure should be considered irreversible
It requires ongoing daily medication after surgery
It provides protection against sexually transmitted infections
It eliminates all risk of ectopic pregnancy entirely
questions.explanation: Tubal ligation should be considered permanent and irreversible, as reversal surgery has variable and often limited success, so thorough counselling before the procedure is essential, particularly for younger women or those uncertain about future fertility. It provides no protection against sexually transmitted infections, unlike barrier methods. Failure, though rare, can still result in ectopic pregnancy if it occurs, since tubal patency may partially recanalise.
questions.question: A 35-year-old requests permanent contraception via tubal ligation. Which counselling point is MOST important to discuss regarding the procedure's characteristics?
A woman with uterine fibroids and menorrhagia undergoes preoperative treatment with GnRH analogues (e.g., goserelin). What is the PRIMARY purpose of this preoperative GnRH analogue therapy?
options: To permanently shrink fibroids and avoid surgery
Reduce fibroid size and correct anaemia pre-surgery
To stimulate endometrial growth for easier curettage
questions.explanation: Preoperative GnRH analogue therapy for 3–6 months induces hypo-oestrogenism causing temporary fibroid shrinkage (up to 30–60% volume reduction) and amenorrhoea, allowing correction of iron-deficiency anaemia before surgery. This reduces intraoperative blood loss and may convert an open to laparoscopic procedure. Importantly, fibroids regrow to original size after discontinuation, so GnRH analogues are not a standalone treatment.

questions.question: A couple requesting sterilization should be counselled that the MOST important factor influencing regret after the procedure is:
questions.explanation: Younger age at the time of sterilization is consistently associated with a higher likelihood of later regret, often related to changes in relationship status or desire for more children, making thorough counselling regarding permanence particularly important for younger patients.
options: Being married at the time of the procedure
Having the procedure performed in a hospital setting
Having more than two living children
Undergoing the procedure under general anaesthesia
Young age at the time of the procedure

questions.question: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) is defined as infection of the upper genital tract. Which combination of organisms is MOST commonly implicated in PID in young sexually active Nigerian women?
questions.explanation: PID is most commonly polymicrobial, involving Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis as primary ascending pathogens from the cervix, with anaerobes (Bacteroides, Peptostreptococcus), Gram-negative enteric organisms, and Mycoplasma as secondary polymicrobial contributors. N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis are the initiating pathogens in the majority of young sexually active women with PID in Nigeria. Treatment must cover all these organisms with broad-spectrum antibiotic combinations.

Fallopian tube carcinoma classically presents with the triad of watery or blood-stained vaginal discharge, colicky pelvic pain, and a palpable pelvic mass, sometimes referred to as hydrops tubae profluens, although this presentation is seen in only a minority of cases.
options: Vaginal discharge, pelvic pain, and a pelvic mass
Postmenopausal bleeding, weight gain, and constipation
questions.question: Fallopian tube carcinoma classically presents with which triad of symptoms?

questions.explanation: LAM is highly effective only when the mother remains amenorrhoeic, is exclusively or nearly exclusively breastfeeding on demand day and night, and the infant is under six months of age, since effectiveness declines significantly once any of these criteria is no longer met.
questions.question: The three criteria that must ALL be met for LAM to be considered highly effective contraception are amenorrhoea, full or near-full breastfeeding, and:
Type II endometrial carcinoma, exemplified by serous carcinoma, characteristically arises in the context of:
questions.explanation: Type II endometrial cancers, including serous and clear cell carcinomas, typically arise from atrophic rather than hyperplastic endometrium in older, often thinner women, and behave more aggressively than the oestrogen-driven type I endometrioid carcinomas.

options: Complete removal of the uterus and both adnexa
Sampling of lymph nodes and omentectomy only
Debulking with residual disease of any volume
questions.question: The term 'optimal cytoreduction' in ovarian cancer surgery refers to:
questions.explanation: Optimal cytoreduction (debulking) in ovarian cancer refers to surgical removal of all visible tumour, ideally leaving no residual disease (R0 resection) or minimal residual disease (less than 1 cm). Optimal surgery significantly improves the effectiveness of subsequent chemotherapy and survival outcomes.

questions.question: A 38-year-old woman with large uterine fibroids is offered myomectomy rather than hysterectomy. What is her primary concern that makes myomectomy the more appropriate choice?
options: Preservation of fertility and the uterus
Elimination of any future fibroid recurrence risk
questions.explanation: Myomectomy removes fibroids while preserving the uterus, making it the appropriate choice for women who wish to retain their fertility or simply keep their uterus, unlike hysterectomy which removes the uterus entirely and precludes future pregnancy. It does carry a risk of fibroid recurrence, unlike hysterectomy, which is a trade-off discussed with the patient. The specific number, size, and location of fibroids influence the feasibility and surgical approach for myomectomy.

questions.question: A woman taking the progestogen-only pill reports she is three hours late taking her dose. What is the MOST appropriate immediate advice regarding her contraceptive protection?
options: Double the next dose to compensate fully
Stop the pill and restart a new pack
Additional contraceptive precautions needed for two days
No additional precautions are needed at all
questions.explanation: Traditional progestogen-only pills have a narrow three-hour window; being late by more than three hours reduces contraceptive efficacy, so additional barrier precautions are advised for the next two days while continuing the pill as normal. Emergency contraception is only needed if unprotected intercourse has already occurred during the period of reduced protection. Desogestrel-only pills have a wider twelve-hour window, an important distinction in counselling.

questions.question: Endometrial hyperplasia in DUB carries clinical significance because:
options: It is painful and causes dysmenorrhoea
It prevents pregnancy by blocking implantation
It requires hysterectomy as the only treatment option
It can progress to adenomatous hyperplasia and carcinoma
questions.explanation: Endometrial hyperplasia is significant because it lies on a spectrum that can progress from simple hyperplasia through adenomatous (complex) hyperplasia to endometrial carcinoma if the underlying hormonal disturbance (unopposed oestrogen stimulation from anovulation) is not corrected. Simple hyperplasia carries a low risk of malignant transformation, while atypical hyperplasia carries a 30–50% risk. Treatment is with progestogens, with re-sampling to confirm regression.

Hysteroscopic myomectomy directly removes the submucosal fibroid distorting the cavity while preserving the uterus and fertility potential, making it the preferred option for cavity-distorting fibroids causing heavy bleeding in women desiring fertility. Uterine artery embolisation and ablation do not reliably restore normal cavity anatomy and may compromise future fertility. Hysterectomy is definitive but removes fertility entirely.
questions.question: A 45-year-old with heavy, prolonged periods is found to have a submucosal fibroid distorting the endometrial cavity on saline infusion sonography. Which treatment option MOST directly addresses the cavity distortion while preserving fertility?
A woman with early-stage cervical carcinoma undergoes treatment and is told her overall 5-year survival, averaged across all stages of the disease, is approximately which figure?
questions.explanation: When averaged across all stages at diagnosis, overall 5-year survival for cervical carcinoma is approximately 50 percent, reflecting the wide range from near-cure in early localised disease to poor prognosis in advanced disease. Early detection through screening significantly improves individual prognosis. This average underlines the importance of population-based cervical screening programmes.

The urorectal septum (a mesodermal fold descending between the allantois and the hindgut) divides the cloaca into the anterior urogenital sinus and the posterior proctodeum (anorectal canal). Failure of this division leads to persistent cloaca, a serious anomaly with combined urinary, genital, and rectal openings. The Müllerian tubercle is where the Müllerian ducts contact the urogenital sinus, and the vaginal plate forms from this contact.
questions.question: The cloaca in the embryo divides into an anterior urogenital sinus and a posterior proctodeum. The structure that divides the cloaca is the:

options: The luteal phase, which is fixed at 14 days
The follicular phase, which varies in length
questions.explanation: The follicular (proliferative) phase is the variable component of the menstrual cycle, lasting anywhere from 7 to 21 days depending on how long it takes for the dominant follicle to mature and produce the oestradiol threshold required for the LH surge. The luteal phase is relatively constant at approximately 14 days (range 12–16) in ovulatory cycles. Cycle irregularity almost always reflects variation in follicular phase length.
questions.question: A patient has irregular periods with cycle length varying from 19 to 42 days over 12 months. Which phase of the cycle is MOST likely to be variable in length, accounting for this irregularity?

questions.explanation: Patients with unhealed complete perineal tears and low RVF learn to kink the rectum forwards by contracting the pubo-coccygeus portions of the levator ani, achieving continence of formed faeces but not flatus or liquid stools. High RVF leakage cannot be controlled by this mechanism because the aperture is above the pelvic floor, making the fistula inaccessible to this compensatory muscular kinking manoeuvre.
options: Voluntary contraction of the external anal sphincter
Reflexic rectal contraction squeezing the fistula closed
questions.question: High RVF differs from low RVF in terms of continence because leakage from high RVF cannot be controlled by the mechanism used in low RVF. What is this mechanism?

questions.explanation: The bio-social gap widens due to earlier biological maturation (declining menarcheal age from improved nutrition) on one hand, and delayed socioeconomic independence (prolonged education, urbanization, delayed marriage) on the other. This gap creates an extended window of sexual activity without the protective framework of marriage or adult independence. It is the central construct explaining adolescent reproductive health vulnerability in Nigeria.
questions.question: A public health review identifies that the bio-social gap in Nigeria has been widening over recent decades. Which two simultaneous trends are responsible?
options: Rising teenage pregnancy rates and falling STI rates
Improved contraceptive access and rising poverty
Later menarche from nutritional improvement and earlier marriage
Rising HIV rates and decreasing sexual debut age in males
Earlier biological maturation and delayed socioeconomic independence

questions.explanation: Interstim therapy is a sacral neuromodulation technique used to treat overactive bladder. An electrode is placed through the corresponding sacral foramen, and a mild electrical current stimulates the sacral nerves. It achieves a 50-80% success rate at 3-5 years. Complications include pain, infection, and lead migration. It represents a minimally invasive neuromodulation option between conservative and surgical management.
questions.question: The Interstim sacral neuromodulation device is placed through which anatomical pathway for overactive bladder treatment?
Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for menorrhagia are most effective when taken:
questions.explanation: NSAIDs for menorrhagia are most effective when started at the onset of menstruation (when prostaglandin levels in the endometrium are rising) and continued throughout the days of heavy flow. Starting before menstruation begins (e.g., 3 days before) offers no additional benefit in most studies and increases unnecessary exposure. They are taken only during menstruation, not throughout the cycle, which reduces side effects compared to continuous use.
options: From Day 1 of the cycle onwards continuously
On Day 14 of the cycle only
From onset of menstruation through the period of heavy flow
Three days before the expected period starts
As a single loading dose at the start of menses

questions.explanation: With bilateral absent fallopian tubes, natural conception and treatments relying on tubal transport such as intrauterine insemination are not viable, making in-vitro fertilisation, which bypasses the tubes entirely by direct embryo transfer into the uterus, the appropriate treatment. This represents the definitive fertility solution for absolute tubal factor infertility. Success rates depend on other factors such as ovarian reserve and uterine receptivity.
questions.question: A 35-year-old woman with infertility and a history of bilateral salpingectomy for ectopic pregnancies is counselled on treatment options. Which fertility treatment is most appropriate given her absent tubes?
Carcinoma in situ of the cervix is distinguished histologically from CIN III by a specific additional feature beyond full-thickness epithelial involvement. What is this distinguishing feature?
questions.explanation: Carcinoma in situ describes full-thickness epithelial replacement by undifferentiated, malignant-appearing cells with complete loss of normal maturation, but critically without invasion through the basement membrane; in modern classification this is essentially equivalent to CIN III. The key feature distinguishing both from invasive carcinoma is the intact basement membrane. Recognising this preserves the distinction between pre-invasive and invasive disease, which has major treatment implications.
options: Invasion through the basement membrane into the stroma
Full-thickness replacement without basement membrane invasion

questions.question: A 45-year-old woman with increasing cycle irregularity, occasional hot flushes, and elevated FSH (45 IU/L) most likely represents:
questions.explanation: In perimenopausal women, menstrual irregularities result from decreasing numbers of ovarian follicles and their increased resistance to gonadotrophin stimulation. This results in elevated FSH levels (as the pituitary responds to declining inhibin and oestrogen), anovulatory cycles, and irregular periods. Hot flushes reflect oestrogen fluctuation. This is physiologically expected in the late 40s–early 50s. Organic disease remains possible and investigation is still indicated.
options: Perimenopausal follicular decline and gonadotrophin resistance
Premature ovarian failure before the expected age

questions.explanation: Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY) is the most common chromosomal cause of male infertility, causing progressive hyalinization and fibrosis of seminiferous tubules with loss of Sertoli and Leydig cells. This results in azoospermia, hypergonadotropic hypogonadism, and testosterone deficiency causing gynaecomastia, small firm testes, and tall stature (due to extra X chromosome's effect on bone growth). Testicular sperm extraction (TESE) combined with ICSI offers limited fertility options.
questions.question: A 26-year-old male presents with gynaecomastia, small firm testes, tall stature, and azoospermia. Karyotype shows 47, XXY. Which condition does this represent and which cell type is primarily affected?
options: Klinefelter syndrome; Sertoli and Leydig cells
Down syndrome; all gonadal cells equally

questions.explanation: Removal of both ovaries directly eliminates the source of oestrogen and eggs, causing immediate surgical menopause with amenorrhoea and a compensatory rise in FSH due to loss of negative feedback, distinct from other causes such as hypothalamic suppression, which would typically show low or normal FSH. Given her young age, hormone replacement therapy is often recommended to mitigate the long-term risks of premature oestrogen deficiency, such as osteoporosis and cardiovascular disease. Fertility preservation counselling is ideally addressed before such surgery when feasible.
questions.question: A woman presents with amenorrhoea after bilateral oophorectomy for endometriosis at age 29. Her FSH is markedly elevated. What is the primary underlying cause of her amenorrhoea?
options: Surgical menopause from removal of both ovaries
Reducing capillary fragility and platelet adhesion
Suppressing gonadotrophin secretion from the pituitary
questions.question: Ethamsylate in DUB treatment works by which mechanism?
questions.explanation: Ethamsylate (Dicynene) reduces capillary fragility and enhances platelet adhesion at the capillary level, reducing blood loss in menorrhagia. It is used as an adjunct in DUB management. Its mechanism differs from NSAIDs (prostaglandin inhibition) and antifibrinolytics (fibrinolysis inhibition). It is particularly useful in patients where other agents are contraindicated, though its efficacy is considered modest compared to antifibrinolytics and NSAIDs.

options: Premature ovarian failure causing streak gonads
questions.explanation: Adolescent DUB results from immaturity of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis: the positive feedback response of the pituitary to rising oestrogen (required to generate the mid-cycle LH surge) is impaired. Without an adequate LH surge, ovulation does not occur, the endometrium is exposed to unopposed oestrogen, and irregular anovulatory bleeding results. This typically resolves spontaneously over 2–5 years as the axis matures. Treatment is expectant; curettage is often delayed.
questions.question: The endocrine basis for DUB in adolescence is primarily:
Which of the following is the FIRST-LINE pharmacological treatment for erectile dysfunction?
options: Phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitors such as sildenafil
Vacuum erection device plus venous constriction band
questions.explanation: PDE5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil) are the established first-line oral pharmacological treatment for ED. They enhance the nitric oxide-cGMP pathway by preventing cGMP breakdown, facilitating smooth muscle relaxation and penile blood flow. They require sexual stimulation to work and are effective in approximately 70% of ED cases. They are contraindicated with nitrates due to hypotension risk.

questions.question: The labia minora differ from the labia majora in that they lack which of the following?
questions.explanation: The labia minora are hairless skin folds that lack a bed of adipose tissue, distinguishing them clearly from the hair-bearing, adipose-cushioned labia majora. The labia minora form the prepuce and frenulum of the clitoris. This anatomical distinction is important in reconstructive gynaecological surgery.

options: Switch immediately to a copper IUD only
Continue using the same diaphragm indefinitely without review
questions.question: A woman is fitted with a diaphragm and gains significant weight over the following months. She should be advised to:
questions.explanation: Significant weight change can alter vaginal dimensions, so a woman experiencing substantial weight gain or loss after diaphragm fitting should have the size reassessed to ensure a proper fit is maintained and contraceptive effectiveness is not compromised.

questions.question: A 30-year-old woman with a missed abortion at 10 weeks is counselled about coagulopathy risk. After how many weeks of retention of dead products of conception does DIC risk become clinically significant?
questions.explanation: The risk of DIC in missed abortion increases significantly after approximately 4–6 weeks of retention of the dead products of conception, as prolonged tissue degeneration releases thromboplastins that progressively activate the coagulation cascade. This is why prompt uterine evacuation is recommended once missed abortion is diagnosed. Serial coagulation profiles should be monitored if there is any delay in evacuation beyond this timeframe.
options: DIC risk is independent of duration of retention

questions.question: Which pelvic ligament is described as the strongest support of the uterus and is also called the Mackenrodt ligament?
questions.explanation: The transverse cervical ligament, also known as the cardinal ligament or Mackenrodt's ligament, arises from the lateral aspect of the cervix and inserts into the lateral pelvic wall. It is the strongest support of the uterus, and once weakened (commonly during childbirth), uterine prolapse becomes likely.

questions.question: A woman at 34 weeks presents with sudden, severe abdominal pain, a tense, tender uterus, and dark vaginal bleeding, with fetal heart rate abnormalities on monitoring. Which diagnosis does this presentation most strongly suggest?
questions.explanation: Sudden severe abdominal pain with a tense, tender ('woody hard') uterus, dark vaginal bleeding, and fetal heart rate abnormalities is the classic presentation of placental abruption, where premature separation of the placenta causes concealed or revealed haemorrhage and can rapidly compromise fetal oxygenation. This differs from placenta praevia, which typically presents with painless bright red bleeding. Urgent assessment and often expedited delivery are required given the risk to both mother and fetus.

options: Stratum compactum is shed; stratum spongiosum regenerates
Entire endometrium is shed including stratum basalis
Stratum basalis is shed; stratum compactum remains
Only stratum spongiosum is shed; compactum and basalis remain
Stratum compactum and spongiosum are shed; basalis remains
questions.explanation: During menstruation, the functionalis layer (comprising the upper stratum compactum at 25%, and the middle stratum spongiosum at 50%) is shed. The lower stratum basalis (25%) remains intact and serves as the regenerative layer from which the new endometrium proliferates in the next cycle under the influence of oestrogen. The basalis has its own blood supply from basal arteries that are spared during menstrual vasoconstriction.
questions.question: The endometrium in the late secretory phase is divided into three layers. Which layer is shed during menstruation and which remains as the basis for regeneration?
Exhibitionistic disorder (exposing genitals to unsuspecting persons for sexual gratification) is classified as:
options: A sexual orientation variant requiring no clinical attention
A personality disorder requiring mood stabilizer treatment
A dissociative disorder following childhood trauma exclusively
A paraphilic disorder under DSM-5 when causing significant distress or involving non-consenting persons
Normal sexual behaviour in individuals with high testosterone levels
questions.explanation: Exhibitionistic disorder is a DSM-5 paraphilic disorder characterized by recurrent, intense sexual arousal from exposing one's genitals to unsuspecting individuals, causing significant personal distress, acting on these urges, or involving non-consenting persons. It is distinguished from exhibitionistic paraphilia (preference without distress or harmful behavior). Treatment combines cognitive-behavioral therapy and pharmacological androgen suppression in severe cases.

questions.question: Genital herpes caused by HSV-2 is characterised by which pattern of recurrence compared with HSV-1 genital infection?
options: Complete absence of recurrence after the first episode
questions.explanation: Genital infection caused by HSV-2 tends to recur more frequently than genital infection caused by HSV-1, reflecting differences in viral latency and reactivation patterns between the two herpes simplex virus types, which is important information for patient counselling regarding prognosis.

questions.question: Vulval intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN) in young women is MOST closely associated with:
questions.explanation: In younger women, VIN is most closely associated with HPV infection, particularly HPV type 16. This HPV-related pathway leads to the usual-type VIN (warty/basaloid), which may progress to invasive squamous cell carcinoma, especially in immunocompromised patients. HPV vaccination may help reduce the incidence of HPV-related vulval neoplasia.

questions.question: Genitourinary atrophy from post-menopausal oestrogen deficiency causes a change in the cervix-to-corpus ratio. What ratio is considered normal in the reproductive years versus post-menopause?
options: No change in corpus:cervix ratio with menopause
questions.explanation: In the reproductive years, the uterine corpus:cervix ratio is approximately 3:1, reflecting the oestrogen-responsive myometrium dominating. After menopause, oestrogen withdrawal causes disproportionate atrophy of the corpus, reversing this ratio to approximately 1:2, which is the norm in post-menopausal and prepubertal women. This reversal is used clinically on ultrasound to assess the degree of post-menopausal atrophy.

questions.question: The Pap smear must be obtained BEFORE digital vaginal examination because:
options: The patient would be too uncomfortable after digital exam
Lubricant from digital exam contaminates cells and compromises cytology
questions.explanation: Lubricant used during digital examination can coat the cervical cells and interfere with cytological interpretation, producing false-negative or inadequate Pap smear results. For this reason, speculum examination and cell collection must precede digital examination. Only water may be used on the speculum to avoid this contamination.

questions.question: Chronic cervicitis specifically differs from acute cervicitis in that the discharge is:
questions.explanation: Chronic cervicitis presents with persistent leukorrhoea that is thick, viscid, and whitish or mucopurulent. Other features include postcoital bleeding, lower abdominal discomfort, and dyspareunia. Investigations include bacteriological examination, Pap smear, colposcopic examination, and biopsy. Treatment options include antibiotics (especially in infertility cases), cryotherapy, thermal cauterization, and laser ablation.
options: Absent, as chronic cervicitis is always asymptomatic

questions.explanation: Post-infective tubal damage from PID (particularly gonorrhoea and chlamydia) is the primary driver of the extraordinarily high rate of tuboperitoneal infertility in Nigeria (66%) versus the USA (30%). The high STI burden, delayed treatment-seeking, and limited healthcare access in Nigeria result in severe tubal scarring and hydrosalpinx. This makes PID prevention through STI treatment the single most impactful strategy for reducing infertility in Nigeria.
questions.question: In Nigeria, the MOST common single cause of female infertility is tuboperitoneal disease, accounting for 66% of cases compared to 30% in the USA. Which condition is the PRIMARY driver of this disparity?

A 17-year-old girl has never menstruated despite normal breast and pubic hair development. Her uterus is confirmed present on ultrasound but she has cyclical lower abdominal pain. Which diagnosis best explains both findings together?
questions.explanation: Cyclical abdominal pain with primary amenorrhoea in a girl with normal secondary sexual characteristics and a present uterus suggests an outflow tract obstruction, such as an imperforate hymen, where menstrual blood accumulates behind the obstruction (haematocolpos) rather than a failure of ovarian or uterine development. This differs from MRKH syndrome, where the uterus is absent. Surgical correction of the obstruction typically resolves the symptoms.

Stress urinary incontinence results from weakened pelvic floor musculature and inadequate urethral sphincter support, allowing leakage when intra-abdominal pressure rises during coughing, sneezing, or exertion, without an associated urge to void. Detrusor overactivity instead produces urgency and urge incontinence, a different underlying mechanism. Recognising the absence of urgency helps distinguish stress incontinence from overactive bladder in clinical assessment.
options: Weakened pelvic floor and urethral support
questions.question: A 55-year-old with stress urinary incontinence leaks urine on coughing and sneezing but has no urgency symptoms. Which underlying mechanism MOST directly explains this pattern?

questions.explanation: Condyloma acuminatum is caused by human papillomavirus. On the cervix, lesions tend to be flatter and less overtly exophytic than the classic cauliflower-like warts seen on the vulva, sometimes requiring colposcopy for identification. HPV subtypes involved also carry oncogenic potential, warranting cytological follow-up. Biopsy may be needed to exclude coexisting dysplasia.
questions.question: A young sexually active woman presents with a cervix showing multiple discrete, warty, cauliflower-like lesions. Which organism is responsible, and how does the cervical lesion typically differ from vulval lesions caused by the same organism?
options: Herpes simplex virus; cervical lesions vesiculate
HPV; cervical lesions are flatter than vulval warts
Treponema pallidum; cervical lesions ulcerate deeply
Chlamydia trachomatis; cervical lesions are follicular only
Neisseria gonorrhoeae; cervical lesions are purulent only

questions.question: A youth health policy document proposes targeting the age group most at risk for simultaneous STI acquisition and unintended pregnancy. According to global statistics, approximately how many teenagers give birth worldwide each year?
questions.explanation: Approximately 15 million teenagers give birth each year globally, accounting for approximately one-fifth (20%) of all births worldwide. This staggering number reflects the scale of the adolescent reproductive health crisis and the inadequacy of current contraceptive and sexual health education programmes. The overwhelming majority of these births occur in low- and middle-income countries, disproportionately contributing to maternal and infant morbidity.

options: Resolution phase with distinct male refractory period
Plateau phase distinguishing sustained from brief arousal
Desire phase as a distinct psychological precursor to physical arousal
questions.question: Helen Singer Kaplan's triphasic model of sexual response adds which component to the Masters and Johnson model?
questions.explanation: Helen Singer Kaplan (1979) extended the Masters and Johnson four-phase model by adding 'Desire' as a separate preceding psychological phase. Kaplan proposed a triphasic model: Desire (cognitive-motivational, dopamine-driven), Excitement/Arousal, and Orgasm. This addition was clinically important because it provided a diagnostic framework for hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD) as a distinct condition, separate from arousal or orgasmic disorders.

questions.question: Vesico-vaginal fistula due to gynaecological surgery is particularly likely when which condition distorts the normal anatomy?
questions.explanation: Gynaecological surgery VVF is particularly likely when there has been anatomical distortion caused by infection (PID), endometriosis, carcinoma, or preceding small blood vessel damage (endarteritis) caused by radiation. These conditions obliterate normal tissue planes, increase the risk of inadvertent bladder injury, and impair healing. Obstructed labour causing avascular necrosis is the other major cause of VVF, predominant in developing countries. SUBTOPIC 6: PERINEAL LACERATION, RECTOVAGINAL FISTULA AND URINARY INJURIES

questions.question: Which physiological amenorrhoea is caused by the same hypothalamic prolactin-mediated GnRH suppression mechanism as hyperprolactinaemia?
questions.explanation: Lactational amenorrhoea occurs because suckling stimulates prolactin release, which suppresses hypothalamic GnRH pulsatility through the same mechanism as pathological hyperprolactinaemia. This is why hyperprolactinaemia mimics the hormonal state of lactation. The longer and more frequently a woman breastfeeds, the more prolonged the lactational amenorrhoea. Understanding this mechanism explains why dopamine agonists restore menstruation in hyperprolactinaemia.

options: Full spontaneous resolution without residual damage
questions.question: Pelvic inflammatory disease caused by an ascending sexually transmitted infection is LEAST likely to produce which of the following long-term outcomes?
questions.explanation: While mild pelvic inflammatory disease may resolve without lasting effects, more significant or recurrent infection frequently causes tubal scarring leading to infertility, chronic pelvic pain, or ectopic pregnancy, so complete resolution without any residual damage is the least likely outcome once significant inflammation has occurred.

Add-back therapy using low-dose oestrogen and progestin alongside continued GnRH agonist treatment mitigates hypoestrogenic side effects such as hot flushes and bone loss while preserving the therapeutic suppression of fibroid growth, allowing safer extended use beyond the usual six-month limit. Calcium alone is insufficient to counter oestrogen deficiency effects. Increasing agonist dose would worsen hypoestrogenism rather than help it.
options: Stop all therapy without alternative plan
Increase the GnRH agonist dose further
Add-back therapy with low-dose hormone replacement
questions.question: A woman on long-term GnRH agonist therapy for symptomatic fibroids develops hot flushes and reduced bone density on follow-up. What is the MOST appropriate strategy to manage this hypoestrogenic side effect if extended therapy is needed?

questions.explanation: Progestogen-only pills do not contain oestrogen, which can reduce milk volume and quality, making them the preferred hormonal option for breastfeeding women who wish to start oral contraception without compromising lactation, unlike combined oral contraceptives.
options: Require less strict timing of daily intake
Eliminate the need for barrier contraception entirely
Provide higher contraceptive efficacy than combined pills
questions.question: Progestogen-only pills are generally preferred over combined oral contraceptives during breastfeeding primarily because they:

questions.explanation: Cryotherapy destroys tissue relatively superficially compared with cone biopsy or deep excisional/ablative techniques, making cervical stenosis a less frequent complication after cryotherapy. Deeper excisional procedures carry a higher risk of scarring and canal narrowing. This informs treatment choice in women wishing to preserve future fertility with minimal stenosis risk.
options: Loop electrosurgical excision with a deep pass
questions.question: A woman undergoing treatment for CIN develops cervical stenosis as a late complication. Which treatment modality for CIN is least likely to be implicated in causing this complication because of its more superficial tissue effect?
CEA (Carcinoembryonic Antigen) as a gynaecological tumour marker is expressed in what percentage of malignant mucinous ovarian tumours?
questions.explanation: CEA is expressed in 100% of malignant mucinous ovarian tumours, making it a useful marker specifically for this histological type. It is also expressed in 100% of atypical endometrial hyperplasia, 60% of endometrial carcinoma, and 50–80% of squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix.

For uterine prolapse in a woman with a completed family, vaginal hysterectomy with pelvic floor repair is the operation of choice. This includes anterior colporrhaphy, posterior colpoperineorrhaphy, and removal of the uterus. For women desiring future fertility, the Manchester operation is preferred, and for elderly non-sexually active women, Le Fort's operation is appropriate.
questions.question: Vaginal hysterectomy with pelvic floor repair in a woman with completed family is specifically indicated for which form of prolapse?

questions.explanation: Precocious puberty is defined as premature initiation of sexual development and/or menstrual bleeding before the age of 8 years in girls (and before 9 years in boys). It is more common in girls than boys, and idiopathic/constitutional causes are most common in girls. Premature thelarche and pubarche are defined at less than 6 and 4 years respectively. Early evaluation is needed to exclude CNS or tumour causes.
questions.question: Precocious puberty is defined as premature development of secondary sexual characteristics before the age of:

questions.explanation: Potent topical corticosteroids (e.g., clobetasol propionate) are the first-line treatment for lichen sclerosus of the vulva. They relieve pruritus, improve skin texture, and reduce the risk of scarring and labial fusion. Regular surveillance is essential given the 4–5% risk of malignant transformation to invasive squamous cell carcinoma.
questions.question: Topical steroids are the first-line treatment for which benign vulval condition?

questions.explanation: Deep lacerations involving the perineal body that are not sutured or fail to heal increase the possibility of subsequent uterovaginal prolapse. This is because the perineal body is a critical point of attachment for multiple pelvic floor structures. Its disruption weakens the posterior pelvic floor support, contributing to the pathogenesis of prolapse over time.
questions.question: An unrepaired deep laceration involving the perineal body increases the risk of which long-term complication?
options: Chronic pelvic pain from nerve entrapment

questions.explanation: Chlamydia trachomatis is characteristically asymptomatic in over 70–80% of infected women, meaning most cases go undiagnosed and untreated. Ascending infection causes pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), endometritis, salpingitis, and perihepatic inflammation (Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome). Repeated or untreated infections cause tubal scarring, ectopic pregnancy, and tubal factor infertility — the most important long-term consequences.
questions.question: Chlamydia trachomatis is the MOST common bacterial STI worldwide. Its significant clinical importance in women lies PRIMARILY in its:
options: Causing visible genital ulcers leading to diagnostic clarity
High likelihood of causing immediate severe pelvic pain at acquisition
Frequently asymptomatic nature that leads to undiagnosed PID and infertility
Primary role in causing hepatitis and liver damage
Causing neonatal meningitis when transmitted at delivery

questions.explanation: Low birth weight and prematurity are the most documented infant complications of adolescent pregnancy, driven by poor maternal nutrition, anaemia, and pre-eclampsia. These neonates are also at greater risk of birth asphyxia, failure to thrive, and increased perinatal mortality. Adolescent mothers are less likely to breastfeed effectively, compounding neonatal nutritional risk.
questions.question: A 16-year-old primigravida is admitted at 36 weeks with severe pre-eclampsia. Her school records show poor nutritional intake. Which infant complication is MOST directly associated with adolescent pregnancy?

A woman requests information on why the diaphragm and cervical cap are generally considered LESS effective than long-acting reversible methods. The MOST accurate explanation is that these barrier methods:
options: Cannot be used with any form of lubricant
Provide guaranteed protection regardless of correct use
Are highly dependent on correct and consistent user technique
Work through a systemic hormonal mechanism
questions.explanation: Unlike long-acting reversible methods such as implants and intrauterine devices, which do not depend on ongoing user action once placed, the diaphragm and cervical cap require correct fitting, insertion technique, and consistent use with every act of intercourse, making their real-world typical-use effectiveness considerably lower.

Rifampicin is a potent enzyme inducer that markedly reduces the efficacy of all hormonal contraceptives — including combined pills, progestogen-only pills, implants, and the levonorgestrel IUS — by accelerating their hepatic metabolism. The copper IUD is a non-hormonal method completely unaffected by liver enzyme induction. It is the safest contraceptive choice during rifampicin therapy.
questions.question: A 26-year-old nurse on rifampicin for pulmonary tuberculosis requests contraception. Which contraceptive method would be LEAST affected by her current medication?

questions.explanation: Premature ejaculation is defined as persistent or recurrent ejaculation occurring within approximately 1 minute of vaginal penetration (lifelong type) or a clinically significant reduction in ejaculatory latency (acquired type), causing personal distress. The distress criterion distinguishes disorder from a man who ejaculates quickly but is not bothered by it. It is the most common male sexual dysfunction.
questions.question: Premature (early) ejaculation is clinically defined when ejaculation occurs:
options: Before any form of genital stimulation
Only during masturbation and not during partnered sex
After more than 30 minutes of sustained intercourse
Within approximately 1 minute of vaginal penetration, persistently and causing distress
In the absence of a full erection

questions.question: A patient with urinary injuries secondary to obstructed labour is noted to have a non-functioning kidney on imaging. At minimum, what FIGO stage of cervical disease should be considered if this finding is attributed to tumour?
questions.explanation: In the context of cervical carcinoma, hydronephrosis or a non-functioning kidney (not due to other causes) places the disease at Stage IIIb, regardless of other tumour extent. This is because ureteric obstruction indicates extension to the pelvic side wall. Obstructed labour, however, can independently cause ureteric injury and non-functioning kidney without malignancy, which is why clinical context is essential.

options: Complete inability to achieve orgasm despite adequate stimulation
Excessive sexual desire causing interpersonal disruption
Deficient or absent sexual fantasies and desire for sexual activity
Physical pain during sexual activity in women
Absence of vaginal lubrication during stimulation
questions.question: Hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD) in women is MOST appropriately defined as:
questions.explanation: HSDD is characterized by persistently deficient or absent sexual fantasies and desire for sexual activity, causing significant personal distress or interpersonal difficulty. The distress criterion distinguishes disorder from simple low desire without personal impact. It may be global or situational, lifelong or acquired, and can have psychological or hormonal underpinnings.

options: Direct endometrial progesterone delivery causing atrophy
Preventing pregnancy by thickening cervical mucus only
Increasing platelet aggregation at the endometrial level
Stimulating FSH to promote regular ovulation
Releasing oestrogen to stimulate endometrial proliferation
questions.question: The levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS, Mirena) in DUB works primarily by:
questions.explanation: The LNG-IUS delivers levonorgestrel directly to the endometrium, causing profound endometrial atrophy and glandular suppression, dramatically reducing menstrual blood loss — often achieving amenorrhoea. It is superior to medical therapy in reducing menstrual flow and is a favourable option for patients with intractable bleeding associated with chronic illness. Amenorrhoea occurs in a significant proportion of users. Systemic progestogenic side effects are minimal due to the local delivery.

Kegel exercises strengthen the levator ani and other pelvic floor muscles, improving their ability to support the bladder neck and urethra. Stronger pelvic floor muscles maintain urethral coaptation and bladder neck elevation during sudden increases in intra-abdominal pressure (coughing, sneezing), preventing the downswing that causes stress leakage. This is the physiological basis for pelvic floor exercises in SUI management.
questions.question: Kegel exercises improve stress urinary incontinence by which mechanism?
options: Stimulating the sacral reflex arc to suppress detrusor

questions.explanation: A premenstrual (late luteal phase) endometrial biopsy is timed to assess whether the endometrium has undergone the expected secretory changes driven by adequate progesterone exposure following ovulation, historically used to evaluate for luteal phase defect. This histological dating has largely been superseded by hormonal and ultrasound assessment of ovulation in modern practice, but remains conceptually important. Correct timing relative to the next expected period is essential for meaningful interpretation.
options: To confirm the presence of an intrauterine device
To directly visualise the fallopian tubes
To assess for secretory change from progesterone
questions.question: During infertility investigation, an endometrial biopsy is taken in the premenstrual (late luteal) phase. What is the primary purpose of timing the biopsy at this specific point in the cycle?

questions.explanation: Papillary excrescences projecting into or from a cyst, combined with ascites, are classic sonographic and clinical markers of ovarian malignancy. Simple unilocular thin-walled cysts are almost always benign. Ascites reflects peritoneal seeding, which does not occur with benign functional cysts.
questions.question: A 45-year-old woman has a complex ovarian mass with papillary excrescences and ascites on imaging. Which feature MOST strongly favours malignancy over a benign process?
options: Presence of papillary projections with ascites

questions.explanation: Hyperemesis gravidarum with dehydration, electrolyte disturbance, and ketonuria requires intravenous fluid and electrolyte replacement alongside antiemetic medication, since conservative dietary measures alone are insufficient once this level of severity is reached. Thiamine supplementation is also important to prevent Wernicke's encephalopathy in prolonged vomiting. Termination of pregnancy is not indicated as a first-line treatment for hyperemesis, which is usually managed successfully with supportive and pharmacological measures.
questions.question: A woman with severe hyperemesis gravidarum in the first trimester develops electrolyte disturbance and ketonuria. Which class of medication is appropriate as part of management if conservative measures fail?
options: High-dose oral iron supplementation as the primary treatment
Antiemetics with fluid and electrolyte replacement
Immediate termination of pregnancy as the only option
Oral corticosteroids as first-line before any other treatment

questions.explanation: Rudimentary horn ectopic pregnancies are particularly dangerous because the thick myometrial wall surrounding the pregnancy allows it to grow to a larger size before rupture, resulting in catastrophic haemorrhage when rupture eventually occurs. Unlike tubal ectopics that rupture early (6–8 weeks), rudimentary horn ectopics may rupture in the second trimester. This makes them associated with higher mortality than ampullary ectopics.
options: It is associated with an intact fallopian tube
Grows larger before rupture due to myometrial support
It has a lower hCG than intrauterine pregnancy
questions.question: A patient presents with an ectopic pregnancy in a rudimentary uterine horn (cornual/rudimentary horn ectopic). This site is listed last in the classification of ectopic sites. What makes a rudimentary horn ectopic pregnancy particularly dangerous?
During bimanual examination of a non-pregnant woman, a bulky uterus smaller than 12 weeks' size with no adnexal mass and no tenderness is MOST likely due to:
questions.explanation: A bulky, non-tender uterus smaller than 12 weeks in a non-pregnant woman without adnexal pathology classically suggests uterine fibroids (leiomyomata) or adenomyosis. Fibroids produce irregular enlargement while adenomyosis produces a uniformly enlarged tender uterus. Ectopic pregnancy and mole require pregnancy as a prerequisite.

Twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome occurs specifically in monochorionic twin pregnancies due to unbalanced blood flow through shared placental vascular connections, causing one twin (the donor) to become growth restricted with oliguria and oligohydramnios, while the other (the recipient) develops polyhydramnios and can develop cardiac strain from volume overload. This complication is unique to monochorionic pregnancies and requires specialist fetal medicine input, sometimes including laser ablation of the shared vessels. Early identification of chorionicity on ultrasound is therefore critical in twin pregnancy management.
questions.question: A woman with twin pregnancy develops polyhydramnios and is found to have a monochorionic diamniotic placentation with significant size discordance between the twins. Which specific complication of monochorionic twin pregnancy should be excluded?
Danazol has been used for endometriosis treatment. Its mechanism involves creating a 'pseudomenopause.' Which best describes the hormonal profile created by danazol?
options: Low oestrogen, low androgens, elevated FSH
High oestrogen, high progesterone, low androgens
High androgens, low oestrogen, low gonadotropins
Elevated prolactin suppressing LH and FSH
questions.explanation: Danazol is an androgen derivative that suppresses the hypothalamic-pituitary axis (reducing LH and FSH), inhibits multiple steroidogenic enzymes, and has direct androgenic and antiprogestin effects — creating a high-androgen, low-oestrogen state (pseudomenopause/pseudoatrophy) that causes regression of endometriotic implants. Its androgenic side effects (weight gain, acne, voice deepening, irreversible virilization) limit its use compared to GnRH analogues.

Bullous oedema of the bladder mucosa on cystoscopy indicates direct tumour extension to the bladder, corresponding to FIGO stage IVA disease, which involves spread to adjacent pelvic organs. This finding significantly changes management toward palliative or combined modality treatment rather than radical surgery. It reflects locally advanced, difficult-to-cure disease.
questions.question: A patient with cervical carcinoma undergoes cystoscopy which reveals bullous oedema of the bladder mucosa. What FIGO stage does this finding most strongly suggest?

questions.explanation: Using sentinel lymph node biopsy rather than complete inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy in appropriately selected early-stage, unifocal vulval cancers significantly reduces the incidence of chronic lower limb lymphoedema while maintaining accurate nodal staging.
questions.question: Postoperative lymphoedema following inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy for vulval cancer is MOST effectively minimised by which surgical strategy?
options: Routine bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy for all stages
Wide radical vulvectomy alone without nodal assessment
Sentinel lymph node biopsy in appropriately selected cases
Delayed lymph node dissection performed months later

questions.explanation: Both electrocautery and electrodiathermy destroy tissue by heat and require regional or general anaesthesia. Electrocautery achieves a depth of destruction of 2-3 mm, while electrodiathermy can destroy up to 1.5 cm depth. Complications for both include excessive bleeding, cervical stenosis, and acute pelvic infection. Laser therapy achieves 5-7 mm depth without requiring anaesthesia.
questions.question: Electrocautery for CIN differs from electrodiathermy in that electrocautery has a depth of destruction of approximately:
Which of the following constitutes 50 to 85 percent of resting anal tone?
questions.explanation: The internal anal sphincter, an extension of the circular muscle layer of the rectum, maintains constant maximal contraction and contributes 50 to 85% of resting anal tone. It has autonomic innervation from the parasympathetic (S2-4) and sympathetic (thoracolumbar ganglia). Both divisions are thought to cause inhibition of contraction.

questions.question: The most common presenting symptom of endometrial carcinoma is:
questions.explanation: Postmenopausal bleeding or a blood-stained postmenopausal discharge is the most common presenting symptom of endometrial carcinoma, occurring in approximately 75% of cases. All postmenopausal bleeding must be investigated, as a significant proportion will have an underlying endometrial malignancy.

questions.question: Submucosal fibroids are MOST strongly associated with which clinical presentation compared with other fibroid locations?
questions.explanation: Submucosal fibroids distort the endometrial cavity, leading to heavy menstrual bleeding and impaired implantation, making them the fibroid location most strongly linked with menorrhagia and infertility. Subserosal fibroids more often cause pressure symptoms rather than bleeding.

questions.question: Uterine fibroids (leiomyomas) can cause infertility depending on their location. Which type of fibroid MOST directly impairs fertility?
questions.explanation: Submucous fibroids are most directly implicated in infertility because they protrude into the uterine cavity, distorting implantation sites and mechanically blocking the uterine ostia (fallopian tube openings). Their presence impairs both sperm transport and implantation. Subserosal and most intramural fibroids (without cavity distortion) have minimal impact on fertility, but all require evaluation in the infertility workup.
options: Subserosal fibroid on the posterior uterine wall

questions.question: Premature (early) ejaculation is defined primarily by which feature?
options: Retrograde flow of semen into the bladder
Persistent ejaculation occurring sooner than desired with minimal stimulation
Complete inability to achieve any ejaculation
questions.explanation: Premature ejaculation is characterised by persistent or recurrent ejaculation occurring with minimal sexual stimulation sooner than the man wishes, causing distress, and is distinguished from delayed ejaculation and retrograde ejaculation, which involve different underlying mechanisms.

FIGO Stage III ovarian cancer involves one or both ovaries with peritoneal implants beyond the pelvis and/or positive retroperitoneal or inguinal lymph nodes. Stage I is confined to ovaries; Stage II involves the pelvis; and Stage IV indicates distant organ metastasis.
questions.question: In FIGO staging of ovarian cancer, Stage III disease is defined as:
options: Tumour with extrapelvic implants or retroperitoneal nodes
Tumour confined to one or both ovaries
Tumour involving ovaries and pelvis only
Tumour confined to the ovarian capsule

questions.explanation: Heavy smoking, defined as more than 15 cigarettes daily, in women aged 35 or older is a UK Medical Eligibility Criteria category 4 contraindication to combined oral contraceptives due to markedly increased risk of arterial thrombosis and myocardial infarction. A normal BMI, controlled hypothyroidism, and resolved gestational diabetes do not carry comparable absolute contraindication status. Recognising this age-and-dose-dependent smoking risk is essential in contraceptive counselling.
options: Family history of migraine without aura
Body mass index of 24 with no other risks
Smoking more than 15 cigarettes daily after age 35
questions.question: A 35-year-old smoker requests combined oral contraceptive pills. Which additional risk factor would MOST strongly contraindicate this method due to cardiovascular risk?

questions.explanation: The ischiococcygeus (coccygeus muscle) arises from the tip of the ischial spine close to the origin of obturator internus and inserts into the coccyx and lower part of the sacrum. It forms the posterior part of the pelvic diaphragm. The iliococcygeus, in contrast, attaches to the posterior half of the arcus tendinous.
questions.question: Which levator ani component arises from the tip of the ischial spine and inserts into the coccyx and lower sacrum?

questions.explanation: The management sequence for emergency DUB is: (1) Admit and resuscitate (blood transfusion if haemodynamically compromised); (2) IV conjugated equine oestrogen 25 mg every 4 hours for up to 24 hours until bleeding controlled; (3) Norethisterone tablets orally to stabilise the endometrium; (4) Follow-up with combined oral contraceptive pills for 6 months to prevent recurrence and regulate cycles. D&C is reserved for cases where medical management fails or pathology is suspected.
questions.question: The management protocol for emergency DUB requiring intravenous treatment includes, in CORRECT sequence:
options: IV oestrogen ? IV progestin ? oral progestin ? combined pill for 6 months
Immediate D&C ? IV oestrogen ? oral combined pill
IV oestrogen (25 mg 4-hourly) ? oral norethisterone ? combined pill ×6 months
Blood transfusion alone ? oral oestrogen ? D&C if no response

questions.question: The MOST time-critical advice for a woman whose partner's condom breaks during intercourse is to consider:
questions.explanation: A condom breaking during intercourse creates a risk of unprotected exposure similar to no contraception being used at all, so prompt consideration of emergency contraception, ideally as soon as possible, is the most time-critical advice to reduce the risk of unintended pregnancy.
options: Taking a pregnancy test immediately after intercourse
Waiting until her next period to assess pregnancy risk
Emergency contraception as soon as possible

questions.question: Which generation of progestogen used in combined oral contraceptives is associated with the highest relative risk of venous thromboembolism?
options: All generations carry an identical risk
Second generation progestogens such as levonorgestrel
Third and fourth generation progestogens such as desogestrel and drospirenone
Progestogen generation has no bearing on thrombosis risk
questions.explanation: Newer third and fourth generation progestogens, including desogestrel, gestodene, and drospirenone, have been associated with a higher relative risk of venous thromboembolism compared with second generation progestogens such as levonorgestrel, an important consideration in individualised prescribing.

Salpingitis causes ectopic pregnancy not necessarily by complete occlusion, but by destroying tubal cilia or causing kinking and stricture that impairs the transport of the fertilized ovum. The fertilized ovum is delayed in transit, allowing trophoblastic development and implantation within the tube before reaching the uterine cavity. This mechanism explains why mild salpingitis, even without complete tubal closure, can cause ectopic pregnancy.
questions.question: Salpingitis is listed as the COMMONEST cause of ectopic pregnancy. Its mechanism involves:

questions.explanation: Spermicides alone have a typical-use failure rate of 18–29%, making them among the least effective reversible contraceptive methods. Critically, high-frequency N-9 use has been shown to cause vaginal epithelial disruption and mucosal inflammation, which may actually increase HIV transmission risk. N-9 is not recommended as STI prophylaxis and should only be used as an adjunct to barrier methods.
options: Highly effective, with a perfect-use failure rate under 1%
Moderately effective and also protective against HIV transmission
Effective only when used with an intrauterine device
Relatively ineffective (18–29% typical-use failure rate) and not protective against HIV
Effective substitutes for barrier methods in women who cannot tolerate latex
questions.question: Spermicides containing nonoxynol-9 (N-9) used ALONE as contraception are best described as:

questions.explanation: Alfred Kinsey (1948) developed the Kinsey Scale to represent sexual orientation on a continuum from 0 (exclusively heterosexual) to 6 (exclusively homosexual), with 3 representing equal bisexuality. It challenged binary conceptions of sexual orientation by demonstrating gradations of homosexual and heterosexual attraction. It does not measure dysfunction or satisfaction.
