questions.explanation: The progestogen challenge test differentiates outflow tract obstruction (no withdrawal bleed despite progesterone — outflow obstruction) from anovulation without obstruction (withdrawal bleed occurs — confirming intact outflow tract and oestrogen primed endometrium). Serum FSH/LH distinguish ovarian from hypothalamic-pituitary causes. The progestogen challenge is the first-line functional test in amenorrhoea evaluation to establish whether the endometrium and outflow tract are intact.

questions.question: Syphilis serology in pregnancy: a woman tests VDRL positive (titre 1:32). The MOST appropriate management is:
questions.explanation: A reactive VDRL in pregnancy requires confirmatory treponemal testing (TPHA, FTA-ABS) to exclude biological false positives. Once confirmed, treatment with benzathine penicillin G is mandatory — stage-appropriate dosing (single dose 2.4MU IM for primary/secondary; 3 doses weekly for late latent/unknown duration). Penicillin is the only antibiotic proven to prevent congenital syphilis. Azithromycin is not recommended in pregnancy due to resistance and inadequate evidence for MTCT prevention.
options: Repeat VDRL in 4 weeks as titres must be confirmed twice before treatment
Perform confirmatory TPHA/FTA-ABS test, treat with benzathine penicillin G based on stage of syphilis, treat sexual partner
Treat only if she develops clinical signs of secondary syphilis
Await neonatal testing at delivery before deciding whether to treat the mother
Administer azithromycin 2g orally as single-dose treatment in pregnancy

questions.question: Polycystic ovarian disease (PCOD) is the most common cause of which menstrual abnormality in clinical practice?
questions.explanation: PCOD is the most common cause of oligomenorrhoea and secondary amenorrhoea in women of reproductive age, due to chronic anovulation from disrupted LH:FSH ratio and elevated androgens. Elevated LH causes excessive theca cell androgen production while suppressed FSH prevents follicular maturation. The resulting anovulation and progesterone deficiency allows oestrogen to act unopposed, predisposing to endometrial hyperplasia with chronic amenorrhoea.

In luteinized unruptured follicle syndrome, the follicle undergoes the hormonal changes of luteinization typical of ovulation, but the oocyte is never actually released from the follicle, resulting in a cycle that appears ovulatory on hormonal testing but is functionally infertile. This condition can be difficult to diagnose without direct visualisation, such as serial ultrasound tracking of follicle collapse. It is a recognised but underappreciated cause of unexplained infertility.
questions.question: A woman is found to have a luteinized unruptured follicle (LUF) syndrome during infertility investigation. What is the fundamental defect in this condition?
options: The ovary produces no follicles at all
The corpus luteum fails to form after normal ovulation
The oocyte is released but immediately degenerates
The follicle ruptures too early before the oocyte matures
The follicle luteinizes without releasing the oocyte at ovulation

questions.explanation: The SRY (Sex-determining Region of the Y chromosome) gene is located on the short arm of the Y chromosome. It encodes testicular determining factor (TDF), which directs the indifferent gonad to differentiate into a testis. Absence of the SRY gene or its product results in ovarian development by default. Mutations in SRY cause XY gonadal agenesis with female phenotype.
questions.question: The SRY gene, responsible for testicular determination, is located on the:
options: Long arm of the Y chromosome
Short arm of the Y chromosome

questions.question: A woman with endometriosis-related infertility has patent tubes and a normal partner semen analysis. Which first-line treatment MOST directly improves her chance of natural conception?
questions.explanation: Laparoscopic excision or ablation of endometriotic lesions improves natural fertility rates in women with mild to moderate disease and otherwise normal fertility parameters, by restoring normal pelvic anatomy and reducing inflammatory factors. Hormonal suppressive therapies such as GnRH agonists or the contraceptive pill control pain but suppress ovulation, making them unsuitable for women actively trying to conceive. Danazol carries significant androgenic side effects and is rarely first-line.
options: Danazol therapy for six months duration

questions.question: A woman with confirmed chlamydia infection completes treatment with doxycycline. What is the MOST appropriate advice regarding resuming sexual intercourse to prevent reinfection of her partner?
options: Abstain until both partners complete treatment
Resume intercourse immediately after her first dose
No abstinence period is necessary at all
Abstain only until her own symptoms resolve
Resume intercourse once her symptoms resolve
questions.explanation: To prevent reinfection and ongoing transmission, both partners should complete treatment and abstain from intercourse until treatment is finished, typically around seven days after single-dose regimens or completion of a full course, rather than basing the decision solely on symptom resolution, since chlamydia is frequently asymptomatic. This mutual completion approach reduces the ping-pong reinfection pattern commonly seen when only one partner is treated. Test of cure is not routinely needed except in pregnancy or persistent symptoms.

Assessment of fetal maturity using cytology involves taking an amniotic fluid sample at 36 weeks and staining with Nile Blue Sulphate. Fetal squames appear brick red because Nile Blue Sulphate stains glycogen and fat collection in cells, which are stored in fetuses at 36 weeks gestation. This technique provides a cytological marker of pulmonary and overall fetal maturity.
questions.question: Which staining technique is used to detect fetal squames in amniotic fluid to assess fetal maturity, and what do they appear as?

options: How many times do you pass urine during the day?
Do you wet yourself when you cough or sneeze?
Do you wake at night to pass urine?
Do you have difficulty starting to pass urine?
Sudden urge preventing toilet access in time
questions.explanation: The clinical assessment tool asks: (1) 'How many times during the last week did you accidentally leak urine with a physical activity like coughing, sneezing, lifting, or exercising?' (assessing SUI), and (2) 'A feeling of strong, sudden need to pass your urine that did not allow you to get to the toilet fast enough?' (assessing urgency incontinence/detrusor instability). These standardised questions differentiate stress from urge incontinence clinically before urodynamic investigation.
questions.question: The FUN mnemonic symptoms of detrusor instability can also be assessed by asking the patient specific questions. Which question specifically addresses urgency incontinence?

A woman with a chronically overdistended bladder from long-standing outflow obstruction develops rising serum creatinine. Which mechanism links her lower urinary tract dysfunction to this renal impairment?
questions.explanation: Chronic bladder overdistension from unrelieved outflow obstruction raises intravesical pressure, which is transmitted retrogradely through the ureters to the renal pelvis, causing hydronephrosis and progressive renal impairment if untreated. This back-pressure effect explains the rising creatinine seen in chronic urinary retention. Timely bladder decompression and relief of obstruction can prevent permanent renal damage.
options: Back-pressure on kidneys from bladder overdistension
Renal artery stenosis from pelvic congestion
Direct bacterial invasion of the renal parenchyma
Autoimmune glomerulonephritis triggered by bladder distension

questions.question: A woman living with HIV who is not yet on antiretroviral therapy requests an IUD. She should be counselled that:
questions.explanation: Clinical wellness rather than antiretroviral therapy status determines IUD suitability, so a woman living with HIV who is otherwise clinically well can be offered an IUD even before starting antiretroviral therapy, while she is also encouraged to begin treatment as part of her overall care.
options: The IUD remains an appropriate option if she is otherwise clinically well
The IUD is contraindicated until her viral load is undetectable
Only barrier methods are appropriate until treatment begins
She must start antiretroviral therapy before any IUD can be considered
The IUD would accelerate her progression to AIDS
It cannot distinguish between benign and malignant endometrium during the procedure
Obliterated cavity segments may allow undetected endometrial carcinoma
It always requires general anaesthesia and ICU admission
It causes immediate menopause in all women treated
questions.explanation: A critical safety concern with endometrial ablation is that if the procedure is incomplete (not all endometrium destroyed), isolated islands of residual endometrium can be sealed off behind scar tissue in the uterine cavity. This residual endometrium — no longer accessible to sampling — can progress to carcinoma while the patient appears amenorrhoeic. This is why ablation is not performed when hyperplasia or malignancy is present, and why hysterectomy remains the definitive treatment when pathology is a concern.
questions.question: The SURGICAL treatment of DUB by endometrial ablation using a urological resectoscope is associated with which specific safety concern?

questions.explanation: In-utero exposure to diethylstilboestrol (DES), a synthetic oestrogen once used to prevent miscarriage, is classically linked to clear cell adenocarcinoma of the vagina and cervix in daughters exposed during fetal development. This association led to discontinuation of DES use in pregnancy. Affected women require lifelong close gynaecological surveillance.
questions.question: A young woman is diagnosed with clear cell adenocarcinoma of the vagina and cervix. Her mother reports having taken a specific medication during pregnancy decades earlier. Which in-utero exposure is classically associated with this tumour?
A blighted ovum is described as an empty gestational sac without an identifiable embryo on ultrasound at 8 weeks. This is technically classified under which broader abortion category?
questions.explanation: A blighted ovum (anembryonic pregnancy) is a form of missed abortion occurring very early in the first trimester, where the trophoblast implants and develops but embryonic development ceases extremely early, leaving an empty gestational sac. The dead product of conception is retained behind a closed cervical os without expulsion, fulfilling the definition of missed abortion. It accounts for approximately 50% of first-trimester losses.

questions.question: A 28-year-old woman is found to have CIN I on a routine Pap smear. What is the most appropriate initial management approach given the high rate of spontaneous regression of low-grade lesions?
questions.explanation: CIN I has a high rate of spontaneous regression, particularly in young women, so conservative management with repeat cytology and colposcopic surveillance is generally preferred over immediate ablative or excisional treatment. This avoids overtreatment of lesions likely to resolve on their own. Treatment is reserved for persistent or progressive disease on follow-up.

Puberty is triggered by reactivation of pulsatile GnRH secretion from the hypothalamus after a quiescent childhood period, which stimulates pituitary gonadotrophins and subsequent ovarian oestrogen production driving thelarche. Adrenarche, the rise in adrenal androgens, contributes to pubic and axillary hair but is a separate process. Growth hormone and prolactin are not the primary triggers of pubertal onset.
options: A sudden surge in adrenal androgens
questions.question: A 9-year-old girl develops breast budding as her first pubertal sign. Which hormonal event MOST directly initiates this earliest stage of puberty?

questions.explanation: Pelvic exenteration involves ultraradical surgery with anterior exenteration (removing bladder, uterus, and vagina), posterior exenteration (removing uterus, vagina, and rectum), and total exenteration (removing all three - bladder, uterus/vagina, and rectum). Both urinary diversion and fecal diversion are required for total exenteration. It is reserved for recurrent or centrally located advanced disease.
questions.question: Pelvic exenteration (ultraradical surgery) for cervical carcinoma may be anterior, posterior, or total. What distinguishes total from anterior exenteration?
options: Total exenteration does not include urinary diversion
Total exenteration includes removal of pelvic lymph nodes only
Total exenteration is indicated only for stage I disease
Total exenteration removes bladder, uterus, vagina

questions.explanation: Some high-risk women (BRCA1/2 carriers) opt for prophylactic oophorectomy with HRT around 40 years of age, after completing their family. This strategy dramatically reduces ovarian cancer risk but requires concurrent HRT to prevent premature surgical menopause complications.
questions.question: Prophylactic oophorectomy in high-risk BRCA mutation carriers is typically recommended at approximately what age?

questions.explanation: Bartholin gland carcinoma, while rare, most commonly arises as adenocarcinoma (reflecting the glandular origin of the Bartholin gland) or squamous cell carcinoma. Transitional cell carcinoma of Bartholin gland origin also occurs. Any Bartholin gland 'cyst' in a postmenopausal woman requires excision and histological examination to exclude carcinoma.
questions.question: Bartholin gland carcinoma most commonly arises as which histological type?

questions.explanation: Lichen simplex chronicus results from chronic scratching and rubbing, producing thickened, leathery (lichenified), intensely pruritic skin. The itch-scratch-itch cycle perpetuates the condition. Unlike lichen sclerosus, which produces thin, fragile skin, lichen simplex chronicus causes epidermal thickening and increased skin markings (lichenification).
questions.question: Lichen simplex chronicus of the vulva (formerly hyperplastic dystrophy) presents MOST commonly with:
A 15-year-old has normal breast and pubic hair development but primary amenorrhoea, cyclical pelvic pain, and a bulging bluish membrane at the introitus. What is the MOST likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Cyclical pain with normal secondary sexual characteristics indicates a functioning uterus and ovaries obstructed by an imperforate hymen, causing menstrual blood to accumulate as haematocolpos, visible as a bulging bluish membrane. Mullerian agenesis and androgen insensitivity both present without a uterus and without cyclical pain. A higher transverse septum would not typically produce a visible introital bulge.

options: Neither is repaired until one year has passed
The urinary fistula only, leaving the rectal fistula untreated permanently
The vesico-vaginal fistula, regardless of contamination risk
The recto-vaginal fistula, to reduce faecal contamination before urinary tract repair
questions.question: A patient has coexisting vesico-vaginal and recto-vaginal fistulae following obstructed labour. In planning staged repair, which fistula is generally addressed first?
questions.explanation: When both fistulae coexist, the recto-vaginal fistula is generally repaired first, since ongoing faecal contamination increases infection risk and can jeopardise the success of a subsequent urinary tract repair. This staged approach improves overall surgical outcomes. Adequate healing time is allowed between the two procedures.

questions.question: A 22-year-old woman with a rapidly growing pelvic mass, elevated LDH, and elevated AFP is MOST likely to have:
questions.explanation: A young woman with a rapidly growing pelvic mass, elevated LDH (produced by ovarian germ cell tumours), and elevated AFP (specific for yolk sac elements) most likely has a mixed germ cell tumour. These tumours arise in young women, grow rapidly, and may contain multiple germ cell elements.

Endometriomas are commonly called chocolate cysts because they contain thick, dark, altered blood resulting from cyclical bleeding of ectopic endometrial tissue within the ovary, giving the cyst contents a characteristic chocolate-brown appearance at surgery.
questions.question: Endometriomas are frequently referred to by which descriptive term reflecting their gross appearance?

questions.explanation: During pelvic examination for incontinence assessment, voluntary pelvic floor contraction is assessed by asking the patient to squeeze the pelvic floor muscles while the examiner's fingers are in the vagina. The strength and voluntary control of levator muscles is determined by palpation. This Oxford scale grading (0-5) guides the need for physiotherapy and biofeedback and helps predict response to conservative therapy.
questions.question: Assessment of voluntary pelvic floor contraction during pelvic examination for incontinence uses which grading approach?
options: Electromyography of the external sphincter only
Measurement of intra-abdominal pressure during Valsalva
Pad weight during a standardised exercise protocol
GP care and palliative services only
questions.question: The Calman and Hine cancer care model (UK 1995) proposed a cancer care pathway of:
questions.explanation: The Calman and Hine model (1995) established a three-tier cancer care framework: Primary Care (GP level), Cancer Units (at district general hospitals managing common cancers), and Cancer Centres (providing specialist services for rare or complex cancers). This framework has shaped modern oncological service delivery.

questions.question: The conjoined longitudinal muscle of the anal canal is an extension of which muscular layer of the rectum?
questions.explanation: The conjoined longitudinal muscle is an extension of the longitudinal muscle layer of the rectum, supplemented by levator ani muscle fibres. Its function is structural support and anchoring of the anorectum to the pelvis. It is distinct from the internal anal sphincter, which is an extension of the circular muscle layer.

questions.question: Malignant change in a mature dermoid cyst most commonly involves transformation to:
questions.explanation: True malignant change in a mature dermoid cyst most commonly involves squamous cell carcinoma developing from the squamous epithelium lining the cyst, typically occurring in women over 40 years of age. This occurs in approximately 2% of dermoid cysts.

options: Restriction of disease to the endometrial cavity only
Penetration of molar villi into the myometrium
Presence of a coexisting normal fetus
questions.explanation: Invasive mole is characterised by penetration of hydropic villi and trophoblast into the myometrium or its vasculature, distinguishing it from a complete mole confined to the uterine cavity, though both share similar villous histology.
questions.question: Invasive mole differs from complete hydatidiform mole primarily by demonstrating:

options: Successful complete abortion requiring no further action
questions.question: A woman undergoes induced abortion at 8 weeks using intravaginal misoprostol. Two days later she presents with ongoing heavy bleeding and passage of tissue with an open cervical os. What is the most likely diagnosis requiring management at this point?
questions.explanation: Ongoing heavy bleeding with an open cervical os and passage of tissue after misoprostol use for induced abortion suggests incomplete abortion, where retained products of conception require surgical or further medical evacuation to prevent haemorrhage or infection. Clinical examination and ultrasound help confirm retained tissue. This is a recognised outcome of medical abortion requiring follow-up care.

questions.question: A 15-year-old girl in a rural Nigerian community is pregnant. Her care provider documents several medical risk factors. Which of the following is NOT a recognized medical complication of adolescent pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Polycystic ovarian disease (PCOD) is a chronic endocrine disorder unrelated to adolescent pregnancy and is not a direct complication of teenage gestation. Recognized complications include anaemia, pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, cephalopelvic disproportion, obstetric fistulae, peripheral nerve injury, and poor breastfeeding. PCOD is a hormonal condition typically diagnosed in the reproductive years independent of pregnancy.

options: Colpotomy and drainage via posterior fornix
Laparoscopic peritoneal lavage without organ removal
questions.question: An ultrasound-guided drainage of a tubo-ovarian abscess (TOA) is performed as an adjunct to antibiotics. If drainage is inadequate, which surgical procedure is the DEFINITIVE treatment for a ruptured TOA?
questions.explanation: A ruptured tubo-ovarian abscess is a surgical emergency with septic peritonitis requiring immediate laparotomy, peritoneal lavage, and in most cases total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (TAH+BSO) to achieve source control. Conservative surgery (preserving the uterus and one ovary) may be attempted in younger women with mild disease who have not ruptured, but ruptured TOA demands definitive removal of all infected tissue. Mortality without surgery approaches 5–10%.

Choriocarcinoma is characterised histologically as a purely epithelial tumour with NO chorionic villi—distinguishing it critically from hydatidiform mole and invasive mole. It consists of sheets of anaplastic syncytiotrophoblast and cytotrophoblast with extensive necrosis and haemorrhage.
options: Presence of chorionic villi with trophoblastic proliferation
Presence of fetal vessels in stroma
Purely epithelial tumour with no chorionic villi
questions.question: The histological hallmark of choriocarcinoma is:

questions.explanation: In advanced ovarian cancer, supraclavicular lymph nodes may become enlarged due to remote (distant) metastases. The majority of patients with ovarian cancer present with advanced disease; therefore, thorough lymph node examination including supraclavicular nodes is part of the clinical assessment.
questions.question: A palpable supraclavicular lymph node in a woman with known ovarian cancer indicates:

options: Vasoconstriction and platelet aggregation — limiting blood loss
Stimulation of fibrinolysis and clot dissolution
Vasodilation and platelet aggregation inhibition (promotes blood loss)
Stimulation of FSH from the pituitary
Direct inhibition of spiral arteriole vasoconstriction
questions.explanation: Prostacyclin (PGI2) is a potent vasodilator and inhibitor of platelet aggregation — effectively the functional opposite of thromboxane A2 (TxA2). Excessive PGI2 in the endometrium of women with menorrhagia promotes vasodilation and prevents platelet plug formation, increasing blood loss. NSAIDs reduce PGI2 production along with other prostaglandins, and the net effect on the TxA2:PGI2 balance is a reduction in blood loss of up to 50%.
questions.question: PGI2 (prostacyclin) has which specific roles relevant to DUB?

options: Continue smoking unchanged since it has no effect
Increase smoking briefly to reduce anxiety before surgery
Delay smoking cessation until well after recovery
Stop smoking as early as possible before surgery
Switch to smoking only on the morning of surgery
questions.explanation: Smoking cessation before elective surgery reduces the risk of respiratory complications, impaired wound healing, and cardiovascular events perioperatively, so patients are strongly encouraged to stop smoking as early as possible before their scheduled procedure to gain maximal benefit.
questions.question: A woman scheduled for elective gynaecological cancer surgery who is a current smoker should MOST appropriately be advised to:
Which generation of progestogen in combined oral contraceptives is associated with the HIGHEST venous thromboembolism risk?
questions.explanation: Third-generation progestogens (desogestrel, gestodene) and fourth-generation (drospirenone) carry approximately 1.5–2 times higher VTE risk compared to second-generation levonorgestrel, despite having lower androgenic activity and fewer androgenic side effects. Less androgenic progestogens fail to counteract estrogen's procoagulant effect on protein S. Levonorgestrel-containing COC are therefore recommended as first-line where VTE risk is a concern.
options: All generations carry identical VTE risk
Third generation (desogestrel, gestodene) and fourth generation (drospirenone)
Natural progesterone-based formulations carry higher VTE risk than synthetic progestogens

questions.question: The SCCA marker is a sub-fraction of which glycoprotein?
questions.explanation: SCCA is a sub-fraction of the glycoprotein TA-4, which can be demonstrated by immunohistochemical methods. It is produced mainly by squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix, vagina, and vulva, and is used as a marker for monitoring squamous and adenosquamous carcinomas. Elevated levels correlate with disease stage and metastatic burden.

Presacral neurectomy (division of the superior hypogastric plexus) interrupts the central uterine pain pathway, specifically targeting central dysmenorrhoea originating from the uterus. It is effective for midline uterine pain but does not relieve lateral pelvic pain (which travels via different neural pathways) or pain from specific organ infiltration. It is performed alongside conservative surgical endometriosis treatment in carefully selected patients with severe dysmenorrhoea.
options: Lateral pelvic pain from sciatic nerve endometriosis
questions.question: A woman with stage III endometriosis undergoes laparoscopic treatment. In addition to removing visible implants, her surgeon performs a presacral neurectomy. What symptom does this procedure specifically target?

questions.explanation: Traditional progestogen-only pills act mainly by thickening cervical mucus to impede sperm penetration, an effect that diminishes if the dose is delayed beyond the 3-hour window, unlike desogestrel-containing pills, which have a longer window because they more reliably suppress ovulation.
options: Systemic oestrogen levels in the bloodstream
Endometrial thickness alone, without mucus effect
Cervical mucus thickening, which fades if delayed
Ovulation suppression, occurring as with combined pills
questions.question: A woman using the progestogen-only pill must take it within the same 3-hour window each day primarily because of its effect on:
A postmenopausal woman with osteoporosis cannot tolerate hormone replacement therapy. Which alternative agent MOST specifically reduces vertebral fracture risk by inhibiting osteoclast activity?
questions.explanation: Bisphosphonates inhibit osteoclast-mediated bone resorption, effectively reducing vertebral and hip fracture risk in postmenopausal osteoporosis, making them a standard alternative when hormone therapy is contraindicated or not preferred. Calcium and vitamin D are important adjuncts but are insufficient alone to substantially reduce fracture risk in established osteoporosis. SSRIs and NSAIDs have no established role in bone density preservation.

questions.question: Which fixative is used for smear preparation in the Papanicolaou method?
questions.explanation: In the Papanicolaou method, after spreading cells on a slide, the smear must be fixed immediately using absolute ethyl alcohol and diethyl ether as the fixative. Fixation prevents cellular distortion and preserves nuclear detail essential for cytological interpretation. The slide should be ground at one end for identification and every cell must be examined completely.

questions.question: CA 19-9 as a tumour marker is mainly expressed by which type of ovarian tumour?
questions.explanation: CA 19-9 (carbohydrate determinant 19-9) is mainly expressed by colonic cancer and also by most mucinous ovarian tumours. It can also be expressed by serous and other non-mucinous ovarian tumours and is used in combination with CA-125 for clinical monitoring of ovarian cancer treatment response.

Combined oral contraceptives increase hepatic sex hormone binding globulin production, which binds free testosterone and reduces its bioavailable fraction, while also suppressing ovarian androgen production, making it effective for both hirsutism management and contraception. Metformin improves insulin sensitivity but has a more modest, indirect effect on androgen levels. Ovulation induction agents such as letrozole and clomiphene are inappropriate when pregnancy is not currently desired.
questions.question: A 24-year-old with PCOS wishes to manage her hirsutism without immediate fertility concerns. Which treatment MOST directly reduces circulating free androgen levels while also providing contraception?

options: Systemic testosterone therapy as first-line treatment
questions.explanation: Vaginal atrophy causing dryness and dyspareunia in postmenopausal women is effectively treated with local vaginal oestrogen or non-hormonal lubricants and moisturisers as first-line management, addressing the physical cause of pain before considering systemic hormonal or psychological interventions for desire.
questions.question: A 58-year-old postmenopausal woman reports reduced sexual desire and vaginal dryness causing painful intercourse. The MOST appropriate initial management addressing the physical symptom is:

questions.explanation: Primary amenorrhoea is defined as absence of menstruation by age 16 when secondary sexual characteristics are present, OR by age 14 in the ABSENCE of secondary sexual characteristics. The different thresholds reflect that pubertal development should have occurred by 14 years; if it has not, investigation should not wait until 16. Both definitions require thorough investigation for organic causes.
questions.question: Primary amenorrhoea is defined as absence of menstruation by a specific age when secondary sexual characteristics ARE present. What is this age threshold?
A 55-year-old postmenopausal woman has a 7 cm simple unilateral cyst on ultrasound with CA-125 of 20 u/ml and normal vascular resistance. The MOST appropriate management is:
questions.explanation: Simple unilateral cysts less than 6 cm in diameter with CA-125 below 35 u/ml and normal vascular resistance patterns are likely benign and may be safely managed conservatively in postmenopausal women with regular follow-up. However, this 7 cm cyst warrants close monitoring and possible intervention.

questions.question: A fibroid pregnancy requires careful management due to specific complications. Which complication is MOST common in pregnancy complicated by uterine fibroids?
questions.explanation: Red (carneous) degeneration is the most common acute complication of fibroids in pregnancy, caused by rapid growth under progesterone stimulation leading to central ischaemic necrosis with haemorrhage into the fibroid. It presents with acute severe localized uterine tenderness in the second trimester. Management is conservative with analgesics and hydration; surgery during pregnancy carries high fetal loss risk.
options: Spontaneous uterine rupture from fibroid growth
Fetal macrosomia from fibroid-related growth factors

questions.explanation: The examining physician in an alleged rape case has a duty to document all findings accurately, collect forensic specimens according to established protocol, and provide emergency care including STI prophylaxis and emergency contraception. The documentation serves as medico-legal evidence. Police notification is the patient's right, not the physician's unilateral duty without consent in most jurisdictions.
questions.question: A woman who was raped presents to the gynaecology clinic. Which of the following represents a medico-legal duty of the examining physician?
options: Immediately inform the police without patient consent
Refuse examination without law enforcement present
Document findings and obtain specimens per protocol
Refer to psychiatry before any examination

questions.question: A postoperative patient develops fever, wound erythema, purulent discharge, and elevated CRP on day 5 after a TAH. The MOST appropriate management is:
questions.explanation: Postoperative wound infection presenting on day 5 with fever, erythema, and purulent discharge requires wound swab for culture and sensitivity, initiation of broad-spectrum antibiotics covering gram-negative organisms and anaerobes, and wound opening/drainage if a collection or abscess is present. Most wound infections can be managed without return to theatre.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST common cause of primary amenorrhoea in the world?
questions.explanation: Turner's syndrome (45,XO) is the most common cause of primary amenorrhoea, with an incidence of 1 in 2000 live born girls. It causes hypergonadotrophic hypogonadism (elevated FSH/LH) because streak gonads produce no oestrogen and the hypothalamic-pituitary axis is uninhibited. MRKH is the second most common cause. The distinction between the two is made by karyotype: XO vs. XX with absent uterus.

options: A viral infection of sebaceous glands
A benign vulval cyst from Bartholin glands
questions.question: Hidradenitis suppurativa of the vulva is BEST classified as:
questions.explanation: Hidradenitis suppurativa is a chronic, recurring inflammatory disease of the apocrine sweat glands that affects the vulva, groins, axillae, and perianal region. It presents with painful nodules, abscesses, and sinus tracts. It is not a malignant condition but can be debilitating and may rarely develop into squamous cell carcinoma in chronic severe cases.

questions.question: During HSG performed for infertility investigation, free spillage of dye from both tubes is seen. A filling defect is noted in the uterine cavity. Which pathology is MOST likely responsible for this filling defect?
questions.explanation: Filling defects in the uterine cavity on HSG are most commonly caused by submucous fibroids, polyps, or intrauterine adhesions (Asherman's syndrome). These intracavitary lesions prevent normal implantation and are important uterine factor causes of infertility. A club-shaped dilated appearance suggests hydrosalpinges, while loculated spill indicates peritubal adhesions.

options: It cannot be used simultaneously with any lubricant
It is less effective than spermicide used alone
It provides no protection against sexually transmitted infections
It has a substantially lower failure rate than the male condom
It can be inserted in advance of sexual activity, offering greater user control
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the female condom compared with the male condom is MOST accurate?
questions.explanation: The female condom can be inserted up to several hours before intercourse, giving the female partner greater control over its use compared with the male condom, which must be applied immediately before penetration, though its overall failure rate is broadly comparable to or slightly higher than the male condom.

questions.question: A woman describes leakage of urine when she bends down or rises from a chair, associated with a slow stream and sensation of incomplete emptying. Which type of incontinence is this?
questions.explanation: Overflow incontinence symptoms include: frequent passage of small volumes, hesitation of micturition, slow stream, sensation of incomplete emptying, and involuntary leakage when bending down or rising from a chair. Physical signs include a palpable bladder, leakage on elevation of the bladder base, slow urine flow rate on cystometry, and high residual urine. Chronic overflow incontinence risks back pressure to the upper urinary tract.

options: Around the bladder neck as a complete ring
From the pubic symphysis to the sacrum
questions.question: The Trans Obturator Tape (TOT) for stress incontinence is passed from the groin, through the obturator foramen, and placed in what configuration?
questions.explanation: The Trans Obturator Tape (TOT) uses a non-absorbable prolene tape with 2 large needles, passed from the groin through the obturator foramen, placed in a hammock-like fashion under the mid-urethra. It achieves an 80% success rate. Complications include haemorrhage and bladder perforation. Discharge is usually next day with recovery in 1-4 weeks. It can be combined with pelvic floor repair or hysterectomy.

options: Surgical intervention as the initial approach
A detailed sexual and relationship history from both partners
Hormonal testing without any history taking
Immediate referral for assisted reproductive technology
questions.question: The MOST appropriate first step in evaluating a couple presenting with infertility related to sexual dysfunction is:
questions.explanation: A thorough sexual and relationship history from both partners is the essential first step in evaluating sexual dysfunction contributing to infertility, helping to identify contributing psychological, relational, or physical factors before proceeding to targeted investigations or treatment.

Chorionic villous sampling (CVS) can be performed earlier in pregnancy (at 10-12 weeks gestation) compared to amniocentesis (at 16 weeks), allowing earlier prenatal chromosomal diagnosis and earlier termination of affected pregnancies if indicated. The chromosomes from the chorionic villi (which are of fetal origin) are harvested, stained, and arranged for karyotypic analysis, identifying chromosomal abnormalities such as trisomies, deletions, and translocations.
questions.question: Chorionic villous sampling (CVS) is mentioned as an alternative to amniocentesis for prenatal chromosomal diagnosis. What is the primary advantage of CVS over amniocentesis?
options: CVS can be done at any gestational age
CVS has a lower complication rate than amniocentesis
CVS provides more chromosomal information than amniocentesis
CVS does not require laboratory culture
CVS performed earlier in pregnancy than amniocentesis

questions.explanation: The buccal smear must be collected after the mouth has been thoroughly washed out to remove food debris, bacteria, and desquamated cells that could obscure nuclear chromatin and lead to inaccurate interpretation. The metal spatula is used to scrape from inside the cheek. The smear is fixed immediately with equal parts 95% alcohol and ether, then stained after 1 hour of fixing.
questions.question: Buccal smear collection requires the mouth to be thoroughly washed before sampling. Why is this instruction critical?
options: Oral medications alter the chromatin pattern
The fixative reacts with food particles causing staining artefacts
Mouth washing stimulates exfoliation of buccal cells

questions.question: Primary vaginal carcinoma is diagnosed only when the tumour does NOT also involve which adjacent structure?
questions.explanation: By convention, a tumour involving both the vagina and cervix, or vagina and vulva, is classified according to the primary site rather than as primary vaginal carcinoma, which is diagnosed only when the vagina is the sole site of origin.

Decubitus ulcers develop on the prolapsed cervix due to kinking of blood vessels causing relative ischaemia, leading to oedematous cervix and abrasions. Treatment involves packing the vagina with antiseptic-containing gauze (moistened with acriflavine or hibitane). Healing of decubitus ulcer is also one of the indications for pessary insertion before definitive surgical repair.
questions.question: A woman with 3rd degree prolapse is treated with vaginal packing moistened with acriflavine. What complication is this treating?

options: Endometriosis always causes complete tubal occlusion preventing any pregnancy
Increased tubal peristalsis speeding transport excessively
Direct hormonal stimulation of ectopic implantation
Peritubal adhesions distorting normal tubal transport
questions.explanation: Endometriosis causes chronic pelvic inflammation, adhesions, and distortion of the fallopian tube's normal anatomy and motility, impairing the coordinated transport of the fertilised ovum toward the uterine cavity and increasing the likelihood of tubal implantation. This mechanism is similar in principle to that seen with pelvic infection-related tubal damage. It is one of several structural causes of ectopic pregnancy beyond salpingitis.
questions.question: An endometriotic implant obstructing the fallopian tube is listed as a cause of ectopic pregnancy. By which mechanism does endometriosis predispose to tubal implantation?
A patient develops sudden dyspnoea and pleuritic chest pain on the second postoperative day following gynaecological laparotomy. The MOST important immediate diagnosis to exclude is:
questions.explanation: Sudden dyspnoea and pleuritic chest pain in the early postoperative period should immediately raise suspicion of pulmonary embolism, a potentially life-threatening complication of venous thromboembolism, requiring urgent investigation and empirical anticoagulation while confirmation is awaited if clinical suspicion is high.

questions.question: An unexplained postmenopausal watery vaginal discharge with abnormal cervical cytology without obvious cause should prompt:
questions.explanation: Unexplained postmenopausal watery discharge or abnormal cervical cytology without obvious cause requires a careful bimanual examination and pelvic ultrasound to exclude fallopian tube pathology. Laparoscopy should be performed in doubtful cases where an adnexal mass is suspected clinically or on imaging.

questions.question: A 58-year-old presents with a sensation of vaginal bulge and pelvic pressure worse at the end of the day, with the cervix visible at the introitus on straining. What is the MOST likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: A bulge sensation worsening with prolonged standing or straining, with visible descent of the cervix toward or through the introitus, is classic for uterovaginal (pelvic organ) prolapse, commonly related to weakened pelvic floor support structures. Bartholin cysts present as localised swelling near the vaginal introitus rather than a generalised bulge with cervical descent. Recognising positional symptom variation is a key diagnostic clue for prolapse.

The wooden spatula (Ayre's spatula) is the classical instrument used to scrape cells from the squamocolumnar junction of the cervix for cytological examination in the Pap smear. It collects exfoliated epithelial cells that are then smeared onto a glass slide for staining and microscopy. It has no role in cervical dilation.
questions.question: During vaginal speculum examination, a wooden spatula is used primarily to:
A researcher measures gonadotrophin-releasing hormone pulse frequency across the menstrual cycle. Which pattern of GnRH pulsatility favours LH secretion over FSH secretion?
questions.explanation: High-frequency GnRH pulsation preferentially stimulates LH synthesis and release, characteristic of the late follicular phase before ovulation. Slower pulse frequencies favour FSH secretion, typical of the luteal phase. Continuous non-pulsatile GnRH exposure paradoxically desensitises the pituitary, the principle behind GnRH agonist suppression therapy.
options: Irregular pulses of variable amplitude only
A transverse incision just above the pubic symphysis
A vertical midline incision from umbilicus to pubis
questions.question: The MOST appropriate site for a Pfannenstiel incision in gynaecological surgery is:
questions.explanation: The Pfannenstiel incision is a low transverse suprapubic incision that follows Langer's lines, offering good cosmetic results and strong healing, and is commonly used for gynaecological procedures such as hysterectomy and caesarean section.

Vitamin deficiency (specifically Vitamin A and folic acid) is listed among the aetiological factors for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN). Vitamin A is important for normal epithelial differentiation and immune function, while folic acid deficiency may increase susceptibility to HPV-associated cervical changes. These are modifiable risk factors that can be addressed through dietary counselling alongside other CIN prevention strategies.
questions.question: Vitamin deficiency is listed among the aetiological factors for CIN. Which specific vitamins are mentioned?
A woman previously treated for gestational trophoblastic neoplasia who achieves hCG remission should have contraception maintained for which period before attempting pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Following successful chemotherapy and hCG normalisation for gestational trophoblastic neoplasia, contraception is recommended for twelve months to allow completion of surveillance and to avoid the confounding effect of a new pregnancy on hCG interpretation.

Increasing paternal age is associated with higher rates of de novo mutations in sperm DNA resulting from the large number of mitotic divisions that spermatogonial stem cells undergo throughout a man's life, accumulating replication errors. These mutations can affect embryonic development and contribute to spontaneous abortion and certain congenital conditions. This mechanism differs from maternal age effects, which primarily involve meiotic non-disjunction causing chromosomal aneuploidy.
options: Older fathers producing fewer sperm overall
Reduced testosterone causing morphologically abnormal sperm
Paternal immune senescence causing maternal immune rejection
Sperm DNA mutations accumulating with age
Paternal epigenetic changes reducing placental invasion
questions.question: An OBGYN lecturer explains that increasing paternal age also increases the risk of spontaneous abortion. The mechanism most likely involves:

questions.explanation: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumours secrete androgens and characteristically cause virilising features such as hirsutism, clitoromegaly, and voice deepening. This androgenic pattern contrasts with the oestrogenic effects of granulosa cell tumours.
options: Virilisation with deepening of the voice
questions.question: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumours of the ovary typically present with which clinical feature?

options: Prolonged high temperature exposure impairs later spermatogenesis
Orchidopexy itself always causes infertility regardless of timing
Later orchidopexy improves fertility potential compared with earlier correction
Undescended testes have no relationship to fertility outcomes
Orchidopexy prevents testicular cancer but has no effect on fertility
questions.question: A man with a history of bilateral undescended testes corrected by orchidopexy at age 12 presents with infertility. Why does the timing of surgical correction matter for his future fertility despite eventual correction?
questions.explanation: The scrotal position is important for maintaining the lower temperature required for normal spermatogenesis; prolonged intra-abdominal or inguinal positioning of the testes before surgical correction exposes the developing germ cells to higher core body temperature, which can impair long-term spermatogenic potential even after eventual successful orchidopexy. This is why earlier surgical correction, typically recommended in early childhood, is associated with better long-term fertility outcomes than later correction. Undescended testes also carry an increased risk of testicular malignancy, which orchidopexy helps to monitor.

options: 30% of women achieve reduced bleeding only
questions.question: The rate of haemostasis following hysteroscopic endometrial ablation for DUB (complete amenorrhoea) is approximately:
questions.explanation: Endometrial ablation results in complete amenorrhoea in approximately 50% of women treated and in reduced (but not absent) menstrual bleeding in about 90% of women with menorrhagia. It is not 100% effective, and residual endometrium can regenerate and potentially progress to carcinoma if the ablation was incomplete. Pre-treatment endometrial suppression (with GnRH analogues, danazol, or MPA for 4–6 weeks) improves outcomes by thinning the endometrium before ablation.

Rising antimicrobial resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae has necessitated updated treatment guidelines, often involving dual therapy or higher-dose regimens, to ensure effective eradication and reduce the risk of treatment failure and further resistance development.
questions.question: Gonorrhoea caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae has increasingly required which change in antibiotic management strategy?
options: No antibiotic treatment since it resolves spontaneously
Dual therapy or updated regimens due to rising antimicrobial resistance
Single-dose penicillin as the universal first-line treatment

questions.explanation: Stress urinary incontinence is demonstrated by asking the patient to cough or bear down (Valsalva manoeuvre) while the physician observes the urethral meatus for an involuntary spurt of urine. This test should be performed with a comfortably full bladder. It is a simple and immediate clinical method to confirm stress incontinence without urodynamic testing.
options: Cough or bear down during vulval observation
Perform a Valsalva manoeuvre standing up only
Drink 500 mL of water before examination
questions.question: Stress incontinence during pelvic examination is best demonstrated by asking the patient to:

options: Increasing obesity and reduced fluid intake with age
Ageing, menopause, and cumulative obstetric injury
Declining renal function increasing urine production
Progressive cerebral atrophy reducing voluntary sphincter control alone
questions.question: A newly qualified doctor observes that urinary incontinence prevalence increases with age. Which combination of age-related factors best explains this pattern?
questions.explanation: Urinary incontinence prevalence increases with age because of the cumulative impact of multiple factors: the ageing process itself (declining muscle mass, connective tissue changes, altered neural control), menopause (hypoestrogenism causing urogenital atrophy), cumulative obstetric injury (pelvic floor damage from previous deliveries), obesity (commonly increases with age), and prior pelvic surgery. This multifactorial aetiology explains why comprehensive assessment and individualised management are essential in older women.

Uncorrected preoperative anaemia is associated with higher rates of perioperative complications, increased need for blood transfusion, and poorer postoperative recovery, so optimisation with iron therapy or other measures before elective surgery improves overall surgical outcomes.
questions.question: Preoperative correction of iron-deficiency anaemia before elective major gynaecological surgery is important primarily because anaemia is associated with:
options: Reduced risk of surgical site infection
Increased perioperative morbidity and transfusion requirement

questions.question: The MOST reliable tumour marker for diagnosis and surveillance of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia is:
questions.explanation: Beta hCG is produced by trophoblastic tissue and serves as an ideal tumour marker for gestational trophoblastic neoplasia because its levels correlate closely with tumour burden, allowing sensitive diagnosis, monitoring of treatment response, and detection of recurrence.

questions.question: Clomiphene citrate is first-line treatment for anovulatory infertility. It achieves ovulation induction by which mechanism?
questions.explanation: Clomiphene citrate is a selective oestrogen receptor modulator (SERM) that competitively blocks hypothalamic oestrogen receptors, preventing negative feedback inhibition of GnRH. The hypothalamus responds by increasing GnRH pulse frequency, stimulating pituitary FSH and LH secretion, which drives follicular development and ovulation. Clomiphene achieves ovulation in approximately 70–80% and pregnancy in 40–50% of anovulatory infertile women.
options: Blocking hypothalamic oestrogen receptors, increasing GnRH and FSH
Direct stimulation of ovarian follicle-stimulating hormone receptors
Stimulating pituitary LH surge to trigger ovulation
Providing exogenous FSH equivalent to stimulate follicular development
Reducing serum prolactin levels to restore GnRH pulsatility

questions.question: A woman with a previous ectopic pregnancy treated by salpingectomy presents with a new positive pregnancy test. Which investigation is most important as an initial step given her surgical history?
questions.explanation: A history of previous ectopic pregnancy and salpingectomy substantially increases the risk of a further ectopic pregnancy in the remaining tube, so early transvaginal ultrasound to confirm intrauterine location is the appropriate first step in a new pregnancy. This allows timely diagnosis and management if the new pregnancy is again ectopic. Serial hCG measurement may be used alongside ultrasound if location is not immediately clear.
options: Early transvaginal ultrasound to confirm pregnancy location
The rectosigmoid colon and pouch of Douglas
questions.explanation: Deep infiltrating endometriosis classically affects the rectosigmoid colon and the pouch of Douglas, and implants in this region can cause cyclical dyschezia as the affected bowel wall is stretched or distorted during defaecation, particularly around menstruation when the implants are most active. This differs from more proximal bowel segments, which are less commonly affected. Recognising this pattern helps direct further imaging and surgical planning if bowel resection is being considered.
questions.question: Endometriosis affecting the bowel is a recognised cause of cyclical dyschezia (painful defaecation). Involvement of which specific bowel structure is most classically implicated in this symptom?

options: 80–95% per act with correct consistent use
questions.explanation: Consistent and correct male condom use reduces the per-act probability of HIV transmission by approximately 80–95%. Meta-analyses of serodiscordant couples show approximately 80% reduction in HIV incidence in the consistent user group. The residual transmission reflects inconsistent use (not using every act), incorrect application, and condom failure. Mathematical models show that even with 70% consistency, substantial population-level HIV prevention occurs.
questions.question: The protective effect of male condoms against HIV transmission reduces per-act transmission probability by approximately:

options: Elective caesarean section in all seropositive mothers
Neonatal prophylaxis with oral erythromycin from birth
Screening all pregnant women with syphilis serology and treating positive cases with benzathine penicillin G
Maternal vaccination against syphilis at 16 weeks gestation
questions.explanation: Universal syphilis screening in antenatal care with serological testing (RPR/VDRL + confirmatory TPHA) and prompt treatment of positive cases with benzathine penicillin G is the cornerstone of congenital syphilis prevention. Treatment adequately given more than 4 weeks before delivery prevents almost all congenital syphilis. Route of delivery does not affect transmission. No syphilis vaccine exists.
questions.question: Congenital syphilis is MOST effectively prevented by:

A woman with PCOS and long-standing anovulation has not had a period for four months, with ultrasound showing an endometrial thickness of 15mm. Why is this finding of MOST concern in the context of PCOS?
questions.explanation: Chronic anovulation in PCOS results in continuous oestrogen exposure without the cyclical progesterone-induced shedding seen in ovulatory cycles, leading to endometrial hyperplasia and an increased long-term risk of endometrial carcinoma if unaddressed. Regular induced withdrawal bleeding, using cyclical progestins or hormonal contraception, is recommended to mitigate this risk. This is why amenorrhoea in PCOS should not simply be regarded as a benign inconvenience.
options: It confirms an ongoing early pregnancy state
It suggests coexisting ovarian malignancy always
It reflects normal endometrial thinning pattern
Unopposed oestrogen increases endometrial hyperplasia risk

questions.question: The MOST common histological subtype of epithelial ovarian cancer overall is:
questions.explanation: Serous carcinoma accounts for the largest proportion of epithelial ovarian cancers and is frequently associated with BRCA mutations and advanced-stage presentation. Mucinous and endometrioid subtypes are less common and often present at an earlier stage.

Turner syndrome (45,X) is strongly associated with coarctation of the aorta and bicuspid aortic valve, making cardiac imaging, typically echocardiography, an essential part of initial and ongoing evaluation to detect these potentially serious anomalies. These specific lesions are far more characteristic of Turner syndrome than the other listed congenital heart defects. Early detection allows appropriate monitoring for aortic dissection risk, particularly relevant if pregnancy is pursued via oocyte donation.
options: Aortic coarctation and bicuspid aortic valve
questions.question: A 46,XX individual with Turner-like features is found to have a 45,X karyotype with streak gonads. Which cardiovascular anomaly is MOST important to screen for given its strong association with this condition?

questions.explanation: The presenting triad of postmenopausal bleeding, watery vaginal discharge, and lower abdominal pain in fallopian tube cancer closely mimics endometrial carcinoma and is frequently misattributed to it. Diagnosis is seldom considered preoperatively; most cases are discovered at laparotomy or after histological analysis.
questions.question: A woman with cancer of the fallopian tube presents with postmenopausal bleeding, watery vaginal discharge, and lower abdominal pain. The MOST likely initial diagnosis mistakenly considered is:

questions.explanation: Complex hyperplasia without atypia requires progestin therapy (typically high-dose MPA or LNG-IUS) for 3 months, followed by mandatory re-sampling to confirm regression before any surgical decision. Persistent hyperplasia or development of atypia on re-sampling may indicate surgical therapy (hysterectomy). Endometrial ablation is not appropriate when hyperplasia is present (because residual endometrium may progress to carcinoma unrecognised). Hysterectomy is reserved for failed medical management.
questions.question: A 42-year-old woman with DUB has failed hormonal therapy. She has completed her family and prefers a definitive solution. Endometrial sampling shows complex hyperplasia without atypia. The MOST appropriate next step is:

questions.explanation: In non-breastfeeding women, ovulation can return as early as 3 weeks (21 days) postpartum, before the first menstrual period. This means a woman can conceive again before she realizes her fertility has returned. Family planning counselling should therefore begin before discharge and contraception initiated by 3 weeks postpartum for non-breastfeeding mothers.
questions.question: During postpartum family planning counselling, the earliest time a non-breastfeeding woman may ovulate after delivery is:
In a mass screening programme for cervical cytology, compared to individual screening, cost-effectiveness is:
questions.explanation: A key shortcoming of cytology in mass screening programmes is that cost-effectiveness is not as high as in individual screening programmes. This is because cytology interpretation (the cytologist's expertise) is costly, there are significant inter-observer variations in reading slides, and cells can be difficult to interpret due to staining failures affecting cellular integrity, necessitating histological confirmation.

Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is perihepatic inflammation (capsular hepatitis) occurring as a complication of ascending genital tract infection with Chlamydia trachomatis or Neisseria gonorrhoeae. It presents as right upper quadrant pain (often confused with cholecystitis), with violin-string perihepatic adhesions visible on laparoscopy. It is an important cause of RUQ pain in sexually active women with concurrent PID symptoms.
questions.question: The Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome (perihepatitis) is associated with which of the following sexually transmitted infections?
options: Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae causing ascending perihepatic inflammation

questions.explanation: Hyperprolactinaemia most commonly presents with menstrual irregularity (oligomenorrhoea or amenorrhoea) rather than galactorrhoea, contrary to common assumption. Prolactin inhibits GnRH pulsatility, suppressing LH and FSH, leading to oestrogen deficiency and anovulation. Galactorrhoea is present in only 30–50% of hyperprolactinaemic women and should not be relied upon as the primary presenting complaint.
questions.question: A woman presents with amenorrhoea and galactorrhoea. Serum prolactin is elevated. Hyperprolactinaemia most commonly presents with which primary symptom according to clinical teaching?

A woman at 30 weeks with preterm prelabour rupture of membranes is admitted for expectant management. Which class of medication is administered to reduce the risk of neonatal respiratory distress syndrome should preterm delivery occur?
questions.explanation: Antenatal corticosteroids, such as dexamethasone or betamethasone, accelerate fetal lung maturation by stimulating surfactant production, significantly reducing the risk and severity of neonatal respiratory distress syndrome if preterm delivery occurs within an appropriate window after administration. This is a standard, evidence-based intervention in women at risk of preterm birth within the relevant gestational age range. Prophylactic antibiotics are also typically given in preterm prelabour rupture of membranes to reduce the risk of ascending infection and prolong latency.

questions.question: A 25-year-old woman is found to have a 10 cm unilateral ovarian cyst during antenatal care. The MOST important reason to defer surgery until the second trimester (if not yet done) is:
options: To allow time for tumour marker results
Because anaesthesia is always contraindicated in the first trimester
Because ovarian cysts always resolve after 14 weeks
questions.explanation: Surgery should be deferred until after 14 weeks gestation to avoid the inadvertent removal of a corpus luteum cyst, which is essential for progesterone production to maintain the pregnancy in the first trimester. Before 14 weeks, the corpus luteum supports the pregnancy hormonally.

questions.question: A woman asks whether the withdrawal method can be combined with fertility awareness to improve effectiveness. She should be advised that:
options: Fertility awareness alone is unnecessary once withdrawal is used
Combining these methods has no effect on overall effectiveness
Combining methods can improve effectiveness but neither eliminates risk during the fertile window
Withdrawal used during the fertile window is completely safe
This combination provides guaranteed protection equivalent to hormonal methods
questions.explanation: While combining withdrawal with fertility awareness to avoid intercourse or add withdrawal specifically during the estimated fertile window may modestly improve overall effectiveness compared with either method alone, neither approach eliminates pregnancy risk, particularly given the inherent unreliability of both methods individually.

Borderline tumours show cellular atypia and proliferation similar to malignant tumours but lack destructive stromal invasion, giving them a much better prognosis. They can still implant on peritoneal surfaces but generally behave indolently compared to invasive carcinoma.
questions.question: Borderline ovarian tumours differ from frankly malignant epithelial ovarian cancers primarily by:
In the MALE embryo, testosterone secreted by Leydig cells is converted by 5-alpha-reductase in cloacal cells to dihydrotestosterone (DHT). DHT then acts on androgen receptors to produce:
questions.explanation: DHT acts on androgen receptors in the cloaca to produce the external male genitalia — the genital tubercle becomes the glans penis and penile shaft, the urogenital sinus becomes the urethral tube, and the urogenital folds form the scrotum. Testosterone itself (without conversion) acts on the Wolffian ducts to produce the internal male structures (vas deferens, epididymis, seminal vesicles). AMH suppresses Müllerian ducts.

A formal, documented count of swabs and instruments performed by theatre nursing staff before closure, cross-checked against the count at the start of the procedure, is the primary safeguard against retained surgical items, supplemented by radiopaque markers as an additional safety net.
options: Limiting the number of staff present in theatre
Formal swab and instrument count before and after the procedure
Postoperative X-ray in every single case regardless of count
Using only radiopaque swabs without any counting protocol
questions.question: The MOST important step in preventing retained surgical swabs during gynaecological laparotomy is:
In FIGO Stage IIA endometrial carcinoma, the tumour has extended to involve:
questions.explanation: FIGO Stage IIA endometrial carcinoma involves endocervical glandular involvement only, without cervical stromal invasion. Stage IIB involves cervical stromal invasion. This distinction is important as stromal invasion (IIB) carries a worse prognosis and may require more aggressive surgical and adjuvant treatment.

options: Hepatic enzyme induction from the first doses reduces efficacy for 7 days
Pill efficacy requires 7 days of hormonal priming of the hypothalamic feedback axis
Estrogen requires 7 days to build adequate endometrial thickness
She may have already ovulated before starting (as Day 1–5 start offers immediate protection only from Day 1)
The progestogen component takes 7 days to reach therapeutic plasma levels
questions.explanation: When COCs are started after Day 1 of the menstrual cycle (the 'quick start' or 'Day 2–5 start'), 7 days of additional contraceptive cover are needed because the suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis and the secondary contraceptive mechanisms (mucus thickening) take approximately 7 days to become fully effective. Starting on Day 1 provides immediate protection because ovarian activity is lowest at menstruation onset.
questions.question: A woman who started her combined oral contraceptive pill on day 3 of her cycle is advised that she needs additional contraception for the first 7 days because:

questions.explanation: A serum beta-hCG level above 100,000 mIU/ml (or 40,000 mIU/ml in some systems) is a significant risk factor in the FIGO/WHO scoring for GTD. While 45,000 mIU/ml specifically may vary by scoring version, persistently high hCG levels contribute to high-risk classification requiring combination chemotherapy.
questions.question: A patient with high-risk GTD has serum beta-hCG of 45,000 mIU/ml. According to FIGO/WHO risk scoring, this level constitutes:

questions.explanation: Preoperative cardiac risk assessment involves evaluating functional capacity and using validated risk indices to determine whether further investigations, such as echocardiography or stress testing, are warranted before proceeding with major surgery, allowing individualised risk stratification rather than blanket cancellation or investigation.
questions.question: Preoperative assessment of cardiac risk before major gynaecological cancer surgery in an elderly patient with known ischaemic heart disease should MOST appropriately include:
options: Substituting local anaesthesia for general anaesthesia automatically
Proceeding to surgery without any cardiac assessment
Routine coronary angiography for every patient regardless of symptoms
Functional capacity assessment and, if indicated, further cardiac investigation
Cancellation of surgery in all cases with any cardiac history

questions.question: A man presents with infertility following mumps orchitis at age 19. Semen analysis shows azoospermia. His FSH is markedly elevated. Which classification best describes his condition?
questions.explanation: Mumps orchitis can cause bilateral testicular damage resulting in non-obstructive azoospermia (testicular failure/primary testicular hypogonadism). The markedly elevated FSH indicates the pituitary is appropriately responding to absent negative feedback from damaged Sertoli and Leydig cells. This contrasts with obstructive azoospermia where FSH is normal because spermatogenesis continues but flow is blocked.

questions.question: A woman with prolapse on clinical examination shows a lump at the introitus that reduces on lying down. This is most consistent with which degree of prolapse?
questions.explanation: 2nd degree prolapse is characterised by descent of the cervix to the level of the introitus. It is the commonest degree encountered clinically. A prolapse that is visible at or near the introitus but reduces on lying down corresponds well with 2nd degree, as gravity worsens descent in the standing position while recumbency relieves it.

questions.question: A 32-year-old nulliparous woman has a 6 cm unilateral ovarian cyst confirmed as serous cystadenoma at laparotomy. The MOST appropriate surgical management preserving her fertility is:
questions.explanation: In young women wishing to preserve reproductive capacity, enucleation of the cyst (cystectomy) is the preferred approach, retaining as much normal ovarian tissue as possible. TAH with BSO is reserved for postmenopausal women or cases with confirmed malignancy.

questions.question: Secondary amenorrhoea is generally defined as cessation of menstruation for a specific minimum duration in a previously menstruating woman. What is this standard minimum duration?
questions.explanation: Secondary amenorrhoea is generally defined as absence of menstruation for more than 6 months in a woman who has previously had normal periods, though some definitions use 3 missed cycles as an alternative threshold. This distinguishes it from a single missed period, which may simply reflect normal cycle variability or early pregnancy. Investigation is warranted once this threshold is reached, or earlier if there are other concerning features.
options: More than 6 weeks in every case regardless of context

questions.question: A patient at 22 weeks presents with abdominal cramps and passage of a fetus weighing 450g without signs of life. She had no antenatal care. According to BOTH Nigerian and WHO definitions, how is this event classified?
options: Abortion by Nigerian and WHO definitions
Preterm neonatal death by both definitions
questions.explanation: At 22 weeks with a fetus weighing 450g (below the 500g WHO threshold and well below the 1,000g Nigerian threshold), this event constitutes an abortion by BOTH the WHO and Nigerian definitions. Nigeria defines abortion as delivery before 28 weeks or <1,000g, and WHO defines it as <500g at expulsion (approximately 20–24 weeks). This case falls below both thresholds simultaneously, confirming classification as abortion under both systems.

questions.question: Struma ovarii is an ovarian teratoma composed predominantly of which tissue type?
questions.explanation: Struma ovarii is a monodermal teratoma composed mainly of mature thyroid tissue and can rarely cause hyperthyroidism. It is distinguished from typical dermoid cysts, which contain a mixture of ectodermal, mesodermal, and endodermal elements.

questions.question: Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome (PCOS) presents with DUB-type bleeding. The DUB in PCOS is primarily anovulatory. Which additional investigation specifically helps confirm PCOS as the cause?
options: Pelvic ultrasound, elevated LH:FSH ratio, and androgens
MRI of the brain for pituitary assessment
questions.explanation: PCOS is confirmed by the Rotterdam criteria (2 of 3): oligo/anovulation (irregular cycles), clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenaemia (elevated testosterone/DHEA-S, hirsutism, acne), and polycystic ovarian morphology on ultrasound (=12 follicles per ovary or ovarian volume > 10 mL). In the context of DUB, an elevated LH:FSH ratio, hyperandrogenaemia, and polycystic ovaries on ultrasound together confirm PCOS as the underlying aetiology. Endometrial biopsy is also important to exclude hyperplasia.

questions.question: Amniocentesis for fibroblast culture is performed at which gestational age?
questions.explanation: Amniocentesis for fibroblast culture (prenatal chromosome diagnosis) is done at 16 weeks gestation to collect amniotic fluid containing fetal fibroblasts. The cells are cultured and chromosomes are harvested, stained, and arranged as a karyotype. Chromosomal abnormalities (deletions, translocations, trisomies) can thus be detected, and therapeutic abortion may be performed where indicated.

options: Temporary inability to achieve another orgasm or erection regardless of stimulation
Release of vasopressin suppressing sexual desire permanently
questions.explanation: The male refractory period is the obligatory recovery time after orgasm during which further orgasm is physiologically impossible regardless of stimulation. It is mediated by serotonin and prolactin release post-orgasm. Duration increases with age. Women have little or no refractory period, enabling multiple orgasms. This is a key sex difference in the sexual response cycle.
questions.question: Which physiological event is the HALLMARK of the male refractory period following orgasm?

options: Both fallopian tubes are completely blocked
There is a uterine septum present
questions.explanation: Free spillage of contrast dye into the peritoneal cavity from both tubal ends during hysterosalpingography confirms that both fallopian tubes are patent, allowing passage of gametes and the fertilised ovum. Absence of spillage, by contrast, suggests tubal occlusion requiring further evaluation. This investigation is a key initial step in assessing tubal factor infertility.
questions.question: During hysterosalpingography performed for infertility investigation, free spillage of dye from both tubes is observed. What does this specific finding indicate about tubal status?
Which of the following best distinguishes 'perfect use' from 'typical use' failure rates of a contraceptive?
options: Perfect use applies to older women; typical use to younger women
Perfect use failure rate reflects consistent, correct use; typical use includes human error and inconsistency
Typical use applies only to barrier methods; perfect use to hormonal methods
Perfect use refers to laboratory conditions; typical use to clinical trials
There is no meaningful difference between the two rates
questions.explanation: Perfect-use failure rate reflects the method's theoretical efficacy when used consistently and correctly every time. Typical-use failure rate includes real-world inconsistencies: missed pills, improper condom application, and non-adherence. The gap between the two reveals how much human behavior affects method effectiveness. Methods like male condoms have a much larger gap than implants.

questions.question: The effectiveness of natural family planning is MOST likely to be compromised by which of the following clinical situations?
options: Regular moderate exercise and normal body weight
Tracking cycles using a standard wall calendar
Intercurrent febrile illness altering BBT readings
questions.explanation: Febrile illnesses elevate the basal body temperature through the same mechanism as the post-ovulatory progesterone rise, making it impossible to distinguish a true thermal shift from fever. This can lead to incorrect identification of the post-ovulatory infertile phase and unprotected intercourse during the fertile window. Any systemic illness or factor affecting temperature (sleep disturbances, alcohol, jet lag) can compromise BBT-based methods.

questions.question: Uterine perforation during IUCD insertion is MOST commonly caused by:
questions.explanation: Uterine perforation during IUD insertion most commonly results from inserting the sound or device forcefully, particularly when the uterus is retroflexed (increasing risk of posterior wall perforation), not adequately sounded beforehand, or the fundal depth is misjudged. The risk is also higher at immediate postpartum insertion (soft uterus) and in breastfeeding women (estrogen-deficient, softened uterus). Careful technique and pre-insertion uterine sounding are critical preventive measures.
options: Forceful insertion without adequate uterine sounding or against abnormal uterine anatomy
Excessive expulsive force by the patient during insertion
Use of a copper rather than hormonal IUD
Leaving the insertion tube in situ for longer than 2 minutes

questions.explanation: Sounding the uterus before IUD insertion establishes the depth and axis of the uterine cavity, helping to confirm that the size is appropriate for the device and reducing the risk of malposition or perforation during subsequent insertion.
questions.question: Uterine sounding performed before IUD insertion is primarily performed to:
options: Fully dilate the cervix before insertion
Provide analgesia for the procedure itself
Measure the length of the cervix
Determine uterine size and the cavity's direction

questions.question: At menarche, the human ovary contains approximately how many primordial follicles?
questions.explanation: At menarche, the human ovary contains approximately 300,000 primordial follicles, which represents a dramatic decline from the peak of 7 million at around 5 months in utero. The decline continues throughout reproductive life through atresia. Of the 300,000 at menarche, only approximately 400–500 will ever ovulate in a lifetime; the remainder undergo atresia.

Cystoscopy is specifically indicated for unexplained haematuria and small bladder volume, as listed in the urodynamic investigations of incontinence and urinary fistula. It allows direct visualisation of the bladder interior, identifying the fistula orifice, bladder tumours, radiation cystitis, or other mucosal abnormalities. It is an essential investigation before surgical repair of VVF to assess the bladder mucosa and fistula characteristics.
questions.question: Which investigation is specifically indicated in unexplained haematuria and small bladder volume in a patient with suspected urinary fistula?

options: Patient self-report of pad usage and clots
Measurement of serum ferritin and haemoglobin
Alkaline haematin method extracting haemoglobin from sanitary materials
Weighing all sanitary materials before and after use
questions.question: The gold standard objective method for measuring menstrual blood loss (MBL) in research settings is:
questions.explanation: The alkaline haematin method is the objective research gold standard for measuring MBL — it extracts total haemoglobin from all sanitary materials used during menstruation and converts it to haematin using sodium hydroxide, which is then measured spectrophotometrically. The 79 mL upper limit of normal MBL was established using this method. In clinical practice, the Pictorial Blood Assessment Chart (PBAC) is a validated semi-objective surrogate used by patients.

Endometrial carcinoma is staged surgically by exploratory laparotomy including TAH, BSO, peritoneal cytology, and pelvic and para-aortic lymphadenectomy. Surgical pathological findings determine the final FIGO stage, which directly guides decisions about adjuvant radiotherapy, chemotherapy, or progestogen therapy.
questions.question: The staging procedure for endometrial carcinoma that also determines adjuvant treatment is:
options: CT abdomen and pelvis with CA-125
