questions.explanation: The transformation zone (TZ) is the area between the original and new squamocolumnar junctions where squamous metaplasia occurs. Immature metaplastic cells in this zone are uniquely susceptible to HPV infection and oncogenic transformation, making the TZ the site of origin of virtually all cervical intraepithelial neoplasias (CIN) and invasive cervical cancers. Colposcopy specifically targets this zone; an inadequate colposcopy is one where the entire TZ cannot be visualized.
options: It is the most glandular area producing the most mucus
It is the zone between internal and external os only
Squamocolumnar junction where metaplastic change increases HPV susceptibility
It provides the best vascular supply protecting against infection
It contains the highest concentration of Nabothian follicles
questions.question: A colposcopy is performed using acetic acid application to the cervix. An acetowhite lesion is identified at the transformation zone. What is the significance of the transformation zone in cervical pathology?

questions.explanation: When both fallopian tubes are patent, the injected methylene blue dye passes through the uterine cavity, along each tube, and spills freely out of the fimbriated ends into the pouch of Douglas (rectouterine pouch) under laparoscopic vision. This free intraperitoneal spillage confirms tubal patency. Failure to spill indicates tubal obstruction at some point along the tube's length.
questions.question: Methylene blue dye is injected during laparoscopy to test tubal patency. When tubes are PATENT, where is the dye observed to flow?
options: Out through fimbriated ends into Douglas pouch
Through the cervix and into the vagina

questions.question: During surgery for a large cervical fibroid, the operating surgeon takes particular care to identify and avoid two closely related structures. Which pair is at greatest risk during this dissection?
questions.explanation: Cervical fibroids distort normal anatomy and displace the ureters, which run close to the uterine vessels near the cervix, placing both structures at risk during dissection. Careful identification before clamping or ligating tissue is essential to avoid ureteric injury. This risk is greater than with corporeal fibroid surgery due to the cervix's proximity to these structures.

HPV types 16 and 18 together cause approximately 70% of all cervical cancers globally, classifying them as high-risk (oncogenic) genotypes. HPV 16 is particularly associated with squamous cell carcinoma, while HPV 18 is more associated with adenocarcinoma. The quadrivalent and nonavalent HPV vaccines target these strains. Persistent high-risk HPV infection is the necessary precursor for virtually all cervical cancers.
questions.question: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) serotypes 16 and 18 are responsible for approximately what proportion of cervical cancer cases worldwide?

The TwoDay Method of natural family planning instructs a woman to avoid unprotected intercourse on any day when she has noticed secretions today OR yesterday. What is the underlying physiological rationale?
options: Secretions in the preceding 48 hours indicate recent ovulation has already occurred
Cervical secretions present on either of two consecutive days indicate ongoing cervical mucus production signalling potential fertility
Any secretions over two consecutive days indicate the fertile phase has ended
Two days of observation is the minimum to confirm cervical infection versus fertile mucus
Secretions lasting more than 2 days indicate pathological cervicitis
questions.explanation: The TwoDay Method simplifies fertility awareness: if secretions were present today or yesterday, the woman considers herself potentially fertile and avoids unprotected intercourse. Any secretions — regardless of type — indicate cervical mucus production, which correlates with estrogen stimulation and potential fertility. The method avoids distinguishing mucus types, making it simpler than the Billings method.

Depth of myometrial invasion strongly correlates with lymph node involvement and overall prognosis in endometrial carcinoma, forming a central component of surgical staging. Deep invasion beyond half the myometrial thickness significantly worsens outcome.
questions.question: The single MOST important prognostic factor in endometrial carcinoma is:

questions.explanation: Randomised trial evidence demonstrated that second-look laparotomy, once used to assess response after chemotherapy, does not translate into improved overall survival, leading most centres to rely instead on non-invasive surveillance such as imaging and tumour markers.
options: Is associated with excessive intraoperative mortality
Does not improve overall survival outcomes
Is required by all current treatment guidelines
questions.question: Second-look laparotomy following chemotherapy for ovarian cancer has largely been abandoned in modern practice primarily because it:

questions.explanation: Chronic cervicitis typically produces a persistent, less purulent, often mucoid discharge compared with the profuse purulent discharge of acute cervicitis. It reflects long-standing low-grade inflammation of the endocervix rather than an acute infective process. Distinguishing the two guides whether antibiotics or longer-term local treatment is appropriate.
questions.question: A woman presents with a thin, watery, non-purulent cervical discharge persisting for months, without the profuse purulence seen in acute infection. This pattern most typically distinguishes which condition from acute cervicitis?

options: Kinking of the urethra or bladder neck
Ureteric obstruction from the prolapsing cervix
Compression of the sacral nerve roots
Increased outflow resistance from urethral keratinization
questions.explanation: Urinary symptoms in prolapse include urinary retention (obstructive uropathy), urgency, and stress incontinence. Retention occurs when the prolapsing bladder, urethra, or uterus causes kinking or distortion of the bladder neck and urethra, obstructing urinary outflow. Frequency and inadequate emptying with residual urine are related symptoms in cystocele/urethrocele.
questions.question: Urinary retention as a symptom of prolapse occurs most likely due to:

questions.explanation: Overflow incontinence caused by obstructive surgery to the bladder neck is treated by urethral dilatation or urethrotomy to relieve the obstruction and restore normal voiding. If caused by weakened detrusor muscle (from extensive pelvic surgery denervation), treatment is continuous drainage with a suprapubic catheter for 2-3 weeks to improve detrusor tone, followed by bladder training or intermittent self-catheterisation.
questions.question: In the treatment of overflow incontinence caused by outflow obstruction, which specific surgical procedure restores normal voiding?

options: Primarily ovulation suppression, which requires a steady hormonal blood level
Endometrial decidualization requiring sustained daily exposure
Inhibition of tubal cilia which reverses within hours of missed dose
Blocking estrogen receptors in the hypothalamus, which requires constant occupancy
Cervical mucus thickening, which is maintained only while progestogen blood levels are above a threshold
questions.question: The progestogen-only pill (POP/mini-pill) must be taken at the SAME time every day within a 3-hour window. This is because its MAIN contraceptive mechanism — unlike COC — is:
questions.explanation: Traditional POPs (e.g., levonorgestrel POP) work primarily by thickening cervical mucus to block sperm penetration, an effect that requires maintaining progestogen blood levels above a minimum threshold. Mucus-hostility begins to reverse within 3 hours of a late or missed dose, dramatically increasing pregnancy risk. Newer desogestrel POPs additionally suppress ovulation in most cycles.

Urinary frequency and incomplete bladder emptying (urinary retention) are caused by cervical fibroids or large anterior wall fibroids that directly compress the bladder dome and neck, reducing functional bladder capacity and obstructing urethral outflow. Posterior fibroids compress the rectum (constipation/tenesmus) rather than the bladder. The bulk effect of fibroid-related pressure symptoms is one of the indications for surgical intervention regardless of menstrual symptoms.
options: Submucosal fibroid distorting the uterine cavity
Cervical or anterior wall fibroid compressing bladder
Pedunculated subserosal fibroid in the broad ligament
questions.question: A 41-year-old woman with large fibroids presents with urinary frequency and incomplete bladder emptying. Which type of fibroid is responsible for this urinary symptom?

A primigravida at 39 weeks with a fetus in cephalic presentation but occipito-posterior position experiences a prolonged, painful labour. Which specific labour complication is she at increased risk of because of this fetal position?
questions.explanation: Occipito-posterior position is associated with a less efficient mechanism of labour, often resulting in prolonged first and second stages, increased maternal back pain, and a higher likelihood of instrumental delivery or caesarean section compared with the more favourable occipito-anterior position. This is a mechanical labour complication distinct from antepartum haemorrhage conditions such as placenta praevia. Recognising the position on examination helps anticipate and manage a potentially longer, more difficult labour.
options: Prolonged labour raising instrumental delivery likelihood

questions.explanation: Adenomyosis classically presents with heavy, painful periods together with a uniformly enlarged, tender, boggy uterus on bimanual examination, reflecting diffuse myometrial infiltration by ectopic endometrial tissue rather than a discrete mass as seen with fibroids.
questions.question: The classic triad of symptoms MOST suggestive of adenomyosis includes menorrhagia, dysmenorrhoea, and:

questions.explanation: Unscheduled bleeding beyond the expected initial adjustment period of continuous combined hormone replacement therapy warrants endometrial assessment, such as ultrasound or biopsy, to exclude endometrial pathology including hyperplasia or malignancy. Simple reassurance would risk missing a significant underlying diagnosis. Switching to oestrogen-only therapy in a woman with an intact uterus would increase endometrial cancer risk rather than resolve the concern.
options: Stop all therapy without further evaluation
Reassure since bleeding is always expected
questions.question: A 52-year-old postmenopausal woman on continuous combined hormone replacement therapy has unscheduled bleeding after eight months of use. What is the MOST appropriate next step?

questions.explanation: Prolonged corpus luteum activity extends progesterone secretion beyond the normal 14-day lifespan of the corpus luteum. This delayed progesterone withdrawal delays the onset of organized endometrial shedding. When shedding finally occurs, it is prolonged and irregular because different areas of the endometrium are at different stages. This is irregular shedding — diagnosed by biopsy on day 4–5 of menses showing mixed secretory and proliferative endometrium.
options: Extended progesterone secretion delays organised endometrial shedding
Corpus luteum produces excess oestrogen causing endometrial hyperplasia
Corpus luteum produces AMH preventing endometrial regeneration
Luteal progesterone excess inhibits spiral arteriole vasoconstriction
Extended corpus luteum life causes persistent secretory endometrium without shedding
questions.question: The endometrial basis for prolonged corpus luteum activity causing prolonged menstruation is BEST understood as:
The oocytes in the female fetus enter which stage of meiosis very early, and remain there until ovulation many years later?
questions.explanation: Oocytes enter prophase I of the first meiotic division very early in fetal development, specifically arresting at the diplotene stage of prophase I. They remain in this suspended state ('dictyotene' arrest) until ovulation occurs decades later, when the LH surge triggers completion of meiosis I and the secondary oocyte is released. Meiosis II is completed only at fertilization.

questions.question: Which postoperative complication is characteristically associated with prolonged immobility, pelvic surgery, and cancer?
questions.explanation: Pulmonary embolism arising from deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is characteristically associated with the Virchow's triad: stasis (immobility, pelvic compression), hypercoagulability (cancer), and endothelial injury (surgery). Cancer patients undergoing pelvic surgery have a significantly elevated risk and require extended thromboprophylaxis.

options: Pelvic adhesions and tubal scarring causing tubal occlusion or dysfunction
Ovarian failure from inflammatory cytokine toxicity to oocytes
Cervical stenosis from repeated mucosal inflammation blocking sperm entry
Hypothalamic suppression from chronic pelvic pain reducing GnRH pulsatility
questions.question: Which complication of untreated chlamydia/gonorrhoea-related PID is MOST directly responsible for secondary infertility?
questions.explanation: The most important long-term consequence of inadequately treated or recurrent PID is tubal factor infertility from peritubal adhesions and intraluminal scarring of the fallopian tube epithelium. Inflammatory cell infiltration, followed by fibrosis during healing, distorts tubal architecture and impairs both sperm and ovum transport. A single episode of PID causes tubal factor infertility in approximately 10–15% of affected women; three or more episodes increase this risk to over 50%.

questions.question: A 60-year-old woman with a serous ovarian cystadenocarcinoma has tumour involving both ovaries but confined to the pelvis with malignant ascites present. This is classified as which FIGO stage?
questions.explanation: Bilateral ovarian involvement together with malignant ascites or positive peritoneal washings, without extension beyond the ovaries, is classified as Stage IC ovarian cancer, reflecting a higher risk of recurrence than Stage IA or IB disease confined without ascitic involvement.

options: The upper vagina from Müllerian ducts
The hymen from the Müllerian tubercle
questions.explanation: The sinovaginal bulbs are solid outgrowths from the urogenital sinus that contact the caudal end of the fused Müllerian ducts (Müllerian tubercle). They proliferate to form the vaginal plate, which subsequently canalizes from below upwards to form the lower vagina. The current consensus is that the upper vagina is of Müllerian origin and the lower vagina (from the vaginal plate) is of urogenital sinus origin.
questions.question: The sinovaginal bulbs are solid outgrowths from the urogenital sinus that contribute to the formation of:

questions.explanation: Among the diagnostic rules for DUB, considering coagulopathy is explicitly listed: Von Willebrand disease, leukaemia, aplastic anaemia, and idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) are all systemic coagulation disorders that can cause or exacerbate uterine bleeding. These must be actively excluded — particularly in adolescents where coagulopathy accounts for 20% of DUB cases. Missing a coagulopathy results in inadequate treatment directed solely at the uterus while the underlying disorder continues.
questions.question: When considering pelvic lesions in DUB, which of the following is cited as a condition that should be actively excluded?
In ovarian cancer, the most important prognostic factor after complete staging is:
questions.explanation: Residual tumour volume after primary cytoreductive surgery is the single most important prognostic factor in ovarian cancer. Optimal debulking—leaving no residual disease or tumour less than 1 cm—significantly improves response to chemotherapy and overall survival compared to suboptimal cytoreduction.

Cystoscopy is specifically indicated pre-operatively to look at the interior lining of the bladder and urethra. It is included in pre-operative investigations for surgical correction of prolapse. IVP shows the upper urinary tract, urodynamic studies assess bladder function, and CT provides detailed pelvic anatomy, but only cystoscopy provides direct visualisation of the bladder mucosa.
questions.question: Which investigation in the workup of prolapse is specifically indicated to look at the interior lining of the bladder and urethra?
A woman with ovarian cancer presents with progressive dyspnoea and haemoptysis. The MOST likely site of metastasis causing these symptoms is:
questions.explanation: Pulmonary metastases from ovarian cancer can present with progressive dyspnoea, haemoptysis, and cough. Chest X-ray may show coin lesions or discrete rounded densities. Pleural effusion is also common. The lungs, vagina, liver, and brain are the most common sites of haematogenous metastasis.

options: Reduced efficacy in smokers above age 35
Substantially elevated risk of venous and arterial thromboembolism
Smoking causes early menopause making pills unnecessary
questions.question: A 38-year-old woman who smokes 20 cigarettes daily requests combined oral contraceptive pills. The MOST important basis for not prescribing this method is:
questions.explanation: In women over 35 who smoke, combined oral contraceptives are absolutely contraindicated (WHO MEC Category 4) because both estrogen and smoking are independent risk factors for arterial and venous thromboembolism. Their combination produces a synergistically elevated risk of myocardial infarction and stroke. Progestogen-only methods are safer alternatives.

questions.question: A couple has been trying for 2 years. The man's testicular examination reveals a soft left testicle smaller than the right. Which additional investigation would best assess whether this size discrepancy reflects impaired spermatogenic function?
questions.explanation: A smaller, softer testicle can reflect impaired spermatogenesis, which is best assessed functionally through semen analysis combined with serum FSH, since FSH rises when spermatogenic tissue is damaged due to loss of negative feedback (inhibin) from the testis. This combination helps distinguish primary testicular pathology from other causes of testicular asymmetry. Further imaging, such as scrotal ultrasound, may also be needed to characterise the structural abnormality.
options: Semen analysis and serum FSH level
Increase sexual experimentation and teenage pregnancy rates
Have no measurable effect on adolescent sexual behaviour
Increase STI rates by encouraging sexual activity through knowledge
Only benefit adolescents in high-income countries with liberal cultural norms
Delay sexual initiation, reduce risk behaviours, improve contraceptive use in adolescents
questions.question: Sexual health education that is comprehensive, age-appropriate, and evidence-based has been shown to:
questions.explanation: WHO and UNESCO reviews of comprehensive sexuality education (CSE) programmes consistently show that quality CSE delays age at first sexual intercourse, reduces the number of sexual partners, increases condom and contraceptive use, and does NOT increase sexual activity. These benefits are seen across cultural contexts including sub-Saharan Africa. Abstinence-only programmes show no evidence of delaying sexual initiation or reducing STI/pregnancy rates.

questions.question: Lichen sclerosus of the vulva is associated with an increased risk of:
questions.explanation: Lichen sclerosus is a chronic inflammatory dermatosis of the vulva associated with an approximately 4–5% lifetime risk of developing vulval squamous cell carcinoma via a non-HPV pathway. It typically presents in postmenopausal women with intense vulval pruritus and characteristic white, thinned, crinkled skin ('cigarette paper' appearance).

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the mechanism by which the TVT (tension-free vaginal tape) differs from traditional sling procedures?
options: TVT uses biological material while traditional slings use synthetic mesh
TVT is tension-free mid-urethral; traditional slings are bladder-neck with tension
TVT requires open abdominal surgery while traditional slings are vaginal
TVT compresses the urethra proximally, traditional slings support the bladder neck
TVT acts retropubically while traditional slings go through the obturator foramen
questions.explanation: Tension-free vaginal tape (TVT) differs from traditional sling procedures in that it is placed tension-free under the mid-urethra (not the bladder neck), relying on dynamic urethral compression only during increases in abdominal pressure. Traditional slings (using nylon, prolene, Teflon, mersilene mesh, or natural tissues like round ligament) may be placed under the bladder neck with intentional tension, using blind directed needles retropubically (e.g. Stamey procedure).

Physical signs of overflow incontinence include a palpable bladder (from chronic urinary retention) and leakage on elevation of the bladder base. This paradoxical leakage occurs because elevating the already overdistended bladder base increases intravesical pressure above the low urethral resistance, causing urine to leak. The bladder is palpable suprapubically when residual urine is substantial.
questions.question: A woman presents with a slow stream, hesitation, sensation of incomplete emptying, and a palpable bladder. Cystometry shows high residual urine. Which physical sign on examination of the bladder base would be characteristic?

questions.explanation: Epispadias (dorsal urethral opening) and hypospadias (ventral urethral opening) cause infertility through misdeposition of ejaculate away from the cervical os, classifying them under the emission/coital factor category. The sperm may be normal in number and motility, but physical inability to deposit semen near the cervix prevents fertilization. Treatment options include surgical correction or intrauterine insemination with self-collected sperm.
questions.question: A couple presents after 3 years of infertility. Investigation reveals the male has epispadias with misdeposited ejaculate. Under which aetiological category of male infertility does this fall?
Serum CA-125 positive predictive value when greater than 35 u/ml during second-look ovarian cancer surgery is:
questions.explanation: When CA-125 exceeds 35 u/ml, the positive predictive value for detecting residual disease at second-look surgery is 100%—disease was always detected. However, a negative CA-125 (below 35 u/ml) has a predictive value of only 56%, meaning disease was still found in 44% of cases at second-look surgery, limiting its use as a sole monitoring tool.

Krukenberg tumours are secondary (metastatic) ovarian tumours, most commonly arising from primary cancers of the stomach, colon, breast, or endometrium. They characteristically contain mucin-secreting signet ring cells and are often bilateral, representing haematogenous metastasis to the ovaries.
questions.question: The Krukenberg tumour of the ovary is best classified as:

questions.explanation: Approximately 50% of choriocarcinomas follow a term pregnancy, 25% follow molar pregnancies, and 25% follow other pregnancies (abortions, ectopics). This pattern is important clinically because choriocarcinoma should be considered even after a seemingly normal term delivery if unexplained haemorrhage or metastatic symptoms develop.
questions.question: What percentage of choriocarcinomas occur after a term pregnancy?
Vulval carcinoma in its usual clinical presentation is MOST common in which age group?
questions.explanation: Vulval carcinoma occurs predominantly in older, postmenopausal women over 60 years of age, often arising on a background of lichen sclerosus. However, a younger group in their 40s–50s exists with HPV-associated VIN progressing to carcinoma. Paget disease and melanoma also occur predominantly in older women.

Second-look laparotomy is performed after completion of primary treatment in patients with no clinical evidence of residual or recurrent disease. It assesses the true pathological status, guides decisions about further therapy, and identifies persistent microscopic disease that clinical examination and imaging may miss.
questions.question: A second-look laparotomy in ovarian cancer management is performed primarily to:
options: Resect residual disease not visible on imaging
Perform prophylactic oophorectomy of contralateral ovary

questions.explanation: At the extremes of maternal age, the excess abortions are euploid — meaning the fetal chromosomes are normal — suggesting maternal factors rather than genetic causes. These euploid abortions are associated with infections, uterine defects, cervical incompetence, immunological factors, and medical conditions. This distinction is clinically important because it directs investigation toward maternal rather than genetic aetiology.
questions.question: Autosomal trisomy is the most frequent chromosomal abnormality found in first-trimester spontaneous abortions, accounting for 50–60% of cases. However, in recurrent abortions in women at the extremes of reproductive age, most fetuses have a different chromosomal profile. What is this profile called?
The MOST important clinical distinction between primary and secondary vaginismus is:
options: Primary vaginismus is more severe and untreatable; secondary vaginismus is mild and self-resolving
Primary involves organic pathology; secondary is always psychogenic
Primary affects nulliparous women only; secondary affects parous women exclusively
Primary vaginismus has been lifelong; secondary developed after a period of painless penetration
Primary requires surgical treatment; secondary responds only to hormonal therapy
questions.explanation: Primary (lifelong) vaginismus: the woman has never been able to achieve comfortable vaginal penetration of any kind throughout her life. Secondary (acquired) vaginismus: the woman previously had painless penetration but subsequently developed involuntary vaginal muscle spasm. Secondary causes include childbirth trauma, sexual assault, painful infections, menopause-related atrophy, or surgical procedures. This distinction guides treatment approach and prognosis.

questions.question: A woman is found to have a pelvic mass and serum HCG of 150,000 mIU/ml. She has no history of recent pregnancy. What is the MOST likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: An extremely elevated HCG of 150,000 mIU/ml in a non-pregnant woman with a pelvic mass strongly suggests gestational trophoblastic disease or an HCG-secreting ovarian tumour (such as a germ cell tumour or epithelial tumour). This level far exceeds what would be expected in a luteal cyst or physiological state.

questions.question: A young woman on the etonogestrel implant reports new-onset acne and hirsutism 6 months after insertion. This is MOST likely explained by:
options: Systemic etonogestrel activating androgen receptors — a known androgenic side effect of this progestogen
Ovarian androgen overproduction triggered by ovulation suppression
Adrenal androgen excess from ACTH stimulation by implant-derived cortisol
Bacterial colonization of the insertion site releasing androgens systemically
Etonogestrel converting to testosterone in adipose tissue
questions.explanation: Etonogestrel has weak androgenic activity (being structurally derived from 19-nortestosterone). In susceptible women, this androgenic activity can manifest as acne, seborrhoea, and hirsutism. These side effects are less common with etonogestrel than with older progestogens but can occur. Management includes topical acne treatments; if troublesome, method change to a less androgenic or anti-androgenic option may be considered.

Adjuvant radiotherapy is most indicated in vulval carcinoma when inguinofemoral lymph nodes are positive for metastasis, particularly two or more positive nodes or with extracapsular spread. Radiotherapy to the groin and pelvis significantly reduces the risk of regional recurrence and improves survival in node-positive disease.
questions.question: Adjuvant radiotherapy in vulval carcinoma is most indicated when:
options: Excise gland; histology to exclude carcinoma
Inguinofemoral lymph nodes are positive for metastasis

questions.explanation: Menopause predisposes to prolapse primarily through oestrogen deficiency. Oestrogen maintains the collagen content, tone, and vascularity of the pelvic floor ligaments and muscles. Hypoestrogenism leads to atrophy and weakening of these structures. Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) is therefore used in management of minor prolapse, especially in post-menopausal patients.
questions.question: What is the primary mechanism by which menopause predisposes to uterovaginal prolapse?
Which of the following statements about tumour markers in clinical practice is MOST accurate?
options: They are primary diagnostic tools replacing histology
Cannot serve as primary diagnostic tools
Most have high and variable specificity making them definitive tests
They are always cheap and widely available
A single marker can diagnose any gynaecological cancer
questions.explanation: Tumour markers cannot be constructed as primary modalities for cancer diagnosis. While they can detect tumour presence, monitor disease progression, and assess treatment response, their lack of universal specificity and sensitivity means they must always be used adjunctively alongside clinical examination, imaging, and histological confirmation.

Nigeria's current HIV PEP guidelines recommend tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) 300mg + emtricitabine (FTC) 200mg + dolutegravir (DTG) 50mg as the preferred 28-day PEP regimen. This regimen is well-tolerated, has a low side-effect profile, and achieves rapid plasma levels. It must be initiated within 72 hours of exposure and taken for the full 28 days. Follow-up HIV testing at 6 weeks, 3 months, and 6 months is required.
questions.question: Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) for HIV uses a 28-day course of antiretrovirals. The combination MOST commonly recommended in Nigeria's current guidelines is:
The operation of trachelorrhaphy is specifically indicated for treatment of which cervical condition?
questions.explanation: Cervical ectropion is eversion of the cervical lips following bilateral lacerations. It often causes mucoid discharge and cervical incompetence leading to mid-trimester abortions and premature delivery. The specific surgical treatment is trachelorrhaphy, which reconstructs the cervical lips. This is distinct from cervical erosion, which is managed with cauterization or cryosurgery.

questions.question: Caution regarding which two structures is explicitly mentioned when performing surgery for cervical leiomyomas?
options: Inferior epigastric vessels and round ligament
questions.explanation: Surgery for cervical leiomyomas requires specific caution regarding the ureters and bladder because of their anatomical proximity to the cervix. The ureter runs in the parametrium 1.5 cm from the cervix and can be easily injured during dissection of cervical fibroids. Bladder injury is also a risk due to the adherent relationship between the cervix and bladder base.

questions.question: A woman is scheduled for immediate primary repair of a 3rd degree perineal tear sustained during vaginal delivery. Which anaesthetic technique is generally preferred to ensure adequate access and sphincter relaxation for this repair?
options: No anaesthesia is required at all
Regional or general anaesthesia for adequate relaxation
questions.explanation: Repair of a 3rd degree perineal tear requires adequate muscle relaxation and pain control to allow precise identification and layered repair of the anal sphincter complex, which is best achieved with regional or general anaesthesia rather than local infiltration alone. Adequate exposure and a relaxed sphincter facilitate accurate apposition of torn ends. This improves the likelihood of good functional outcome and continence.

options: Spiral arteriole vasoconstriction causing ischaemia and shedding
Rupture of the basal arteries of the endometrium
Venous thrombosis in the endometrial stroma
Increased capillary permeability from prostaglandin E2
questions.explanation: The key vascular event in menstruation is vasoconstriction of the spiral arterioles, which causes endometrial ischaemia, stasis, white cell infiltration, interstitial haemorrhage, and eventual shedding of the functionalis layer. This vasoconstriction is mediated by the withdrawal of oestrogen and progesterone, which removes the vasodilatory influence. After initial vasoconstriction and shedding, oestrogen-induced vasoconstriction, tissue repair, and clot formation arrest bleeding.
questions.question: The key event in menstruation at the vascular level is:

questions.explanation: Primary syphilis is characterized by the appearance of a painless, indurated genital ulcer (the Treponema pallidum chancre) at the site of inoculation, with associated non-tender regional lymphadenopathy. The chancre heals spontaneously within 3–6 weeks, even without treatment, giving a false sense of recovery before secondary syphilis develops. The painlessness distinguishes it from other causes of genital ulcer (herpes, chancroid).
options: Multiple painful ulcers, purulent discharge, and inguinal buboes
Genital warts, dyspareunia, and post-coital bleeding
Diffuse maculopapular rash, oral ulcers, and alopecia
Painless genital ulcer, regional lymphadenopathy, and spontaneous resolution
questions.question: The classic triad of primary syphilis consists of:

options: Surgery at age 12 causes permanent damage to the vas deferens
The testicular blood-testis barrier matures before orchidopexy reversal
Orchidopexy sutures obstruct the epididymal lumen
Late orchidopexy causes anti-sperm antibody formation
Prolonged exposure to intra-abdominal temperature damages spermatogonial stem cells irreversibly
questions.explanation: Undescended testes are exposed to intra-abdominal temperature (2–4°C above scrotal temperature) during the critical window of neonatal spermatogonial development (within the first year of life). Prolonged heat exposure irreversibly damages spermatogonial stem cells and the supporting Sertoli cell architecture. Early orchidopexy (ideally 6–12 months) prevents this thermal damage; delayed surgery at age 12 is insufficient to reverse years of heat-related germ cell loss.
questions.question: A man with a history of bilateral undescended testes corrected by orchidopexy at age 12 presents with infertility. Semen analysis shows severe oligospermia. Orchidopexy at age 12 is late; the recommended age for orchidopexy is within the first year of life. Why does delayed orchidopexy lead to persistent impaired spermatogenesis?

questions.explanation: A 2nd degree tear involves the perineal muscles and skin but the anal sphincter complex remains intact. This distinguishes it from a 3rd degree tear, where the external anal sphincter is disrupted. Correct classification determines whether specialist repair in theatre is required.
questions.question: A woman sustains a tear during vaginal delivery that disrupts the perineal body but spares the anal sphincter complex on examination. Which structure remains intact to differentiate this from a 3rd degree tear?

questions.explanation: Gonococcal resistance to penicillins, fluoroquinolones (ciprofloxacin), and some cephalosporins has made ceftriaxone the last reliable first-line treatment. Current WHO and national guidelines recommend intramuscular ceftriaxone 500mg as a single dose. Dual therapy with azithromycin was previously recommended but was discontinued in many guidelines due to emerging azithromycin resistance. Pharyngeal gonorrhoea is harder to eradicate and may require different regimens.
questions.question: Gonorrhoea, caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae, is MOST accurately described regarding its antibiotic management in 2024 as:
options: Adequately treated with a single dose of oral amoxicillin
Best managed with oral doxycycline monotherapy for 7 days
Sensitive to penicillin in over 90% of isolates in sub-Saharan Africa
Treated identically regardless of site of infection (genital, rectal, pharyngeal)
Treated with intramuscular ceftriaxone 500mg single dose due to widespread resistance
Isolated hyperprolactinaemia as the sole cause
Primary hypothyroidism as the sole cause
Hyperinsulinaemia driving excess ovarian androgen production
questions.question: A 34-year-old presents with 3 years of primary infertility, irregular cycles, and elevated serum androgens with a polycystic appearance on ultrasound. Which underlying endocrine abnormality is most characteristic of this presentation?
questions.explanation: Polycystic ovary syndrome is characteristically associated with insulin resistance and compensatory hyperinsulinaemia, which stimulates excess ovarian androgen production and disrupts normal follicular development, leading to irregular cycles and anovulatory infertility. This distinguishes it from other endocrine causes of infertility, though hyperprolactinaemia and thyroid dysfunction should still be excluded as part of a complete workup. Weight management and insulin-sensitising agents such as metformin are often used alongside ovulation induction in management.

questions.question: A patient who had a total abdominal hysterectomy 48 hours ago develops frank haematuria and pain in the right flank. The MOST likely diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Frank haematuria with flank pain at 48 hours after a total abdominal hysterectomy strongly suggests ureteric injury (ligature, kinking, or transection). The ureter is at particular risk during hysterectomy near the uterine artery crossing and at the pelvic brim. Urgent imaging (CT urogram or IVU) and urology consultation are required.

options: Maternal prolactin receptors downregulate after 6 months
Infant digestive maturity changes breast milk composition suppressing LAM
Supplementary feeding reduces suckling frequency, restoring GnRH pulsatility and ovulation
Ovarian follicles become resistant to prolactin inhibition over time
Breast milk fat content decreases below the threshold needed for contraceptive effect
questions.question: LAM is considered highly effective (>98%) ONLY if the infant is under 6 months of age. The MAIN reason effectiveness declines after 6 months is:
questions.explanation: After 6 months, most infants begin supplementary feeds (WHO-recommended complementary feeding), which reduces the frequency and duration of suckling. This decrease in nipple stimulation lowers prolactin levels and restores hypothalamic GnRH pulsatility, allowing follicular development and ovulation to resume. The contraceptive effect of LAM is directly dependent on sustained suckling frequency.

DMPA-associated weight gain is real but variable. Some users (particularly adolescents, those with overweight/obesity at initiation) experience clinically meaningful weight gain. Proposed mechanisms include DMPA's stimulatory effect on appetite and lipogenesis. However, many users do not gain significant weight. The key clinical approach is pre-counselling about the possibility of weight gain, monitoring at follow-up visits, and switching methods if weight gain becomes a concern.
options: Universal and inevitable — all DMPA users gain 5–10kg per year
Exclusively fluid retention from mineralocorticoid activity resolving upon discontinuation
A myth with no evidence base — studies show DMPA does not affect weight
Variable — some women experience meaningful weight gain, possibly related to increased appetite and lipogenic effects; others do not
Exclusively affecting adolescents and women with pre-existing obesity
questions.question: Weight gain attributed to DMPA (Depo-Provera) use is MOST accurately described as:

questions.explanation: Risk-reducing bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy substantially reduces ovarian and fallopian tube cancer risk in BRCA1 mutation carriers and is recommended once childbearing is complete, typically around age 35-40 for BRCA1. Hysterectomy alone does not address ovarian or tubal cancer risk, the primary concern in this mutation. Screening with CA-125 and ultrasound has not proven effective for early detection in this high-risk population, making risk-reducing surgery the preferred strategy.
questions.question: A woman with a strong family history of ovarian and breast cancer tests positive for a BRCA1 mutation. Which risk-reducing surgical intervention is MOST strongly recommended after completion of childbearing?

questions.explanation: Duloxetine (40 mg twice daily) is the first and only drug licensed specifically for moderate to severe SUI. It works by blocking the reuptake of serotonin and noradrenaline in the sacral spinal cord, believed to increase pudendal nerve activity, thereby increasing external urethral sphincter contraction strength and reducing stress urinary incontinence symptoms. Anticholinergics (oxybutynin, probanthine) are used for urge incontinence.
options: Blocking muscarinic receptors in the detrusor muscle
Stimulating alpha-adrenergic receptors in the bladder neck
Directly relaxing the urethral smooth muscle
questions.question: Duloxetine for stress urinary incontinence works primarily by which pharmacological mechanism?

questions.explanation: Uterovaginal prolapse is graded based on descent relative to the ischial spines and introitus. In 1st degree, the cervix descends below the ischial spine but remains within the vagina. In 2nd degree, the cervix reaches the introitus. In 3rd degree, the entire uterus protrudes beyond the introitus, while 4th degree (procidentia) involves the full vaginal wall.
options: Cervix descends below the ischial spine
Entire uterus protrudes beyond the introitus
Uterus descends with cervix at introitus level
Only the cervix comes through the introitus
questions.question: Which of the following accurately describes a 3rd degree uterovaginal prolapse?

options: Remove the entire uterus and prevent all future bleeding
Destroy the basalis layer to prevent endometrial regeneration
Correct the hormonal imbalance driving DUB
Remove endometrial polyps causing the bleeding
Sterilize the patient as a side effect
questions.question: Endometrial ablation as treatment for DUB aims to:
questions.explanation: Endometrial ablation destroys the basal layer of the endometrium (from which regeneration occurs) using laser (Nd:YAG), thermal balloon, or hysteroscopic transcervical resection (TCRE). It results in complete amenorrhoea in approximately 50% of women and reduced bleeding in about 90%. It is more conservative than hysterectomy. Best results occur with pre-treatment endometrial suppression (GnRH analogues, danazol, or MPA for 4–6 weeks) to thin the endometrium before ablation.

questions.question: A woman with an unstable bladder is asked about associated symptoms using the 'FUN' mnemonic taught in clinical assessment. Beyond frequency and urgency, which additional symptom completes this mnemonic?
questions.explanation: The FUN mnemonic for detrusor instability symptoms stands for Frequency, Urgency, and Nocturia, reflecting the classic triad of an overactive bladder. Recognising this pattern on history helps distinguish overactive bladder from stress incontinence, which lacks these irritative symptoms. Nocturia in particular reflects reduced functional bladder capacity or overactivity occurring even during sleep.

questions.question: The Billings Ovulation Method relies PRIMARILY on observation of:
questions.explanation: The Billings Ovulation Method (BOM) teaches women to identify fertile and infertile phases exclusively through daily observation of cervical mucus characteristics. Fertile mucus is clear, slippery, and elastic (like raw egg white), indicating approaching ovulation. Infertile mucus is thick, cloudy, and scant or absent. No other parameters are measured in the pure Billings method.
options: Basal body temperature changes throughout the cycle
Changes in cervical mucus consistency and appearance
Calendar calculation of expected ovulation based on previous cycle lengths
Urinary LH surge detected by home test kits

questions.explanation: Stanzolol is an anabolic steroid listed specifically for the treatment of established osteoporosis in menopausal women, as it has anabolic (androgenic) effects that increase total body calcium and bone mass in patients who already have osteoporosis. It is not first-line therapy (bisphosphonates and oestrogens are preferred) but is an option when other treatments fail or are contraindicated. Its androgenic side effects (virilization) limit its use in women.
questions.question: Stanzolol is an anabolic steroid listed for treatment of which specific menopausal complication?

questions.explanation: Urine cytology examines cells exfoliated from the urothelium into the urine, making it particularly useful for detecting or monitoring urothelial (bladder) malignancy, especially in patients with haematuria or a history of bladder cancer. It is not used for cervical or ovarian pathology, which require different sampling techniques. It complements cystoscopy in the urological workup of suspected bladder tumours.
questions.question: Urine cytology is listed as a possible specimen source in cytological examination. For which clinical scenario would examination of exfoliated cells in urine be most specifically useful?
options: Screening or surveillance for urothelial (bladder) malignancy

questions.explanation: Krukenberg tumours are bilateral metastatic ovarian tumours containing signet-ring mucin-producing cells, classically originating from a gastric primary. They may also arise from colon or breast primaries, but gastric origin is the most typical.
questions.question: Krukenberg tumours of the ovary are MOST characteristically metastatic from which primary site?

options: Relatively low hCG levels despite significant tumour bulk
Markedly elevated hCG proportional to tumour size
questions.explanation: Placental site trophoblastic tumour arises from intermediate trophoblast and secretes relatively little hCG compared with the tumour bulk, in contrast to choriocarcinoma where hCG levels closely reflect disease burden, making hCG a less reliable marker in this variant.
questions.question: Placental site trophoblastic tumour is distinguished from choriocarcinoma by which biochemical feature?

options: Medial aspect of the dominant upper arm, subdermally
Abdominal subcutaneous tissue, superior to the umbilicus
Inner aspect of the non-dominant upper arm, subdermally
questions.explanation: Nexplanon is inserted subdermally in the inner aspect of the non-dominant upper arm, approximately 8–10 cm above the medial epicondyle of the humerus, in the sulcus between the biceps and triceps muscles. Using the non-dominant arm minimizes interference with daily activities. The subdermal (not intramuscular or deep subcutaneous) position is critical for correct release kinetics and for palpability and later removal.
questions.question: The subdermal etonogestrel implant (Nexplanon) is inserted in which ANATOMICAL location?
Leiomyosarcoma of the uterus presents suspicion when a presumed fibroid undergoes which change?
questions.explanation: Leiomyosarcoma should be suspected when a presumed uterine fibroid shows rapid growth with increasing pain after menopause, since benign fibroids normally remain unchanged or shrink after menopause. Leiomyosarcomas grow more rapidly, are softer than fibroids, and have haemorrhagic areas and degenerative softening on cut surface.

An ectopic ureter opening into the upper vagina allows a continuous leak of urine into the vagina, producing true incontinence (constant wetness) rather than the intermittent leakage of stress incontinence. Remarkably, this condition is often not diagnosed until age 10–13, when pelvic floor maturation at puberty makes the leak more apparent and the patient is presented for 'persistent bedwetting.' The normal urethra is present, so voiding also occurs normally.
options: Primary amenorrhoea with normal secondary sexual characteristics
questions.question: An ectopic ureter that opens into the upper vagina most characteristically causes:

options: Colles' (forearm) ? Vertebral crush ? Neck of femur
Neck of femur ? Colles' ? Vertebral crush fractures
Vertebral crush ? Colles' ? Neck of femur
Colles' ? Neck of femur ? Vertebral crush
Vertebral crush ? Neck of femur ? Colles'
questions.question: The long-term effects of osteoporosis at menopause include three specific fracture types listed in order of increasing morbidity and mortality. Rank these from LOWEST to HIGHEST morbidity:
questions.explanation: The three osteoporotic fracture types in ascending order of morbidity and mortality are: Colles' (distal radius/forearm fracture — relatively low morbidity, good functional recovery), vertebral crush fractures (causing progressive height loss of 10–12cm and chronic back pain — moderate morbidity), and neck of femur fractures (highest morbidity and mortality — up to 20–30% die within 1 year from complications). This sequence is specifically taught in menopause management.

questions.question: Para-urethral injection of collagen in the treatment of stress incontinence works by which mechanism?
questions.explanation: Para-urethral injection of collagen stimulates fibrin formation around the urethra, augmenting urethral coaptation and closure pressure. This injectable therapy is an option for stress urinary incontinence in patients unfit for or unwilling to undergo surgery, or as adjunctive treatment. It is distinct from sling operations (which create a suburethral hammock) and colposuspension (which suspends the vaginal wall).

options: Any GTD in women over 30 years
questions.question: In the surgical management of GTD, hysterectomy is specifically indicated for which form of disease?
questions.explanation: Hysterectomy is the treatment of choice for placental site trophoblastic tumour (PSTT) because it is relatively resistant to chemotherapy. Hysterectomy is also indicated in invasive mole in women who have completed their family and for uncontrollable haemorrhage, tumour perforation, or septicaemia in other GTD.

questions.question: Which ovarian tumour marker is MOST useful for monitoring treatment response in a young woman with a dysgerminoma?
questions.explanation: Dysgerminomas characteristically produce elevated lactate dehydrogenase, making it the preferred marker for monitoring disease activity and treatment response. CA-125 lacks specificity for germ cell tumours, while alpha-fetoprotein is more typical of yolk sac elements.

questions.question: The MOST important predictor of continued and correct use of a chosen contraceptive method is:
questions.explanation: Continuation and correct use of contraception are most strongly influenced by individualised counselling that addresses a person's specific needs, concerns, and lifestyle, allowing an informed choice that they are more likely to sustain, rather than the characteristics of any single method in isolation.
options: The cost of the method alone
Availability of the method in pharmacies
General popularity of the method locally
Counselling that matches the method to individual needs

questions.question: During parturition, the pubococcygeus muscle assists in which of the following sequence of actions?
options: Supports and guides the fetal head
Compresses the fetal head against the pelvic brim
Tightens the vaginal canal to slow descent
Prevents engagement of the fetal head
questions.explanation: During parturition, the pubococcygeus muscles perform three sequential functions: they help support the head of the baby, help guide the head towards the vaginal canal, and help in the expulsion of the fetus. This active muscular contribution is critical to normal vaginal delivery mechanics.

Torsion of an ovarian cyst presents as acute or subacute pain, which may be accompanied by mild shock. The lower abdomen is tender with guarding and rigidity, and pelvic examination reveals a tender adnexal mass. Laparotomy is indicated and removal of the affected ovary is usually necessary.
questions.question: Torsion of an ovarian cyst classically presents with:
options: Gradual onset of dull pelvic pain

questions.question: A woman undergoes induced abortion at 8 weeks using misoprostol intravaginally. Two days later she presents with incomplete expulsion. Mifepristone was combined with misoprostol for this patient. Which mechanism makes the combination more effective than misoprostol alone?
options: Mifepristone enhances cervical prostaglandin E2 metabolism
Mifepristone inhibits hCG production from trophoblast
questions.explanation: Mifepristone competitively blocks progesterone receptors, leading to decidual degeneration and increased myometrial sensitivity to prostaglandins, making the subsequently administered misoprostol far more effective at inducing uterine contractions and expulsion. The combination achieves >95% complete abortion rate compared to approximately 80–85% with misoprostol alone. This synergistic mechanism forms the basis of the gold-standard medical abortion regimen.

questions.question: Dilatation and curettage (D&C) for DUB has higher sensitivity than office endometrial biopsy. Which lesion does BOTH methods FAIL to detect, requiring hysteroscopy?
questions.explanation: Both blind D&C and office endometrial biopsy (Vabra) fail to detect focal lesions such as endometrial polyps and submucous fibroids, because these instruments sample tissue blindly and may miss lesions between the curette strokes. Hysteroscopy directly visualises the endometrial cavity and can identify, locate, and allow targeted biopsy of polyps and fibroids. This is a major advantage of hysteroscopy over D&C in the investigation of DUB.

Normal mature squamous epithelium is rich in glycogen, which binds iodine to produce a mahogany-brown colour, whereas dysplastic or neoplastic epithelium has reduced glycogen content and therefore fails to stain, appearing pale against the surrounding tissue. This iodine-negative area helps direct the colposcopist to the site for biopsy. It is a useful adjunct to acetic acid colposcopy.
options: Abnormal areas are always ulcerated and cannot retain stain
Abnormal cells have excess glycogen that repels iodine
Normal cells lack nuclei so cannot bind iodine
Iodine reacts only with keratin in normal cells
Dysplastic and neoplastic cells contain little or no glycogen
questions.question: During Schiller's test, normal glycogen-rich squamous epithelium stains dark brown with Lugol's iodine, while abnormal areas remain unstained. What is the underlying biochemical reason for this difference?
A woman with a large ovarian fibroma is found to have ascites and a right pleural effusion, both of which resolve after tumour removal. What is this clinical triad MOST correctly termed?
questions.explanation: Meigs syndrome describes the triad of a benign ovarian fibroma with ascites and pleural effusion, both of which characteristically resolve following surgical removal of the tumour, distinguishing it from malignant causes of similar fluid accumulation. Recognising this benign entity avoids unnecessary aggressive treatment when the underlying tumour is confirmed benign on histology. The pathophysiology involves transudation of fluid from the tumour surface with transdiaphragmatic passage into the pleural space.

questions.question: A surgeon preparing for manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) for incomplete abortion notes the gestational age is 18 weeks. Which surgical alternative for incomplete abortion at this gestational age is SPECIFICALLY listed in the curriculum materials?
questions.explanation: Dilation and evacuation (D&E) is the surgical method specifically indicated for second-trimester induced or incomplete abortion, as standard MVA or D&C instruments cannot adequately remove the larger second-trimester products. D&E requires greater cervical dilation and use of larger forceps or suction cannulae. It is listed alongside hysterotomy and hysterectomy as methods for second-trimester surgical abortion.

questions.question: WHO defines dysplasia of the cervix as a lesion in which part of the thickness of the epithelium is replaced by cells showing varying degrees of atypia. In severe dysplasia, how much of the epithelial thickness is involved?
questions.explanation: CIN is classified by the extent of epithelial involvement: CIN I (mild) involves the lower one-third, CIN II (moderate) involves the lower two-thirds, and CIN III (severe dysplasia/carcinoma-in-situ) involves all three-thirds of the epithelial thickness. Features include loss of polarity, nuclear enlargement with irregular dark staining, mitoses, and disparity in cytoplasm ratio.

questions.question: A 17-year-old girl has primary amenorrhoea with normal secondary sexual characteristics. Examination reveals a normal vulva but a blind-ending vaginal pouch. Karyotype is 46,XX. The MOST likely diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: A blind-ending vaginal pouch with normal secondary sexual characteristics, normal female karyotype (46,XX), and primary amenorrhoea is the classic presentation of MRKH syndrome. Normal oestrogen production from normal ovaries drives secondary sexual development. The absence of a cervix and uterus (Müllerian agenesis) causes the blind-ending vagina and primary amenorrhoea. CAIS has XY karyotype, and Turner's has XO karyotype with absent secondary development.

questions.question: A 19-year-old nulliparous woman requesting a copper IUD is often perceived by providers as having increased difficulty of insertion primarily due to which factor?
questions.explanation: Nulliparous women may have a smaller uterine cavity and a tighter cervical os, which can make insertion technically more challenging or uncomfortable, though nulliparity itself is not a contraindication, and IUDs remain a safe and effective option for this group with appropriate technique.
options: A smaller or more tightly closed cervical os
Increased risk of malignancy at this age
Contraindication of IUDs in all nulliparous women
Reduced motivation to use the method effectively

questions.question: A 20-year-old male (XY) has co-existing Müllerian and Wolffian derived internal structures and normal male external genitalia. The MOST likely underlying defect is:
questions.explanation: The combination of normal male external genitalia (indicating normal testosterone and DHT), normal Wolffian-derived structures, and persistent Müllerian structures (uterus and fallopian tubes) points to deficient AMH production or AMH receptor mutation. AMH is required to cause Müllerian regression; without it, Müllerian structures persist alongside otherwise normally virilized male. This is the hallmark of Persistent Müllerian Duct Syndrome.

questions.question: Ascites associated with ovarian tumours is MOST likely a sign of:
questions.explanation: Ascites in the context of an ovarian tumour is usually a sign of peritoneal metastasis, particularly if the fluid is blood-stained. However, Meigs syndrome (fibroma with benign ascites and pleural effusion) must always be remembered as a benign cause of ascites with an adnexal mass.

questions.question: HCG can be detected in pregnancy at the earliest:
questions.explanation: HCG can be detected in pregnancy one day after implantation, approximately 8 days after ovulation and 9 days after the LH surge. This early detectability makes hCG the basis for pregnancy testing and the primary monitoring tool in GTD. It rises exponentially until 9–10 weeks with a doubling time of 1.3–2 days.

Early mobilisation improves venous return, reducing stasis-related thromboembolism, and promotes better lung expansion, lowering the risk of atelectasis and pneumonia, both of which are significant contributors to postoperative morbidity if patients remain immobile for prolonged periods.
questions.question: Early postoperative mobilisation after gynaecological surgery is encouraged primarily to reduce the risk of:

questions.explanation: The elevated intra-abdominal pressure of CO2 pneumoperitoneum (typically 12–15 mmHg) compresses the inferior vena cava, reducing venous return and cardiac output. Combined with hypercapnia (CO2 absorption), which causes cardiovascular stimulation (tachycardia, hypertension), the net cardiovascular effect can be deleterious in patients with limited cardiac reserve. This is the physiological basis for cardiopulmonary disease being a relative contraindication to laparoscopy.
options: Increased cardiac output from Trendelenburg position
Hypertension from aortic compression by gas
Bradycardia from CO2-mediated vagal stimulation only
Reduced venous return from abdominal pressure
questions.question: Laparoscopy uses CO2 pneumoperitoneum which has systemic effects. Which cardiovascular effect of CO2 pneumoperitoneum is most clinically significant?
A woman with sickle cell disease undergoing major gynaecological surgery requires which specific perioperative precaution to reduce complication risk?
questions.explanation: Patients with sickle cell disease are at increased risk of perioperative vaso-occlusive crisis, so maintaining adequate hydration, oxygenation, warmth, and acid-base balance throughout the perioperative period is essential to minimise sickling and associated complications during major surgery.
options: Preoperative blood transfusion is always mandatory regardless of haemoglobin level
Delay of surgery until adulthood only
Adequate hydration, oxygenation, and avoidance of hypothermia

questions.question: The role of leukotrienes in IUCD-related menorrhagia is BEST explained by:
options: Leukotriene B4 directly causes uterine artery vasoconstriction
Leukotrienes stimulate prostaglandin F2a production, reducing blood loss
IUCDs directly activate the complement system causing leukotriene release
IUCD-driven leucocyte infiltration causing excess leukotriene production
questions.explanation: IUCDs cause excessive leucocyte infiltration of the endometrium as a foreign-body response. Since leukotrienes are produced by leucocytes, excessive infiltration leads to excess leukotriene production. The degree of IUCD-related menorrhagia is roughly proportional to the degree of leucocyte infiltration. Leukotrienes cause vasoconstriction followed by plasma leakage and extravasation of erythrocytes, contributing to increased bleeding. This is why NSAIDs and antifibrinolytics are effective for IUCD menorrhagia.

questions.question: What is the MOST accurate statement about the effectiveness of coitus interruptus (withdrawal) as commonly practised?
options: It is as effective as combined oral contraceptive pills with perfect use
It provides complete protection from sexually transmitted infections
It is no more effective than using no contraception
Its effectiveness is limited solely by timing errors, not pre-ejaculatory fluid
Typical-use failure rate is approximately 22 pregnancies per 100 women per year
questions.explanation: With typical use, withdrawal has a failure rate of approximately 22 per 100 women per year (22%), reflecting inconsistent or incorrect use including failure to withdraw fully before ejaculation. With perfect use, it improves to approximately 4%. Withdrawal provides no STI protection. While more effective than no method, it is substantially less effective than modern contraceptive methods.

questions.question: Incomplete (pseudoprecocious) puberty differs from true precocious puberty in that it occurs without:
questions.explanation: Incomplete (pseudoprecocious) puberty involves secondary sexual characteristics developing without full hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis activation and without ovulation. It results from sex steroid production independent of central control (e.g., from an autonomous ovarian cyst, adrenal tumour, exogenous oestrogen, or from peripheral aromatization of androgens). LH and FSH levels are low or suppressed in contrast to the elevated levels seen in true precocious puberty.

questions.question: Postoperative deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis with graduated compression stockings should be avoided in patients with which coexisting condition?
questions.explanation: Graduated compression stockings can further compromise arterial perfusion in patients with severe peripheral arterial disease, so their use is avoided or used with caution in this group, and alternative mechanical or pharmacological thromboprophylaxis methods are considered instead.

questions.question: The preferred treatment for a small volume CIN 3 lesion fully visible at colposcopy in a woman wishing to preserve fertility is:
options: Large loop excision of the transformation zone
questions.explanation: Large loop excision of the transformation zone removes the abnormal tissue while preserving the uterus and cervix, making it the treatment of choice for CIN 3 in women wishing to retain fertility. More radical procedures are reserved for invasive disease.

ICSI (intracytoplasmic sperm injection) involves direct microinjection of a single sperm into an oocyte, bypassing the requirement for normal sperm-egg interaction. It is the primary treatment for severe male factor infertility, including severe oligospermia, asthenospermia, and obstructive or non-obstructive azoospermia where sperm are retrieved surgically (TESE, MESA). ICSI has revolutionized male infertility treatment, enabling biological parenthood for men with near-absent sperm counts.
questions.question: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) is a form of ART used for which PRIMARY indication?
options: Endometrial receptivity failure after previous IVF

questions.question: A woman undergoes repeated dilatation and curettage procedures after a postpartum haemorrhage. She subsequently develops secondary amenorrhoea and cyclical pelvic pain. Hysteroscopy reveals intrauterine adhesions. What is this condition MOST correctly termed?
questions.explanation: Asherman syndrome describes intrauterine adhesions typically resulting from aggressive endometrial curettage, particularly after pregnancy-related procedures, leading to amenorrhoea, infertility, or cyclical pain from trapped menstrual blood behind adhesions. Mayer-Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser syndrome instead refers to congenital Mullerian agenesis, an unrelated developmental condition. Recognising the surgical history clue is key to distinguishing acquired adhesive disease from congenital anomalies.

options: Increasing chance of male sex outcome
Reducing risk of high-order multiple pregnancy
Reducing risk of ovarian hyperstimulation now
Reducing overall cost of the treatment cycle
Improving egg retrieval success rate later
questions.question: A woman undergoing in-vitro fertilisation has embryos created and is deciding on the number to transfer. Which factor MOST directly guides limiting the number of embryos transferred in a single cycle?
questions.explanation: Limiting the number of embryos transferred, often to a single embryo in favourable prognosis patients, is primarily aimed at reducing the risk of high-order multiple pregnancy, which carries substantial maternal and neonatal risks including preterm birth. This consideration is distinct from ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome, which relates to the stimulation phase rather than transfer number. Modern practice increasingly favours single embryo transfer with cryopreservation of remaining embryos for later use.

questions.question: A 33-year-old woman with a history of recurrent second-trimester miscarriage is planned for elective cervical cerclage in her current pregnancy. At what gestational age is this procedure typically performed?
questions.explanation: Elective cervical cerclage for a history of cervical incompetence is typically performed around 12 to 14 weeks gestation, early in the second trimester, before significant cervical shortening or dilatation has occurred, aiming to provide mechanical support to prevent recurrence of painless cervical dilatation and pregnancy loss. Performing the procedure at this earlier stage, rather than waiting for cervical changes to become apparent, is more likely to be successful. The suture is typically removed around 36 to 37 weeks to allow for normal labour and delivery.
options: Around 12 to 14 weeks, before further cervical shortening or dilatation occurs
Around 30 to 32 weeks, immediately before anticipated preterm labour
Only in the immediate postpartum period
Only after the cervix is already fully dilated

questions.question: The MOST common postoperative complication following major gynaecological surgery in the first 24 hours is:
questions.explanation: Primary haemorrhage (occurring within the first 24 hours of surgery) is the most serious and common early postoperative complication following major gynaecological surgery. It requires prompt recognition with resuscitation and return to theatre if haemostasis is inadequate. Vital signs, wound drains, and abdominal girth should be monitored closely in the initial recovery period.

questions.question: Primary repair of a 3rd degree perineal tear should be deferred if more than what time has elapsed after delivery?
questions.explanation: Primary repair of perineal lacerations must be done as soon as possible for satisfactory healing. Primary repair more than 12 hours after delivery is seldom successful, and repair should be deferred for 6 weeks. Primary repairs that break down, like lacerations seen too late for primary suture, should be deferred for 6-8 weeks after all local sepsis has subsided and tissues have returned to normal.

options: The sponge physically blocks the cervical os and continuously releases spermicide throughout the 24-hour period
The sponge alters cervical mucus pH making it permanently hostile to sperm
The sponge is made of hormonal material that prevents ovulation when inserted
Repeated insertion would cause toxic shock, so 24-hour continuous use is mandatory
The sponge has no spermicidal component and works by absorption only
questions.explanation: The contraceptive sponge (e.g., Today Sponge) works through three simultaneous mechanisms: physical barrier covering the cervix, continuous release of spermicide (N-9) from its core for 24 hours, and trapping/absorbing semen. Unlike the diaphragm, no additional spermicide is needed for subsequent acts of intercourse within 24 hours. However, it must remain in place for 6 hours after the last act.
questions.question: The sponge contraceptive method provides protection for multiple acts of intercourse within a 24-hour period WITHOUT requiring additional spermicide. This is because:
Secondary tumours to the fallopian tube most commonly originate from:
questions.explanation: Secondary (metastatic) tumours to the fallopian tube most commonly originate from ovarian cancer, followed by breast and GI tract primaries. This reflects the anatomical proximity and lymphatic connection between the ovary and tube. The distinction from primary fallopian tube cancer is important for staging and prognosis.

options: Aggressive tumour biology in Nigerian women
Lack of CA-125 test availability worldwide
High rates of BRCA mutations in Nigerian population
questions.explanation: In Nigeria, ovarian cancer patients often present with advanced disease due to a combination of poor health education, traditional and cultural beliefs that delay medical consultation, limited facilities for surgery and adjuvant therapy, and poverty. These socioeconomic factors significantly worsen outcomes.
questions.question: In the Nigerian clinical setting, which factor MOST contributes to late-stage presentation of ovarian cancer?

A 70-year-old presents with a persistent vulval ulcer and a palpable inguinal lymph node. Biopsy confirms squamous cell carcinoma of the vulva. Which lymphatic drainage pattern is MOST relevant to staging and surgical planning?
options: Primary drainage to internal iliac nodes only
Primary drainage to mesenteric nodes only
Primary drainage to obturator nodes only
questions.explanation: Vulval cancer characteristically drains first to the superficial and deep inguinofemoral lymph nodes before spreading further to pelvic nodes, making inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy or sentinel node biopsy central to staging and treatment planning. Cervical and endometrial cancers instead drain primarily to pelvic (obturator, internal iliac) and para-aortic nodes. This distinct lymphatic pathway explains the groin-focused surgical approach for vulval malignancy.

In CAIS (46,XY with androgen receptor mutation), the testes may be intra-abdominal or may descend into the inguinal canal or labia majora (following the route of testicular descent in males). They present as bilateral inguinal masses in phenotypic females. The combination of XY karyotype, female phenotype, primary amenorrhoea, and bilateral inguinal masses is pathognomonic for CAIS. The testes are histologically normal but will never descend further due to the female developmental environment.
questions.question: A 16-year-old girl presents with primary amenorrhoea and a normal female phenotype. On examination she has a 4 cm mass in each groin. Karyotype returns as 46,XY. The structure in each groin MOST likely represents:
options: Inguinal lymph nodes enlarged from infection
Testes retained in the inguinal canal

questions.explanation: Vulval pruritus (itching) of long duration is the most common presenting symptom of vulval carcinoma, often preceded by years of benign vulval disease such as lichen sclerosus. Many women delay presentation due to embarrassment, resulting in advanced disease at diagnosis. Ulceration and a visible lesion may follow the initial pruritic phase.
questions.question: The MOST common presenting symptom of vulval carcinoma is:

questions.explanation: Antiphospholipid syndrome is the most important treatable immunological cause of recurrent abortion and falls under the immunological factors category of euploid abortion aetiology. Antiphospholipid antibodies cause thrombosis of placental vessels, leading to placental insufficiency and fetal loss. Treatment with low-dose aspirin and low molecular weight heparin significantly improves pregnancy outcomes in this condition.
questions.question: A patient with recurrent abortion is found to have antiphospholipid syndrome. Which cause of euploid abortion does this represent?

A woman is being counselled about the difference between primary and secondary dysmenorrhoea before further evaluation. Which feature would MOST strongly suggest a secondary rather than primary cause?
options: Onset of pain many years after menarche
Pain accompanied by nausea and fatigue
Pain confined to the first two days of bleeding
Pain beginning within one year of menarche
questions.explanation: Primary dysmenorrhoea typically begins within one to two years of menarche once ovulatory cycles are established, whereas new-onset dysmenorrhoea appearing many years later suggests an underlying secondary cause such as endometriosis, adenomyosis, or fibroids requiring further investigation. Pain confined to early menses and response to NSAIDs are typical, reassuring features of primary dysmenorrhoea. Recognising this temporal pattern helps direct appropriately targeted evaluation.

questions.question: A smoker aged 38 who smokes fewer than 15 cigarettes daily requesting combined oral contraceptives is classified under which WHO MEC category?
options: Category 4 for all smokers regardless of age
questions.explanation: Women aged 35 or older who smoke, even fewer than 15 cigarettes daily, are classified as WHO MEC Category 3 for combined hormonal contraceptives, reflecting a risk that generally outweighs the advantages, whereas smokers under 35 fall into Category 2 for the same criterion.

A Day 21 serum progesterone level above 15 ng/mL (or 2–3 times the baseline of 3–6 ng/mL) is accepted as evidence of ovulation in a standard 28-day cycle. Levels below this suggest anovulation or inadequate corpus luteum function. If progesterone is normal but FSH should also be checked as it is more specific for confirming ovulation, particularly with borderline results.
questions.question: Mid-luteal serum progesterone is used to confirm ovulation. Which Day 21 progesterone level (in a 28-day cycle) is accepted as evidence of ovulation?

questions.explanation: A hallmark of adolescent psychology is the contradiction between perceiving themselves as grown up and still being in the process of mental and emotional development. This mismatch leads to impulsive decisions, including around sexual behaviour, that carry serious health consequences. Clinicians must understand this developmental dissonance to provide effective adolescent counselling.
questions.question: A 13-year-old girl is brought to clinic. Her mother is concerned about her 'grown-up' attitudes. Which feature is MOST characteristic of the adolescent psychological profile described in gynaecological teaching materials?
options: Fully mature judgment with adult decision-making
Stable emotional responses to peer interactions
Viewing themselves as grown while maturing
Reduced sexual awareness compared to adults

questions.question: A 45-year-old with multiple intramural fibroids and heavy bleeding has completed childbearing and wants definitive treatment. Which option offers the MOST definitive cure of her symptoms?
options: GnRH agonist therapy for six months
questions.explanation: Hysterectomy is the only definitively curative treatment for fibroid-related heavy bleeding since it removes the uterus entirely, eliminating any possibility of recurrence, making it appropriate for women who have completed childbearing. Myomectomy preserves fertility but carries a risk of fibroid recurrence. Embolisation and medical therapies reduce symptoms but do not guarantee permanent resolution.

questions.question: Ulipristal acetate as emergency contraception works primarily through which mechanism?
options: Producing an inflammatory reaction toxic to sperm
Inducing immediate menstruation regardless of cycle day
Delaying or inhibiting ovulation by acting on progesterone receptors
Thickening the endometrium to prevent implantation permanently
questions.explanation: Ulipristal acetate is a selective progesterone receptor modulator that primarily works by delaying or inhibiting ovulation, similar in principle to levonorgestrel emergency contraception but generally more effective when taken closer to the time of ovulation.

questions.question: During colpomicroscopy, which stains are applied to achieve higher magnification than colposcopy for cervical epithelium examination?
questions.explanation: Colpomicroscopy achieves higher magnification than the standard colposcope. The cervical epithelium is stained with Meyer haematoxylin or toluidine blue for examination. This technique allows more detailed cellular analysis than standard colposcopy. Other diagnostic colposcopy-related techniques include cervicography (hand-held 35mm camera photograph) and standard colposcopy with acetic acid application. SUBTOPIC 5: URINARY FISTULAE AND INCONTINENCE OF URINE
options: Nile Blue Sulphate and light green

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the FIGO staging of vulval carcinoma when inguinal lymph nodes are involved?
questions.explanation: FIGO Stage III vulval carcinoma includes tumour of any size with unilateral positive inguinofemoral regional lymph node metastasis. Stage IVA includes tumour invading adjacent structures (upper urethra, bladder, rectum, pelvic bone) or bilateral positive inguinal nodes.
