Disruption of this balance (e.g., by antibiotics or alkaline semen) predisposes to bacterial vaginosis, candidiasis, and other vaginal infections.

questions.question: Posterior colpo-perineorrhaphy is performed specifically for which compartment defect?
questions.explanation: Posterior colpo-perineorrhaphy is the surgical repair for rectocele and enterocele, which are posterior compartment defects. For cystocele and urethrocele (anterior compartment), anterior colporrhaphy is performed. Comprehensive pelvic floor repair during vaginal hysterectomy typically includes both anterior and posterior colporrhaphy to address all compartments.

questions.question: A patient is found to have genital herpes with HSV-2 on PCR. Which statement MOST accurately reflects the natural history of genital herpes?
questions.explanation: After primary HSV-2 infection, the virus establishes lifelong latency in the sacral dorsal root ganglia (S2–S4). Periodic reactivation (triggered by stress, fever, UV light, immunosuppression) causes recurrent genital lesions or, more commonly, asymptomatic viral shedding. Asymptomatic shedding is an important source of transmission. No currently available antiviral therapy eradicates the latent HSV reservoir.
options: After primary infection resolves, HSV-2 is completely eliminated from the body
HSV-2 infection provides immunity against future HSV-1 oro-labial herpes
HSV-2 recurrences decrease in frequency with time in immunocompetent individuals uniformly by Year 2
Antiviral therapy with aciclovir permanently eradicates HSV-2 from the sensory ganglia
HSV-2 establishes latency in dorsal root ganglia with periodic reactivation causing recurrent lesions or asymptomatic shedding

questions.explanation: Postoperative management after repair of a 3rd degree perineal tear includes confining the bowel for at least 6-7 days to allow the repair to consolidate without faecal stress. A low residue diet is continued, and digital examination and liquid paraffin are avoided. Antibiotics, twice-daily sitz baths, and effective analgesia are also prescribed to reduce infection, oedema, and discomfort.
questions.question: The postoperative care after repair of a 3rd degree perineal tear includes confining the bowel for at least how many days?

questions.explanation: Situational erectile difficulty that occurs only in specific circumstances, such as with a new partner, while normal erections occur during masturbation or with a familiar partner, strongly suggests a predominantly psychological cause, such as performance anxiety, rather than an organic physical cause.
options: An organic vascular cause of erectile dysfunction
Diabetes mellitus as the underlying cause
Neurological disease affecting the pelvic nerves
A predominantly psychological cause such as performance anxiety
questions.question: A young man reports consistent difficulty maintaining an erection only with a new partner but normal erections during masturbation. This pattern is MOST suggestive of:
The clinical significance of DUB in adolescents includes iron deficiency anaemia and coagulopathy in what percentage of affected adolescents?
options: 5% of affected adolescents have a coagulopathy
20% of affected adolescents have a coagulopathy
40% of affected adolescents have a coagulopathy
10% of affected adolescents have a coagulopathy
35% of affected adolescents have a coagulopathy
questions.explanation: Coagulopathy is found in approximately 20% of adolescents being treated for DUB, making it a critically important consideration in this age group. Von Willebrand disease is the most common such disorder. Iron deficiency anaemia is also a significant consequence of heavy menstrual bleeding in adolescents. These clinical sequelae underscore why DUB in adolescents should not be dismissed as simply 'normal for their age' without investigation.

Achieving and maintaining an undetectable viral load in the HIV-positive partner through effective antiretroviral therapy, combined with strategies such as timing intercourse to the fertile window, substantially reduces transmission risk to the uninfected partner while allowing natural conception.
questions.question: In a serodiscordant couple wishing to conceive where the male partner is HIV-positive, the strategy MOST likely to minimise transmission risk to the female partner is:
options: Delaying conception attempts until the female partner develops symptoms
Using only barrier contraception throughout the attempt to conceive
Achieving maternal viral suppression through effective antiretroviral therapy and timed intercourse
Conceiving only through unprotected intercourse without any preparation
Avoiding any form of antiretroviral therapy before conception

questions.question: Depot medroxyprogesterone acetate is administered as a deep intramuscular or subcutaneous injection at which interval to maintain contraceptive efficacy?
questions.explanation: Depot medroxyprogesterone acetate is given every 12 weeks, providing sustained progestogen levels sufficient to suppress ovulation throughout the injection interval, with a short grace period typically allowed before efficacy is considered compromised if the next dose is delayed.

questions.question: A 27-year-old woman with HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy asks about breastfeeding her newborn. Current guidance in many resource-limited settings supports that she may breastfeed provided she:
options: Breastfeeds without any antiretroviral therapy at all
Avoids exclusive breastfeeding in favour of mixed feeding
Stops antiretroviral therapy immediately after delivery
Breastfeeds only if her CD4 count is below 200
Continues antiretroviral therapy with sustained viral suppression throughout breastfeeding
questions.explanation: In many resource-limited settings, WHO guidance supports breastfeeding for women living with HIV who maintain effective antiretroviral therapy and viral suppression throughout the breastfeeding period, since this substantially reduces transmission risk while preserving the broader nutritional and health benefits of breastfeeding for the infant.

questions.question: A preliminary temporary colostomy before RVF repair is considered unnecessary when the RVF is located in which part of the vagina?
questions.explanation: A preliminary temporary colostomy may be required before RVF repair. It is unnecessary if the RVF is in the lower half of the vagina. It is a wise precaution in the case of high fistula greater than 1 cm in diameter. Transverse colostomy is preferred over iliac colostomy because it leaves the abdominal wall below the umbilicus clear for pelvic access and does not tether the pelvic colon.

questions.question: Vulval Paget disease differs from vulval intraepithelial neoplasia in that it:
questions.explanation: Vulval Paget disease is an intraepithelial adenocarcinoma arising from apocrine gland-bearing skin, and a proportion of cases are associated with an underlying invasive adenocarcinoma of the vulva or another site, distinguishing it biologically from HPV-related squamous vulval intraepithelial neoplasia.
options: Is always associated with high-risk HPV infection
Never recurs after wide local excision
Arises from apocrine gland-bearing skin and may indicate an underlying adenocarcinoma
Presents exclusively in women under thirty years old

questions.question: Granulosa cell tumours of the ovary are classified as sex cord stromal tumours and may produce oestrogen, causing postmenopausal bleeding. Their malignant potential is best described as:
options: Exclusively benign in reproductive age group
questions.explanation: Granulosa cell tumours belong to the granulosa-theca cell group of gonadal stromal tumours. They are not infrequently malignant but are usually low grade with an indolent course. Their oestrogenic effects cause precocious puberty in children, endometrial hyperplasia in premenopausal women, and postmenopausal bleeding in older women.

Caesarean scar ectopic pregnancy implants within the weakened, fibrous scar tissue of a previous uterine incision, carrying a high risk of invasion into the myometrium leading to uterine rupture and life-threatening haemorrhage as the pregnancy advances, requiring early diagnosis and specialist management. This risk profile differs substantially from tubal ectopic pregnancy, where rupture affects the fallopian tube rather than the uterine wall itself. Early recognition through targeted ultrasound in women with prior caesarean delivery is essential.
questions.question: A 38-year-old with three previous caesarean sections presents with a scar ectopic pregnancy diagnosed on early ultrasound. Why does this specific type of ectopic pregnancy carry a MOST particularly high risk of severe complication compared with tubal ectopic pregnancy?
options: Higher risk of chronic pelvic infection only
Higher risk of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome
Risk of uterine rupture and massive haemorrhage
Higher risk of subsequent tubal blockage
Higher risk of gestational trophoblastic disease

questions.question: Seminal fluid analysis is performed as part of a male infertility workup. Which combination of parameters is assessed to determine overall semen quality?
questions.explanation: Standard seminal fluid analysis assesses sperm concentration, motility, and morphology, along with volume and other basic parameters, providing the cornerstone initial investigation of male fertility potential. Abnormalities in any of these parameters can guide further, more specific investigation such as hormonal profiling or genetic testing. Repeat analysis is often recommended given natural variability in semen quality.

Ovulatory DUB occurs in mid-reproductive years (20s–30s) with regular cycles and confirmed ovulation. It is characterized by regular, predictable heavy periods, often with associated dysmenorrhoea and premenstrual symptoms (breast tenderness, bloating — from normal progesterone production). Anovulatory DUB produces irregular, unpredictable bleeding without premenstrual symptoms (as there is no corpus luteum and no progesterone). This distinction guides treatment: NSAIDs and antifibrinolytics work in ovulatory DUB.
questions.question: Which symptom pattern is MOST consistent with ovulatory DUB (as opposed to anovulatory DUB)?
options: Regular heavy cycles with premenstrual symptoms and confirmed ovulation
Irregular, unpredictable heavy bleeding without premenstrual symptoms
Absent periods for months followed by sudden heavy bleeding
Heavy bleeding beginning at menarche with no variation between cycles

questions.explanation: Pelvic inflammatory disease presents with lower abdominal/pelvic pain, cervical motion tenderness (pathognomonic), adnexal tenderness, fever, and abnormal discharge. It results from ascending infection by C. trachomatis, N. gonorrhoeae, or mixed anaerobes. Painless vulvar ulceration is the presentation of primary syphilis chancre — an entirely different condition. PID does not characteristically cause genital ulceration.
questions.question: PID (pelvic inflammatory disease) caused by an ascending STI is LEAST likely to produce which of the following clinical features?
options: Cervical motion tenderness on bimanual examination
Fever and raised inflammatory markers (CRP, ESR)
Abnormal vaginal discharge with positive NAAT for Chlamydia

questions.explanation: Lynch syndrome results from germline mutations in DNA mismatch repair genes such as MLH1 and MSH2, leading to microsatellite instability and a markedly increased lifetime risk of both colorectal and endometrial carcinoma.
questions.question: Lynch syndrome predisposes affected women to endometrial cancer through germline mutations in which class of genes?
options: Tumour suppressor genes controlling apoptosis alone

questions.explanation: Pseudomyxoma peritonei results from rupture of a mucinous tumour, usually of appendiceal origin, with diffuse mucinous ascites filling the peritoneal cavity. It requires aggressive cytoreductive surgery and is distinct from typical peritoneal carcinomatosis.
questions.question: A woman with a mucinous cystadenoma of the ovary undergoing surgery is found to have gelatinous material throughout the peritoneal cavity. This finding is termed:

questions.explanation: Urine-based nucleic acid amplification testing offers good sensitivity for detecting Chlamydia trachomatis while avoiding an invasive pelvic examination, making it a convenient, well-tolerated screening option, particularly valuable in asymptomatic individuals or settings where genital examination is not readily accepted or available.
questions.question: A first-catch urine sample is an acceptable specimen for nucleic acid amplification testing of chlamydia primarily because it:
options: Eliminates the need for any laboratory processing at all
Can only detect gonorrhoea and not chlamydia
Requires the sample to be collected several hours after voiding
Avoids the need for an invasive genital examination while retaining good sensitivity
Is more sensitive than a directly collected endocervical swab

questions.question: A woman requests conservative, non-surgical treatment for early-stage prolapse and is referred for postnatal physiotherapy. Which degree of prolapse is most appropriately managed this way as first-line therapy?
questions.explanation: Pelvic floor physiotherapy, including exercises and adjuncts like faradic stimulation, is most effective for mild, first-degree prolapse where supportive tissues retain some function. Advanced prolapse with significant anatomical descent generally requires surgical correction. Early intervention with physiotherapy can also prevent progression.

Endometriosis is listed under the miscellaneous category of ectopic pregnancy aetiology alongside IUCD use, ART, and previous ectopic pregnancy. Endometriosis can obstruct the fallopian tube through adhesion formation or direct tubal implants, creating the same mechanical delay in ovum transport as inflammatory salpingitis. It is an important non-inflammatory cause of ectopic pregnancy.
questions.question: An endometriotic implant obstructing the fallopian tube causes ectopic pregnancy. Endometriosis as a cause of ectopic pregnancy is classified under which aetiological category?

questions.explanation: When cervical ectropion causes persistent bothersome symptoms such as postcoital bleeding despite normal cytology excluding malignancy, cryotherapy or cautery can ablate the columnar epithelium and resolve symptoms with minimal invasiveness. Cone biopsy and hysterectomy are excessive interventions for this benign condition. Recognising normal cytology first is essential before considering any ablative treatment to avoid missing coexisting pathology.
options: Cryotherapy or cautery to the ectropion
Immediate cone biopsy of the cervix
questions.question: A 35-year-old with symptomatic cervical ectropion causing postcoital spotting has normal cervical cytology. Which treatment is MOST appropriate if symptoms persist despite reassurance?

questions.explanation: Central precocious puberty results from early, otherwise normal, activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, producing a pubertal gonadotrophin response to GnRH stimulation testing. Peripheral causes, such as autonomous ovarian cysts, McCune-Albright syndrome, or exogenous hormone exposure, instead suppress gonadotrophins because the axis itself is not activated. This distinction determines whether GnRH agonist therapy will be effective.
options: Premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis
questions.question: Central precocious puberty in a 6-year-old girl is confirmed by pubertal LH response to GnRH stimulation testing. Which underlying mechanism defines this form of precocious puberty?

questions.explanation: Vulval scraping (scraping the vulval surface) is listed as a source of specimen in gynaecological cytology specifically applicable to carcinoma of the vulva. This cytological technique allows cells from vulval lesions to be collected for microscopic examination without requiring surgical biopsy as the initial diagnostic step. It is analogous to the cervical Pap smear but applied to the vulval epithelium.
questions.question: Vulval scraping as a cytological specimen source is specifically applicable to which condition?

questions.explanation: Norethisterone 5 mg orally three times daily is given on days 5–25 of the cycle for ovulatory DUB (to cover the entire non-menstrual period, suppressing endometrial growth), and on days 15–25 for anovulatory DUB (to provide progestin in the second half when the corpus luteum should be active). The different day ranges reflect the different hormonal mechanisms: ovulatory DUB requires earlier progestin coverage while anovulatory DUB needs only luteal phase support.
questions.question: Norethisterone 5 mg orally three times daily (days 5–25) is used in which type of DUB?

options: Converting endometrium to secretory type, diminishing oestrogen
Directly causing vasoconstriction of spiral arterioles
Stimulating FSH to drive follicular development and ovulation
Inhibiting prostaglandin synthesis via cyclo-oxygenase inhibition
Preventing fibrinolysis of endometrial blood clots
questions.question: Progestational agents (progestins) in DUB act by which mechanism to control bleeding?
questions.explanation: Progestins (e.g., medroxyprogesterone acetate, Provera) control DUB by: stopping endometrial growth; stabilizing and converting the endometrium to secretory type so shedding occurs in an organized manner; diminishing the effect of oestrogen on target endometrial cells; reducing mitotic activity; and preventing or reversing hyperplastic processes. They do not directly cause vasoconstriction — that is the mechanism of oestrogen. Cyclo-oxygenase inhibition is the mechanism of NSAIDs.

options: Streak gonads, female phenotype, and high malignancy risk
Testes and female phenotype with absent pubic hair
Ovaries and uterus with normal secondary sexual characteristics
XY karyotype, testes, and male phenotype
Ambiguous genitalia with both Müllerian and Wolffian structures
questions.question: Swyer's syndrome (46,XY gonadal agenesis) differs from Complete Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome in that Swyer's patients have:
questions.explanation: In Swyer's syndrome, a mutation in the short arm of the Y chromosome prevents TDF production, resulting in absence of testicular development despite XY karyotype. Streak gonads and a uterus are present (Müllerian structures persist because no AMH is produced), giving a female phenotype. Unlike CAIS where testes are present, Swyer's has no testicular tissue. The streak gonads carry a high risk of malignancy (gonadoblastoma), requiring prophylactic gonadectomy.

questions.question: Women are generally advised to avoid pregnancy for how long after hCG levels normalise following molar evacuation?
questions.explanation: Contraception is advised for approximately six months after hCG normalises following molar pregnancy evacuation, allowing completion of the surveillance period so that a new pregnancy does not confound interpretation of hCG trends indicating possible persistent disease.

options: A regular cycle length of 26 to 32 days
A regular cycle length of 21 to 35 days
Ovulation occurring on day 21 in all women
questions.question: The Standard Days Method of natural family planning identifies days 8 to 19 of the cycle as fertile based on which assumption?
questions.explanation: The Standard Days Method relies on the assumption of a regular cycle between 26 and 32 days, within which days 8 to 19 are designated as the fertile window. It is unsuitable for women with irregular cycles outside this range, as fertility awareness accuracy declines significantly.

options: Bilocular cystic mass with smooth walls
Diffuse mixed echogenic pattern with absent fetus
Bilateral adnexal cysts with free fluid
questions.question: Which ultrasound finding is CHARACTERISTIC of a complete hydatidiform mole?
questions.explanation: The classical ultrasound appearance of a complete hydatidiform mole is a diffuse mixed echogenic pattern often described as a 'snowstorm' appearance, with an absent fetus and abnormally high hCG levels. Partial moles may show focal cystic spaces in placental tissue with embryonic remnants.

questions.question: A woman at 41 weeks gestation with a normally grown fetus is being counselled about induction of labour. Which specific risk increases with prolongation of pregnancy beyond term that primarily justifies this recommendation?
options: Placental insufficiency and increased risk of stillbirth
questions.explanation: Prolongation of pregnancy beyond term is associated with a gradually increasing risk of placental insufficiency and stillbirth, as placental function may decline while fetal oxygen and nutrient demands continue to rise, which is why induction of labour is generally recommended once pregnancy extends significantly past the due date. Careful fetal monitoring can be used if expectant management is chosen instead, but the underlying risk rationale for induction relates specifically to this placental ageing process. This differs entirely from early pregnancy risks such as miscarriage or ectopic pregnancy.

Topical vaginal antifungal preparations, such as clotrimazole pessaries, are preferred in pregnancy due to established safety, while oral azole antifungals, particularly at higher doses, carry potential teratogenic risk and are generally avoided, especially in the first trimester. This route selection reflects the general principle of minimising systemic drug exposure during pregnancy when effective topical alternatives exist. Treatment duration for topical therapy may need to be longer than in non-pregnant women.
questions.question: A woman with recurrent candidal vulvovaginitis in pregnancy is being treated. Which route of antifungal administration is MOST appropriate given pregnancy safety considerations?

options: IUD use is absolutely contraindicated in all HIV-positive women regardless of clinical status
HIV-positive women who are clinically well can safely use copper IUDs — WHO MEC Category 2 or 3
HIV-positive women not on ART should not use any IUD under any circumstances
The LNG-IUS is contraindicated in all HIV-positive women due to immunosuppression risk
IUD use accelerates HIV disease progression and reduces CD4 count significantly
questions.explanation: WHO MEC 2016 classifies copper IUD use in HIV-positive women as: Category 2 for women on ART (benefits outweigh risks) and Category 3 for women not on ART with AIDS (theoretical risks outweigh benefits). Clinically well HIV-positive women on ART can safely use copper IUDs with appropriate STI screening before insertion. IUD use does not affect HIV disease progression or CD4 count. Regular STI and HIV viral load monitoring is advised.
questions.question: Which statement about HIV and the intrauterine device is MOST accurate according to current WHO guidance?

questions.explanation: Pregnancy occurring with an intrauterine device in situ carries a disproportionately higher relative risk of ectopic implantation, since the device is more effective at preventing intrauterine than tubal implantation. Any pregnancy in a woman with an IUCD in place should therefore prompt urgent evaluation to exclude ectopic pregnancy. Early ultrasound localisation of the pregnancy is essential in this scenario.
questions.question: A woman using an intrauterine contraceptive device presents with a positive pregnancy test. Which type of pregnancy is she at disproportionately increased risk of compared with the general pregnant population?

options: Cornual (interstitial) location with cardiac activity present
Small, unruptured mass with low, declining hCG
Very high hCG with a large adnexal mass
questions.explanation: Medical management of ectopic pregnancy with methotrexate is most appropriate when the pregnancy is unruptured, relatively small, associated with a low and ideally declining hCG level, and without fetal cardiac activity, since these features predict a higher chance of successful resolution without surgery. Ruptured, unstable, or advanced ectopic pregnancies require surgical intervention instead. Careful patient selection improves the success rate of medical treatment.
questions.question: A woman with a known ectopic pregnancy of 6 weeks, stable haemodynamics, low serum hCG, and no fetal cardiac activity is being considered for expectant or medical management. Which specific criterion most strongly supports choosing medical management with methotrexate over surgery?

A woman treated for CIN by loop excision is counselled that residual or recurrent disease can occur with all ablative and excisional techniques except one. Which treatment carries the lowest residual/recurrence risk because it removes the entire transformation zone for histological assessment?
questions.explanation: Hysterectomy removes the entire cervix and transformation zone, virtually eliminating the risk of residual or recurrent CIN compared with ablative or local excisional techniques, which carry a measurable residual/recurrence rate even when adequately performed. It is generally reserved for women who have completed childbearing or have other gynaecological indications. Excisional techniques like cone biopsy still allow histological confirmation of clearance margins.

questions.question: A patient taking rifampicin for tuberculosis alongside combined oral contraceptives should be advised that:
questions.explanation: Rifampicin is a potent hepatic enzyme inducer that increases the metabolism of both oestrogen and progestogen, substantially reducing the efficacy of combined oral contraceptives, so additional or alternative non-hormonal or less enzyme-dependent contraception is recommended during and after rifampicin therapy.
options: Only injectable contraceptives are affected by rifampicin
Rifampicin has no interaction with hormonal contraceptives
Rifampicin reduces contraceptive efficacy through hepatic enzyme induction
The interaction only affects progestogen-only pills, not combined pills

questions.explanation: While HPV is sexually transmitted, cervical cancer requires persistent infection with high-risk HPV strains (types 16 and 18 predominantly) followed by progressive oncogenic transformation over years. Not all HPV-infected adolescents develop cervical cancer; persistence and co-factors determine progression. This explains why cervical cancer is listed as a distinct, later-stage consequence rather than an immediate STI complication.
questions.question: In a study on adolescent sexual health problems, Ca cervix is listed separately from STDs. This distinction is clinically significant because cervical cancer in young women requires which additional pathway beyond STI transmission?
options: Repeated syphilitic chancres on the cervix
History of gonococcal PID causing cervical metaplasia
Persistent high-risk HPV infection with oncogenic transformation
Herpes simplex virus integration into cervical epithelium

questions.explanation: Anterior colporrhaphy with bladder neck buttress has a long-term success rate of approximately 40% for curing stress incontinence. Despite being a simple operation that permits simultaneous repair of other prolapses, its inferior incontinence cure rate compared to retropubic colposuspension (85-90%) means that in patients where cure of incontinence is the primary goal, a colposuspension or TVT/TOT should be considered instead.
questions.question: A woman with uterovaginal prolapse and concomitant stress incontinence undergoes anterior colporrhaphy alone. What is the expected long-term success rate for curing her incontinence?

questions.explanation: Uterine fibroids are classified by their location: intramural (within the myometrium, most common), submucosal (distorting the endometrial cavity, most likely to cause menorrhagia), subserosal (projecting from the outer surface), cervical, and broad ligament. Intramural fibroids tend to cause bulk symptoms as they enlarge, distorting the uterine shape and compressing adjacent structures.
questions.question: Uterine leiomyomas (fibroids) arising within the myometrium and not yet distorting the cavity or serosa are classified as:
The Levonorgestrel intrauterine system is classified as WHO MEC Category 1 (unrestricted use) for women with which of the following conditions?
options: Active breast cancer currently under treatment
Endometriosis causing heavy menstrual bleeding and pelvic pain
Migraine with aura in a 45-year-old smoker
questions.explanation: Endometriosis is a WHO MEC Category 1 (unrestricted use) indication for the LNG-IUS, which is both contraceptive and therapeutic. The LNG-IUS suppresses endometrial tissue through local progestogen, significantly reducing dysmenorrhoea, menorrhagia, and endometrioma recurrence. Active breast cancer, unexplained bleeding, and severe cirrhosis are Category 4 (absolute contraindications); migraine with aura is Category 3–4 for systemic hormonal methods but Category 2 for LNG-IUS.

questions.question: The hCG level at which the plateau in normal pregnancy is maintained for the remainder of gestation is approximately:
questions.explanation: After peaking at approximately 100,000 IU/ml (10^5 IU/ml) at 60–90 days of gestation, hCG decreases to a plateau level of approximately 10,000–20,000 IU/ml, which is maintained for the remainder of the pregnancy. The level returns to non-pregnant levels of less than 5 mIU/ml within 21–24 days after delivery.

Benzathine penicillin remains the treatment of choice for syphilis in pregnancy, as it effectively crosses the placenta to treat fetal infection and prevent congenital syphilis, unlike doxycycline which is contraindicated in pregnancy due to fetal effects on bone and teeth. Azithromycin resistance and inadequate placental penetration make it an unreliable alternative. Recognising penicillin allergy requires desensitisation rather than substitution in pregnancy given the lack of an equally effective alternative.
questions.question: A pregnant woman is diagnosed with primary syphilis based on a painless genital ulcer and positive treponemal serology. Which treatment is MOST appropriate to both treat her infection and prevent congenital transmission?

A sexually inactive 78-year-old with severe procidentia and multiple comorbidities is being considered for a definitive but non-reconstructive surgical option. Which procedure specifically obliterates the vaginal canal and is suited to her?
questions.explanation: Le Fort's colpocleisis surgically obliterates the vaginal canal by suturing anterior and posterior vaginal walls together, providing a low-risk definitive option for frail, sexually inactive women unfit for major reconstructive surgery. It preserves the uterus in situ. Sexual activity is precluded afterward, so patient counselling is essential.

options: Elevated serum FSH above LH ratio
questions.question: A 24-year-old with oligomenorrhoea, hirsutism, and bilateral polycystic ovaries on ultrasound is being evaluated using Rotterdam criteria. Which additional finding would confirm the diagnosis of PCOS?
questions.explanation: Rotterdam criteria require any two of oligo-/anovulation, clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism, and polycystic ovarian morphology, after excluding other causes. Since this patient already has oligomenorrhoea and polycystic ovaries, confirming hyperandrogenism satisfies the third possible criterion, though only two of three are actually needed for diagnosis. Elevated AMH is supportive but not a formal diagnostic criterion in Rotterdam guidelines.

options: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948)
The ICPD Programme of Action, Cairo
The Alma Ata Declaration on Primary Healthcare (1978)
questions.explanation: The 1994 ICPD Programme of Action in Cairo was the landmark global agreement that shifted population policy from demographic targets to a rights-based approach centred on individuals' reproductive rights, health, and empowerment. It defined reproductive rights as including the right to decide freely the number and spacing of children, access to reproductive healthcare, and freedom from discrimination and coercion.
questions.question: Which international agreement MOST significantly established reproductive health and reproductive rights as fundamental human rights?

questions.explanation: Asymptomatic bacteriuria is generally not treated in the general population, but before surgery involving urological manipulation, mesh insertion, or prosthetic material, treatment is recommended to reduce the risk of postoperative infection related to the procedure.
questions.question: A patient scheduled for elective gynaecological surgery who is found to have asymptomatic bacteriuria on routine preoperative screening should MOST appropriately be:
options: Started on lifelong prophylactic antibiotic therapy
Left completely untreated in all circumstances
Cancelled from the surgical list indefinitely
Treated before surgery if a prosthetic procedure is planned
Given antifungal therapy instead of antibiotics

questions.question: Vulval carcinoma has an overall 5-year survival of approximately what percentage for Stage I disease?
questions.explanation: Stage I vulval carcinoma (confined to the vulva with no lymph node involvement) has an overall 5-year survival of approximately 90%. Survival declines dramatically with nodal involvement: Stage III (unilateral nodes) has approximately 50–60% survival, and Stage IV disease has less than 15%. Early detection is therefore critical.

options: Fetal hypoxia requiring urgent evaluation and likely expedited delivery
Normal variation requiring only routine continued observation
Maternal fever alone with no fetal implication
A normal, reassuring fetal heart pattern
Fetal sleep cycle only, requiring no action
questions.question: A woman in labour develops a fetal heart rate showing recurrent late decelerations with reduced variability. What does this pattern most specifically suggest about fetal wellbeing?
questions.explanation: Recurrent late decelerations with reduced baseline variability are a concerning cardiotocographic pattern suggestive of fetal hypoxia, typically reflecting uteroplacental insufficiency, and require urgent clinical assessment with consideration of expedited delivery if the pattern does not resolve with conservative measures such as maternal repositioning and oxygen. This differs from early decelerations, which are typically benign and related to head compression. Prompt recognition of this pattern is essential to prevent adverse neonatal outcomes.

Functional hypothalamic amenorrhoea from exercise and low energy availability requires addressing the energy deficit as first-line treatment — increasing caloric intake and reducing exercise intensity to restore energy availability and allow spontaneous resumption of GnRH pulsatility. Hormonal therapy (OCP) treats the bone density without addressing the underlying cause and may mask recovery. Energy availability restoration is the only intervention that reverses the hypothalamic suppression and restores fertility naturally.
questions.question: A runner presents with amenorrhoea of 8 months. Her bone density scan (DEXA) shows osteopenia. She has a low BMI of 17.5 and exercises 3 hours daily. What is the MOST appropriate initial treatment?
options: Bisphosphonate therapy for bone density restoration
Reduce exercise intensity and increase caloric intake
Combined oral contraceptive pill for hormonal replacement

questions.explanation: The bio-social gap results from an earlier age of reproductive maturity (declining menarcheal age) combined with a societal trend of delaying marriage due to educational pursuits. This gap means adolescents are biologically capable of reproduction long before they are socially ready or independent. This gap creates conditions for high-risk unprotected sexual activity.
options: Rising poverty and falling educational quality
Increase in contraceptive access and urbanization
Male sexual dominance and female passivity
questions.question: A medical student is asked to explain what creates the 'bio-social gap' in adolescent reproductive health. Which combination correctly identifies the two factors responsible?

questions.explanation: Vesico-vaginal fistula creates a pathological tract between the urinary system and the vaginal epithelium, causing true (continuous) incontinence by bypassing the normal urethral controlling mechanisms entirely. This is classified separately from the functional types of incontinence (stress, urge, overflow, reflex). Patients describe constant, uncontrollable leakage of urine through the vagina day and night.
options: True incontinence bypassing normal controlling mechanisms
Reflex incontinence from spinal cord injury
questions.question: A VVF causes which specific type of urinary incontinence?

options: Only when clinical DVT is confirmed postoperatively
Only in patients already on warfarin
12 hours before/after major surgery, continued weeks
questions.question: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) prophylaxis with low-molecular-weight heparin is typically commenced:
questions.explanation: LMWH for DVT prophylaxis in major gynaecological surgery is typically commenced 12 hours before or immediately after surgery and continued for at least 7–10 days or until the patient is fully mobile. In cancer patients, prophylaxis is recommended for 28 days after major abdominal-pelvic surgery, reflecting their prolonged high-risk period.

options: The patient is under 25 years with anovulatory cycles
Medical therapy has succeeded in controlling bleeding
Suspected endometrial disease, uncontrolled bleeding, or failed sampling
There is irregular bleeding in a 20-year-old on oral contraceptives
questions.question: In the investigation of abnormal uterine bleeding, dilatation and curettage (D&C) is indicated specifically when:
questions.explanation: D&C is indicated to exclude intrauterine disease (polyp, hyperplasia, carcinoma, tuberculosis), to sample the endometrium when office biopsy fails, and to arrest severe uncontrollable bleeding. It has higher sensitivity than office endometrial biopsy for detecting intrauterine lesions. Specific indications include high-risk patients for endometrial hyperplasia or carcinoma, suspected endometritis or atypical hyperplasia, and bleeding unresponsive to medical therapy.

questions.question: The urethral transitional epithelium lining the bladder is described as waterproof. What is the clinical significance of this property?
options: It allows selective reabsorption of water from urine
It secretes mucus to lubricate urine flow
It actively transports sodium into urine
It allows diffusion of antibiotics into urine
Prevents diffusion of urinary toxic substances
questions.explanation: The transitional epithelium lining the bladder is waterproof and does not allow diffusion of the urinary constituents (including urea, creatinine, ammonia, and other toxic substances) across its walls. This property is essential for the bladder to act as an effective urine reservoir. Disruption of this epithelium (by carcinoma, radiation cystitis, or chronic inflammation) can increase bladder permeability and hypersensitivity.

questions.question: The 'quick start' method of initiating combined oral contraceptives allows a woman to start the pill on ANY day of her cycle. The MOST important additional requirement when quick-starting on a day other than Day 1 is:
options: A transvaginal ultrasound to confirm no dominant follicle is present
A negative urinary pregnancy test and use of backup contraception for the first 7 days
Completion of a full cycle before starting the next pack
A prescription from a specialist rather than a general practitioner
Thyroid function testing to ensure no hormonal interference
questions.explanation: Quick-start initiation requires a negative pregnancy test (to exclude pre-existing pregnancy) and use of additional contraception (barrier method or abstinence) for 7 days to cover the time needed for the pill to suppress ovulation and thicken cervical mucus. Starting on days 2–5 of the cycle offers excellent effectiveness; starting after day 5 requires the additional 7-day backup. The key advantage is reducing the delay to effective contraceptive cover.

options: Sexually transmitted infection transmission alone with no contraceptive effect
Both unintended pregnancy and sexually transmitted infection transmission
Unintended pregnancy alone with no effect on infection risk
questions.explanation: The safe sex message promoting correct and consistent condom use addresses the dual goal of preventing both unintended pregnancy and the transmission of sexually transmitted infections, reflecting the combined reproductive and sexual health benefits of reliable barrier method use.
questions.question: The 'safe sex' message emphasising correct and consistent condom use is MOST accurately targeted at reducing which combined risk?
Dyspareunia occurring specifically at initial penetration rather than with deep thrusting is MOST suggestive of which underlying cause?
questions.explanation: Pain localised to the entrance of the vagina at initial penetration typically points to superficial vulval or introital causes such as vestibulitis or atrophic changes, whereas pain occurring with deep thrusting is more suggestive of pelvic pathology such as endometriosis or pelvic inflammatory disease.
options: Vulval or introital pathology such as vestibulitis

questions.explanation: The gubernaculum connects the developing gonad to the inguinal region. In females, the cranial portion becomes the suspensory (ovarian) ligament, and the caudal portion becomes the ovarian ligament (attaching the ovary to the uterus) and then the round ligament (attaching to the labium majus). The gubernaculum thus gives rise to three distinct ligamentous structures in the female.
questions.question: In the female fetus, the cranial portion of the gubernaculum becomes:
options: The round ligament of the uterus
The suspensory ligament of the ovary

questions.question: A woman with vaginal atrophy from oestrogen deficiency reports dyspareunia unresponsive to lubricants alone. Examination shows pale, thin, friable vaginal epithelium with loss of rugae. Which histological change MOST directly explains this appearance?
questions.explanation: Oestrogen deficiency reduces glycogen content and overall thickness of the vaginal epithelium, leading to thinning, loss of rugae, reduced lubrication, and increased fragility characteristic of atrophic vaginitis. This is why local oestrogen therapy, which restores epithelial thickness and glycogen, is effective treatment. Reduced glycogen also raises vaginal pH by limiting lactobacilli-mediated lactic acid production, predisposing to secondary infection.
options: Reduced vaginal epithelial glycogen and thickness
Increased vaginal blood flow and congestion
Hypertrophy of vaginal smooth muscle layer

questions.explanation: Detrusor instability (overactivity) is diagnosed on cystometry when involuntary detrusor contractions exceeding approximately 15 cm H2O occur during the filling phase, provoking urgency and often leakage. This objective threshold distinguishes true detrusor overactivity from normal filling pressure changes. Treatment is directed at suppressing these contractions pharmacologically or behaviourally.
questions.question: On cystometry, a woman is found to have involuntary detrusor contractions during the filling phase, provoking a strong urge and leakage. Above what pressure rise are these contractions considered diagnostic of detrusor instability?

questions.explanation: Frothy, greenish-yellow vaginal discharge with vulval pruritus and motile flagellated organisms on wet mount is pathognomonic of Trichomonas vaginalis infection. Treatment is metronidazole 2g as a single oral dose (or 400mg BD for 7 days), and the sexual partner must be treated simultaneously to prevent reinfection. Trichomoniasis is listed in teaching materials as causing a characteristic greenish-yellow frothy discharge.
questions.question: A 28-year-old woman presents with frothy, greenish-yellow vaginal discharge with vulval itching. Wet-mount microscopy shows motile flagellated organisms. Which organism is responsible and what is the first-line treatment?

questions.explanation: In perimenopausal anovulatory DUB, a low Day 21 progesterone (confirming absence of ovulation and corpus luteum formation) is the most direct biochemical confirmation of anovulatory status. Elevated FSH and LH are consistent with declining ovarian reserve. However, the specific correlation between anovulatory bleeding and a low Day 21 progesterone is the most actionable finding for treatment planning — it confirms that progestin supplementation is needed and that the bleeding is not from an ovulatory corpus luteum insufficiency.
options: Elevated FSH (above 40 IU/L) and low oestradiol
Elevated plasma FSH and LH consistent with decreasing follicle number and gonadotrophin resistance
Elevated androgen levels from adrenal hyperfunction
Low progesterone on Day 21 consistent with absent corpus luteum
Low TSH consistent with subclinical hyperthyroidism
questions.question: In perimenopausal women with DUB, the diagnosis of anovulatory cycles can be confirmed biochemically by demonstrating:

questions.explanation: Arrhenoblastoma (Sertoli-Leydig cell tumour) secretes androgens and presents with signs of masculinisation including secondary amenorrhoea, hirsutism, clitoral enlargement, and voice deepening. Initial defeminisation is followed by progressive virilisation. This distinguishes it from oestrogenic tumours like granulosa cell tumours.
questions.question: Which of the following ovarian tumours would MOST likely present with signs of masculinisation in a 35-year-old woman?

questions.explanation: Craniopharyngioma compresses the hypothalamus or pituitary stalk, preventing normal GnRH secretion or transport to the pituitary portal circulation, resulting in hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and amenorrhoea. It may also elevate prolactin (by compressing the stalk, removing dopamine inhibition). Craniopharyngiomas typically present in childhood/adolescence with growth failure, visual field defects, and diabetes insipidus alongside amenorrhoea.
options: Direct compression of the ovaries through descending neural pathways
Secretion of prolactin-like substances suppressing FSH
Physical compression of the hypothalamus impairing GnRH secretion
questions.question: A craniopharyngioma is a brain tumour listed as a hypothalamic cause of amenorrhoea. By which mechanism does it cause amenorrhoea?

questions.explanation: Hyperthyroidism causes oligomenorrhoea or secondary amenorrhoea through suppression of GnRH pulsatility and altered sex hormone binding globulin (SHBG) levels. Elevated thyroid hormones suppress hypothalamic function and alter oestrogen metabolism. In contrast, hypothyroidism is associated with menorrhagia (heavy periods) from anovulatory cycles and coagulation dysfunction. Thyroid function testing is therefore essential in the evaluation of menstrual irregularities.
options: Prolonged menstruation from excess thyroid hormone stimulation
Oligomenorrhoea or amenorrhoea due to suppressed gonadotrophins
questions.question: Hyperthyroidism is a recognised cause of which menstrual abnormality?
Haematometra refers to:
questions.explanation: Haematometra is the accumulation of menstrual blood within the uterine cavity secondary to obstruction of outflow. It can result from imperforate hymen, transverse vaginal septum, cervical stenosis, or other outflow obstruction. It typically presents with cyclical abdominal pain. Haematocolpos is blood in the vagina, haematosalpinx is blood in the fallopian tube. Haematometra may extend to haematosalpinx if pressure is sufficient.
options: Blood accumulation within the uterine cavity
Blood clot within the cervical canal
Dilatation and curettage of the uterus
Methotrexate therapy with follow-up hCG monitoring
questions.explanation: Medical management with methotrexate is appropriate for haemodynamically stable women with low beta-hCG, small ectopic size, no significant pain, and no evidence of rupture, provided close hCG monitoring confirms resolution. Surgery is reserved for ruptured, symptomatic, or methotrexate-unsuitable cases. Curettage would not address tissue outside the uterine cavity and risks missing the true diagnosis.
questions.question: A woman with a confirmed unruptured ectopic pregnancy has a beta-hCG of 1200 IU/L, no significant pain, and no free fluid on scan. Which management option is MOST appropriate?

questions.explanation: A Sister Mary Joseph nodule refers to a palpable, often firm periumbilical metastatic deposit, and its presence in a woman with an ovarian mass indicates advanced intra-abdominal malignant spread rather than early, localised disease.
questions.question: A palpable Sister Mary Joseph nodule in a woman with an ovarian mass suggests which clinical significance?
options: Localised early-stage disease confined to one ovary

questions.question: A 35-year-old woman presents with lower abdominal pain and irregular vaginal bleeding. Which element of history is MOST critical to obtain FIRST before any examination?
questions.explanation: In any woman of reproductive age presenting with bleeding and pain, pregnancy must be excluded before all other considerations, as ectopic pregnancy is life-threatening. LMP and pregnancy status thus precede all other history elements. Failure to consider pregnancy is among the commonest causes of diagnostic catastrophe in gynaecology.
options: Last menstrual period and pregnancy status
Surgical history in the past five years
Invasion to less than half the myometrium
questions.explanation: FIGO Stage IC endometrial carcinoma is defined as tumour invasion to more than half the depth of the myometrium. Stage IA is limited to the endometrium, Stage IB is invasion to less than half the myometrium, and Stage IC is the deepest myometrial invasion within Stage I (confined to corpus).
questions.question: In FIGO surgical staging of endometrial carcinoma, Stage IC is defined as:

A woman with long-standing prolapse develops abnormal vaginal discharge and intermittent spotting unrelated to menses. Chronic mucosal exposure and friction in prolapse most commonly produce which finding responsible for this?
options: Ulceration and infection of exposed epithelium
questions.explanation: Chronic friction and exposure of prolapsed vaginal and cervical epithelium against clothing predisposes to decubitus ulceration, which becomes secondarily infected and causes discharge with intermittent bleeding. This must be differentiated from malignancy by examination and biopsy if the ulcer fails to heal after prolapse reduction. It is a recognised complication of neglected long-standing prolapse.

questions.question: A woman with congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency has ambiguous genitalia at birth. Which biochemical abnormality is MOST characteristic of this specific enzyme defect?
questions.explanation: 21-hydroxylase deficiency blocks conversion of 17-hydroxyprogesterone to 11-deoxycortisol, causing marked accumulation of 17-hydroxyprogesterone, which is diverted toward androgen synthesis and causes virilisation of the female fetus, along with variable cortisol and aldosterone deficiency. ACTH is actually elevated, not reduced, due to loss of cortisol negative feedback. Measuring elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone is the key diagnostic biochemical test for this condition.

Pap smear reporting by Papanicolaou's original grading: Grade I (Normal), Grade II (Infections), Grade III (Mild dysplasia), Grade IV (Moderate to severe dysplasia), Grade V (Carcinoma). The modern Bethesda classification uses LSIL (low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion) and HSIL (high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion) which broadly correspond to CIN I and CIN II-III respectively.
questions.question: The Papanicolaou smear result of Grade V corresponds to which clinical finding?

options: Oral progestogen combined with oral oestrogen
questions.question: A 52-year-old post-menopausal woman is started on HRT. Which route of oestrogen administration AVOIDS first-pass liver metabolism and is associated with fewer coagulation and triglyceride effects?
questions.explanation: Transdermal oestrogen (patches, gels, subcutaneous implants) bypasses first-pass hepatic metabolism, delivering oestradiol directly into systemic circulation. This avoids the stimulatory effect of oral oestrogen on hepatic production of clotting factors (factors II, VII, X) and triglycerides, which partly explains why transdermal HRT is associated with lower VTE risk than oral HRT. Transdermal routes also achieve more physiological serum oestradiol levels.

questions.question: Cervical stump carcinoma (after subtotal hysterectomy) is most appropriately managed with:
questions.explanation: Cervical stump carcinoma (occurring in the cervical stump remaining after subtotal hysterectomy) is uncommon. It should be staged and managed according to the same criteria as primary cervical carcinoma. Radiotherapy is generally preferred for cervical stump carcinoma because surgical access to the residual cervix is limited, and radiotherapy modifications are applied to account for the altered anatomy.

questions.question: An arcuate uterus differs from a septate uterus in that:
questions.explanation: The arcuate uterus has only a small midline depression (indentation) at the fundus rather than a full internal septum dividing the cavity. It is the mildest form of Müllerian fusion abnormality and is generally considered the least clinically significant, with minimal impact on reproductive outcomes. A septate uterus has a complete or partial internal septum but a normal external contour, and is associated with the highest miscarriage rate among Müllerian anomalies.
options: It has a completely divided uterine cavity
It has two completely separate cervices
It causes the most severe obstetric complications

questions.question: A patient with recurrent pregnancy loss is found to have antiphospholipid syndrome. Under which broad category of causes of spontaneous abortion does this diagnosis fall?
questions.explanation: Antiphospholipid syndrome is an autoimmune (immunological) cause of recurrent pregnancy loss, in which antiphospholipid antibodies promote placental thrombosis and insufficiency, distinguishing it from chromosomal, structural, infective, or endocrine causes of abortion. Recognising this category is important because it responds to specific treatment with anticoagulation and low-dose aspirin in subsequent pregnancies. Testing for antiphospholipid antibodies is part of the recurrent miscarriage workup.

options: To assess renal function before closure
To confirm complete healing before closure
questions.question: Following recto-vaginal fistula repair with a protective colostomy, a dye test is performed before colostomy closure. What is the primary purpose of this test?
questions.explanation: A dye test performed before colostomy closure instils dye into the rectum to check for any leakage through the repaired fistula site into the vagina, confirming complete healing before bowel continuity is restored. Proceeding with colostomy closure without confirming healing risks recurrent contamination and repair breakdown. This test is a standard safety step in staged fistula management.

Hydronephrosis or a non-functioning kidney resulting from ureteric obstruction by tumour indicates extension to the pelvic wall and is classified as Stage IIIB regardless of other clinical findings. This reflects the significant prognostic impact of ureteric involvement.
questions.question: Bilateral hydronephrosis in a woman with locally advanced cervical cancer is classified as which FIGO stage?
The Cusco speculum is preferred over the Sims speculum for routine cervical inspection because it:
questions.explanation: The Cusco (bivalve) speculum allows simultaneous retraction of anterior and posterior vaginal walls, providing a direct view of the cervix in the lithotomy or dorsal position. The Sims speculum is used in the left lateral position to assess prolapse or fistulae. For routine cervical inspection and Pap smear, the Cusco speculum is standard.
options: Is used in the lateral position

questions.explanation: The number of Barr bodies equals the number of inactive X chromosomes, which is (total X chromosomes minus 1). A 47XXX female has 3 X chromosomes, so 2 are inactivated (Lyonization), producing 2 Barr bodies. A normal female (46XX) has 1 Barr body; a 47XXY male (Klinefelter's) is Barr body positive with 1; males and 45XO females are chromatin negative (no Barr bodies).
questions.question: A 47XXX female would demonstrate how many Barr bodies on buccal smear examination?
Varicocele is a congenital/acquired testicular cause of male infertility. By what MECHANISM does varicocele impair spermatogenesis?
options: Antibody production against sperm surface antigens
Compression of the vas deferens obstructing outflow
Testosterone deficiency from Leydig cell compression
questions.explanation: Varicocele impairs spermatogenesis primarily through increased scrotal temperature caused by pooling of warm blood from abdominal veins into the pampiniform plexus. Normal spermatogenesis requires scrotal temperature 2–4°C below core body temperature; varicocele raises this temperature, disrupting the precise thermal regulation needed for sperm production. Varicocelectomy can improve semen parameters in approximately 60–70% of cases.

questions.question: A 32-year-old woman wants to use LAM but must return to work at 12 weeks postpartum when her infant will receive supplementary bottle feeds twice daily. The MOST appropriate advice is:
questions.explanation: LAM requires exclusive breastfeeding (no supplements of any kind), amenorrhoea, and infant under 6 months — all three simultaneously. Introducing supplementary bottle feeds, even twice daily, breaks the exclusivity criterion and reduces suckling frequency, which may restore ovulation before menstrual return. She should start a compatible contraceptive method (progestogen-only pill, implant, or copper IUD) before returning to work.
options: LAM remains effective as long as she breastfeeds at least once daily
LAM will no longer be reliable at 12 weeks due to supplementary feeding; she should start an additional contraceptive method before returning to work
LAM remains effective until her first menstrual period regardless of feeding pattern
She can use LAM until 6 months postpartum regardless of supplementary feeding if she breastfeeds at least 4 times daily
Supplementary formula improves infant nutrition and has no effect on LAM contraceptive efficacy

questions.explanation: Retropubic bladder neck suspension (Burch - suturing vaginal wall to pectineal ligament; or Marshall-Marchetti-Krantz - paravaginal tissues to back of pubic symphysis) achieves an 85-90% cure rate of stress incontinence. In contrast, anterior colporrhaphy with bladder neck buttress has only a 40% long-term success rate but permits repair of other prolapses simultaneously.
questions.question: The Burch colposuspension retropubic bladder neck suspension procedure achieves incontinence cure rates of approximately:

options: Malignant transformation of the cervical epithelium
Bacterial superinfection of the prolapsed tissue
Chronic abrasion of prolapsed vaginal epithelium
Vascular occlusion of the prolapsed area
questions.explanation: Keratinization is one of the local complications of uterovaginal prolapse and occurs because the prolapsed vaginal epithelium is continuously exposed to the environment and subjected to repeated abrasion and friction. This leads to thickening and squamous metaplasia of the normally moist vaginal mucosa. Decubitus ulcers develop due to kinking of blood vessels with relative ischaemia.
questions.question: Keratinization occurring in long-standing genital prolapse is best explained by:

options: A relatively ineffective method with a high typical-use failure rate
A highly effective standalone contraceptive method
A method requiring no additional barrier for full protection
A method that also provides strong protection against HIV
questions.question: Nonoxynol-9 spermicide used ALONE as a contraceptive method is best described as:
questions.explanation: Spermicide used alone, without a barrier method, has a relatively high typical-use failure rate and does not provide reliable protection against sexually transmitted infections; in fact, frequent nonoxynol-9 use may cause genital irritation that can increase susceptibility to HIV transmission.

options: The appendix testis and prostatic utricle
The fimbriae of the fallopian tubes
The round ligaments of the uterus
questions.explanation: In the female, Wolffian (mesonephric) duct remnants include the epoophoron (lateral to the ovary), paroophoron (medially), and Gartner's cysts (along the anterolateral vaginal wall). In the male, Müllerian remnants include the appendix testis and prostatic utricle. These female remnants are clinically important as they can form cysts that mimic adnexal pathology.
questions.question: The remnants of Wolffian ducts in the female are CORRECTLY identified as:
CIN management during pregnancy prioritises which approach?
questions.explanation: During pregnancy, CIN management involves investigations (cytology, colposcopy, and careful colposcopically-directed biopsies or wedge biopsy of one suspicious area) to exclude invasive carcinoma. There is no absolute need to treat CIN during pregnancy if invasive disease is ruled out. A complete reevaluation with biopsies is done 8-12 weeks postpartum. Cone biopsy in pregnancy is associated with more complications.
options: Immediate cone biopsy to prevent progression
LLETZ (large loop excision) in the first trimester

questions.question: The background inhibition of the sacral reflex arc is suppressed at the onset of micturition, allowing efferent impulses to reach the detrusor. This suppression occurs at the level of:
questions.explanation: At the onset of micturition, higher cortical and pontine centres voluntarily suppress the background inhibition of the sacral reflex arc (S2-4). This allows efferent parasympathetic impulses to pass to the detrusor muscle, causing a rise in intravesical pressure that exceeds intraurethral pressure and initiates urine flow. Simultaneously, the pelvic floor striated muscle voluntarily relaxes, reducing intraurethral pressure.

questions.question: Congenital tubal causes and salpingitis are both structural causes of ectopic pregnancy, but PID is described as the commonest overall aetiological cause. Which organism has been most strongly implicated in causing the tubal damage that leads to ectopic pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Chlamydia trachomatis is the organism most strongly implicated in causing pelvic inflammatory disease that damages the fallopian tubes, leading to both tubal infertility and increased risk of ectopic pregnancy, often through silent, undiagnosed infection. This underlies the importance of chlamydia screening and prompt treatment of pelvic infections in reducing future ectopic pregnancy risk. Its often asymptomatic course makes early detection challenging.

options: Depends only on breast tenderness as an indicator
Combines basal body temperature with cervical mucus changes
questions.explanation: The symptothermal method combines multiple fertility indicators, typically basal body temperature and cervical mucus changes, sometimes with calendar calculation, cross-checking signs against each other to improve the accuracy of identifying the fertile window compared with using a single indicator alone.
questions.question: The symptothermal method of fertility awareness improves reliability over single-indicator methods primarily because it:

options: Endometrial proliferation during the follicular phase
questions.question: Dihydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) is particularly relevant in reproductive health because it is the hormone responsible for:
questions.explanation: DHEA (and its sulfate, DHEA-S) is synthesized by the adrenal glands and is elevated before visible signs of puberty appear. It is the primary androgen responsible for adrenarche — the development of pubic and axillary hair. Thelarche is driven by oestrogen, ovulation by the LH surge, and endometrial proliferation by ovarian oestradiol. Girls achieve higher DHEA concentrations at a similar bone age compared to boys.

Oral contraceptives have the same protective effect against ovarian cancer as pregnancy. The reduction in ovulation (incessant ovulation theory) is thought to underlie this protection, reducing the repetitive minor trauma to the ovarian surface epithelium that predisposes to malignant transformation.
questions.question: The protective effect of oral contraceptives against ovarian cancer is comparable to which other factor?
Kallmann's syndrome causes hypogonadotrophic hypogonadism and delayed puberty by which mechanism?
questions.explanation: Kallmann's syndrome is characterized by hypogonadotrophic hypogonadism due to defective GnRH neuronal migration from the olfactory placode to the hypothalamus, resulting in GnRH deficiency. This is associated with anosmia (absent sense of smell) because the olfactory nerves share developmental pathways with GnRH neurons. Treatment involves pulsatile GnRH administration via portable infusion pump.
options: Gonadotrophin receptor mutations blocking FSH action
Primary ovarian failure from streak gonads
Thyroid hormone deficiency impairing GnRH release

questions.question: The diaphragm must ALWAYS be used in combination with spermicide because:
questions.explanation: The diaphragm functions as a physical barrier covering the cervix but may not seal perfectly against the cervical os, especially with penile thrusting during intercourse. Spermicide applied inside the dome kills any spermatozoa that enter past the rim. Without spermicide, the diaphragm's failure rate increases substantially. Additional spermicide must be applied before each subsequent act of intercourse.
options: Spermicide neutralizes the latex to prevent allergic reactions
Spermicide provides lubrication enabling easier insertion
Combined use provides protection against HPV and herpes
The diaphragm alone cannot reliably cover the entire cervical os and spermicide kills any spermatozoa passing the rim
Spermicide prevents the diaphragm from dislodging during intercourse

questions.explanation: Because mucinous ovarian tumours can be difficult to distinguish from metastatic appendiceal mucinous neoplasms, the appendix should be carefully inspected, and appendicectomy considered, during surgery for a mucinous ovarian tumour to exclude an occult primary appendiceal source.
questions.question: A woman undergoing surgery for a mucinous ovarian tumour should MOST appropriately also have which additional organ inspected intraoperatively?
In the Baden-Walker Halfway System of prolapse classification, the reference point used is:
questions.explanation: The Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification (POP-Q) system measures descent in centimetres relative to the hymen (either positive or negative), providing an objective quantitative description. The Baden-Walker Halfway System combines anatomic site with associated symptoms. Both reference systems are used to standardise grading for research and clinical communication.

questions.question: The bladder can accommodate what volume of urine with minimal rise in intravesical pressure under normal circumstances?
options: 300-500 mL with pressure rise of 0-15 cmH2O
100-200 mL with pressure rise of 0-5 cmH2O
200-300 mL with pressure rise of 5-10 cmH2O
500-700 mL with pressure rise of 20-30 cmH2O
questions.explanation: The bladder acts as a reservoir with high compliance, accommodating 300-500 mL of urine with very little rise of intravesical pressure (0-15 cmH2O). It is lined with water-proof transitional epithelium, can expand suprapubically and extraperitoneally without constraint, and maintains higher urethral pressure than intravesical pressure to prevent leakage under normal circumstances.

Phospholipase A2 (activated in the endometrium) acts on phospholipids in cell membranes to release arachidonic acid — the essential precursor for all prostaglandins, thromboxanes, and leukotrienes. Arachidonic acid is then converted by cyclo-oxygenase to unstable endoperoxides (PGH2, PGG2), which are further converted by specific synthases into PGF2a, PGE2, prostacyclin (PGI2), and thromboxane A2. This is why NSAIDs (which inhibit cyclo-oxygenase) are effective in reducing prostaglandin-mediated menorrhagia.
options: Fibrin degradation products in menstrual blood
questions.question: Phospholipase A2 in the endometrium initiates the synthesis of prostaglandins by acting on which substrate?

A 65-year-old presents with vague abdominal bloating, early satiety, and weight loss over three months. CA-125 is markedly elevated and CT shows omental thickening. Which diagnosis is MOST likely given this presentation?
questions.explanation: Vague, non-specific symptoms such as bloating, early satiety, and weight loss combined with markedly raised CA-125 and omental thickening on imaging strongly suggest epithelial ovarian carcinoma with peritoneal spread, reflecting the typically late and non-specific presentation of this malignancy. Benign cysts and fibroids do not typically cause omental disease or such marked marker elevation. Early recognition despite vague symptoms is crucial given the poor prognosis of late-stage diagnosis.

Normal seminal fluid analysis parameters are: volume 2–6 mL, sperm density >20 million/mL, and motility and morphology >50% each. The sample must be collected after 3 days of abstinence, by masturbation, kept at body temperature, and examined before analysis within 1 hour. An abnormal result should be repeated in 2–3 months as spermatogenesis cycles take approximately 72 days.
questions.question: Seminal fluid analysis is a cornerstone of male infertility workup. Which set of parameters represents the MINIMUM normal values?

questions.explanation: Ultrasound-guided local injection of methotrexate directly into the gestational sac, sometimes combined with systemic methotrexate, is a recognised management approach for stable caesarean scar ectopic pregnancy, aiming to resolve the pregnancy while minimising the risk of haemorrhage associated with more invasive removal. Curettage alone carries high risk of uncontrolled bleeding due to the scar's poor contractility. Expectant management is inappropriate given the significant rupture and haemorrhage risk if the pregnancy continues to grow.
options: Dilatation and curettage as first-line only
Vaginal delivery attempt at term later
questions.question: A woman with a known caesarean scar ectopic pregnancy at seven weeks gestation is haemodynamically stable. Which management approach is MOST appropriate to minimise haemorrhage risk while treating the pregnancy?
Tanner staging is used to assess pubertal development. A girl with breast stage 3 and sparse, slightly curled pubic hair over the mons is at approximately which Tanner stage for pubic hair?
questions.explanation: Tanner pubic hair stage 2 describes sparse, slightly pigmented, straight or slightly curled hair mainly along the labia, the earliest visible pubic hair growth. Stage 1 denotes prepubertal absence of hair, while stages 3 to 5 reflect progressively coarser, curlier, and more extensive distribution. Breast and pubic hair staging can progress at different rates in the same individual.

options: Age is not relevant to this diagnosis
questions.question: Premature ovarian insufficiency is diagnosed in a 32-year-old woman based on amenorrhoea and elevated FSH on two occasions. Below what age is this diagnosis specifically defined?
questions.explanation: Premature ovarian insufficiency is defined as ovarian failure with amenorrhoea and elevated FSH occurring before the age of 40, distinguishing it from natural menopause, which typically occurs later. This earlier age of onset carries specific implications, including a longer duration of oestrogen deficiency exposure and greater long-term risk of osteoporosis and cardiovascular disease if untreated, generally warranting hormone replacement until at least the natural age of menopause. Fertility counselling, including consideration of donor oocytes, is also an important part of care in this group.

A pad test involves weighing a perineal pad before and after a period of standardised activity to quantify the actual volume of urine leaked, providing an objective measure of incontinence severity. It is useful for confirming and grading incontinence, especially when symptoms and clinical findings are discordant. It does not identify the underlying mechanism, which requires urodynamic testing.
questions.question: A pad test is performed in a woman with suspected urinary incontinence. What does this test primarily quantify?

questions.explanation: Hepatitis B vaccination provides highly effective, long-lasting protection against infection and is the most effective preventive strategy for an uninfected sexual partner, alongside consistent condom use, since hepatitis B is efficiently transmitted through sexual contact with infected bodily fluids.
questions.question: Hepatitis B virus can be transmitted sexually. The MOST effective strategy for preventing this transmission in a sexual partner is:
options: Delaying treatment until symptoms develop in the infected partner
Hepatitis B vaccination of the uninfected partner

questions.explanation: The decision between laparoscopic and open surgery in ovarian cancer management should be based on disease stage, tumour characteristics, and the primary goal of achieving optimal cytoreduction. Advanced-stage disease with bulky pelvic and abdominal disease typically requires open surgery for complete debulking, while early-stage disease may be suitable for laparoscopic staging.
questions.question: The decision between laparoscopic and open surgery for ovarian cancer should PRIMARILY be based on:

questions.explanation: Surgery is indicated for cervical leiomyomas because they cause pressure symptoms on adjacent organs (bladder and rectum), complications in pregnancy (malpresentation, abnormal placentation), and potential obstruction of the birth canal during labour. The surgical approach requires great caution regarding the ureters and bladder due to their anatomical proximity to the cervix.
questions.question: The treatment of a leiomyoma (fibroid) of the cervix is surgery. What is the primary reason for this recommendation?
options: They are universally associated with HPV infection
They cause cervical stenosis in all cases

questions.explanation: Clustered pleomorphic microcalcifications are a recognised early radiological sign of ductal carcinoma in situ or invasive cancer, requiring stereotactic core biopsy for tissue diagnosis since they may not correspond to a palpable or ultrasound-visible mass. Fine needle aspiration provides only cytology and is less reliable than core biopsy for architectural assessment of calcifications. Delaying to routine follow-up risks missing early malignancy.
options: Stereotactic core biopsy of the area
questions.question: A 55-year-old undergoing routine mammography is found to have clustered pleomorphic microcalcifications without an associated mass. What is the MOST appropriate next step?
A patient undergoing gynaecological surgery under spinal anaesthesia develops sudden hypotension shortly after the block is established. The MOST likely underlying mechanism is:
questions.explanation: Spinal anaesthesia blocks sympathetic outflow below the level of the block, causing vasodilation and a fall in systemic vascular resistance, which commonly produces hypotension shortly after administration and is managed with intravenous fluids and vasopressors as needed.

questions.question: The 'eligibility wheel' tool used in family planning counselling is PRIMARILY designed to:
options: Calculate the Pearl Index for each individual patient's contraceptive choice
Determine the ideal method based on the patient's reproductive goals exclusively
Provide a quick reference for WHO MEC to screen conditions affecting contraceptive safety
Calculate the optimal time for emergency contraception based on cycle day
Train patients on self-administration of injectable contraceptives
questions.explanation: The WHO eligibility wheel allows providers to rapidly cross-reference a patient's medical conditions against the safety category for each contraceptive method. It operationalizes the WHO MEC guidelines at the point of care, improving the speed and accuracy of contraceptive safety screening during consultations.

questions.question: A woman with a copper IUD presents with lower abdominal pain, fever, and cervical excitation tenderness. The MOST appropriate initial management is:
questions.explanation: Signs suggestive of pelvic inflammatory disease in an IUD user warrant prompt antibiotic treatment according to local guidelines, with the device usually left in place initially unless symptoms fail to improve, since removal is not always necessary for successful treatment of the infection.
options: Reassure her that IUDs cannot cause any infection
Remove the IUD immediately before any antibiotics
Treat this as a normal side effect needing nothing
Treat for pelvic infection and reassess IUD removal need

questions.explanation: Primary infertility is defined as failure to conceive with no previous pregnancy, and investigations are indicated after 12 months of regular unprotected intercourse, as 80–85% of normal couples achieve pregnancy within 1 year. At 14 months, investigation is appropriate and overdue. Among normal couples, 60% conceive within 6 months and 90% within 18 months.
questions.question: A couple presents after 14 months of unprotected intercourse without achieving pregnancy. The woman has regular menstrual cycles and her partner is healthy. How should this condition be classified and when should investigations commence?
options: Subfertility; no investigation needed before 24 months
Impaired ciliary motility affecting sperm flagella and fallopian tube cilia
Absent testes and ovaries from birth
Excess androgen production in both sexes
questions.question: Kartagener's syndrome causes infertility in both males and females through the same fundamental cellular defect. What is this shared underlying mechanism?
questions.explanation: Kartagener's syndrome results from a primary ciliary dyskinesia affecting the structure and function of cilia and flagella throughout the body; in males this impairs sperm motility, while in females it impairs the ciliary transport function of the fallopian tubes, causing infertility in both sexes through the same underlying ciliary defect. The syndrome also classically causes situs inversus and chronic respiratory infections due to impaired respiratory cilia. Recognising the syndrome allows appropriate counselling regarding assisted reproduction options.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly identifies the recommended timing for postpartum IUD insertion?
options: Only after the first postpartum menstrual period
Exactly at 6 weeks postpartum only, at the routine postnatal check
Not before 3 months postpartum in breastfeeding women
