options: Vasectomy is a simpler, safer, more effective, and less expensive procedure
Vasectomy is less effective than tubal ligation in all circumstances
Both procedures carry identical complication rates and procedural complexity
Vasectomy requires general anaesthesia while tubal ligation can be done under local anaesthesia
Vasectomy is reversible in 90% of cases while tubal ligation is completely irreversible
questions.explanation: Vasectomy is performed under local anaesthesia through small scrotal incisions or the no-scalpel technique, taking approximately 15–30 minutes with minimal complications. Female tubal ligation requires intra-abdominal access, carries higher anaesthetic and surgical risks, costs more, and has longer recovery. Vasectomy failure rate is approximately 0.1% vs 0.5% for tubal ligation. Despite its advantages, vasectomy uptake remains very low globally due to male misconceptions.
questions.question: Which of the following CORRECTLY describes vasectomy compared to female tubal ligation?

options: Deep pelvic nodes without inguinal involvement
questions.explanation: Vulval carcinoma spreads in an orderly fashion, first to the superficial inguinal nodes before progressing to deep inguinofemoral and then pelvic nodes, which is why sentinel or superficial inguinal node assessment underpins surgical staging and management decisions.
questions.question: Groin lymph node dissection in early vulval carcinoma is performed primarily because lymphatic spread occurs FIRST to which nodal group?

options: Permitted only after an AIDS-defining illness
Safe only if her partner is HIV-negative too
Contraindicated absolutely in all HIV-positive women
Restricted to women with CD4 above 500 only
Safe to start and continue if she is clinically well
questions.question: In HIV-positive women, WHO guidance regarding IUD use states that the method is generally:
questions.explanation: Current WHO guidance classifies IUD initiation and continuation as generally safe for women living with HIV who are clinically well, whether or not on antiretroviral therapy, since HIV status alone does not significantly increase complication risk from IUD use.

The ischio-rectal fossa has the pudendal vessels and nerve (housed within the pudendal canal/Alcock's canal) on its lateral wall. The medial wall is formed by the fascial covering of the levator ani and external anal sphincter. The posterior wall is the sacrotuberous ligament, and the floor is formed by skin and subcutaneous fat.
questions.question: In the ischio-rectal fossa, the pudendal canal (Alcock's canal) is found on which wall?
When prescribing a diaphragm, the CORRECT sequence for determining the appropriate size involves:
questions.explanation: Diaphragm sizing requires pelvic examination to identify the posterior fornix with the examining finger, then marking where the finger meets the pubic bone (pubococcygeal distance). This measurement approximates the appropriate diaphragm diameter. Five millimeters are added to account for vaginal expansion during sexual arousal. Both excessively small and large diaphragms have increased failure rates.
options: Performing pelvic examination, identifying the posterior fornix, measuring the pubococcygeal distance, then adding 5mm for vaginal expansion
Measuring vaginal pH and choosing based on acid-base balance
Prescribing the largest size the patient can insert without discomfort regardless of anatomical measurement
Using cervical os diameter as the exclusive determinant of diaphragm size
Having the patient insert trial diaphragms and choose by comfort alone

questions.explanation: Dysgerminomas are highly radiosensitive and chemosensitive germ cell tumours, meaning that even if recurrence occurs after conservative fertility-sparing surgery, subsequent treatment achieves excellent cure rates, supporting the rationale for fertility preservation in early-stage disease.
options: Resistant to all forms of chemotherapy
Only treatable by radical pelvic exenteration
Never associated with recurrence after any treatment
Highly sensitive to chemotherapy and radiotherapy
questions.question: A young woman undergoing fertility-sparing surgery for a Stage IA dysgerminoma should be counselled that recurrence, if it occurs, is MOST likely to be treated successfully because dysgerminomas are:

questions.explanation: CA-125 is elevated in approximately 25% of non-gynaecological conditions including cancers of the GI tract, breast cancer, liver cirrhosis, and inflammatory conditions. This lack of specificity means CA-125 cannot be used in isolation for diagnosis and must be interpreted alongside clinical findings and imaging.
questions.question: Which non-gynaecological condition can elevate CA-125 levels and thus confound its interpretation as a tumour marker?
Postoperative paralytic ileus after major gynaecological surgery is BEST managed initially by:
questions.explanation: Postoperative paralytic ileus is managed conservatively with nasogastric tube decompression (if vomiting or distension is severe), IV fluid and electrolyte replacement (hypokalaemia is a common perpetuating cause), and withholding oral intake until bowel sounds return and flatus passes. Urgent return to theatre is reserved for suspected mechanical obstruction or perforation.

questions.question: Carcinoma-in-situ of the cervix is distinguished from CIN III by which additional feature?
questions.explanation: CIN III includes severe dysplasia and carcinoma-in-situ (CIS). CIS is defined as a lesion where all or most of the epithelium shows cellular features of carcinoma without stromal invasion, and crucially, the lesion involves the glands (endocervical crypts). This glandular involvement distinguishes CIS from severe dysplasia (CIN III) which does not show glandular involvement.

options: Large intramural fibroid without cavity distortion
questions.question: Which fibroid type is most closely associated with recurrent implantation failure and early pregnancy loss?
questions.explanation: Submucosal fibroids distort the endometrial cavity and are most strongly associated with menorrhagia, recurrent implantation failure, and early pregnancy loss. By altering the uterine cavity environment, blood supply, and endometrial receptivity, they interfere with implantation and early placentation. They are best assessed and treated hysteroscopically.

questions.question: In moderate to severe endometriosis (non-menstrual phase), CA-125 levels typically range between:
questions.explanation: In moderate to severe endometriosis during the non-menstrual phase, CA-125 levels typically range between 13–95 u/ml. Normal women without endometriosis have levels of 8–22 u/ml, and minimal to mild endometriosis shows 14–31 u/ml. Levels during the menstrual phase are higher, and a menstrual to follicular phase ratio above 1.5 is a more sensitive marker.

questions.question: A 33-year-old with subfertility and recurrent miscarriage is found to have a submucosal fibroid on hysteroscopy. Which mechanism MOST directly explains how this fibroid impairs implantation?
questions.explanation: Submucosal fibroids distort the endometrial cavity contour and disrupt local endometrial receptivity and vascularity, impairing implantation and increasing miscarriage risk, unlike subserosal or small intramural fibroids that do not affect the cavity. This distinction is why hysteroscopic myomectomy specifically targets cavity-distorting fibroids. Tubal ostia compression is a less typical mechanism for submucosal lesions confined to the cavity.
options: Compression of the fallopian tube ostia
Distortion of the endometrial cavity contour

questions.question: A 25-year-old woman presents with vulval pruritus and curdly white vaginal discharge with satellite lesions on the vulva. She is 28 weeks pregnant. What is the MOST likely organism and treatment of choice in pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Curdly white discharge with vulval pruritus and satellite lesions is characteristic of vulvovaginal candidiasis (Candida albicans). In pregnancy, topical clotrimazole pessaries are the treatment of choice as systemic azoles (fluconazole) are associated with teratogenicity in the first trimester and caution is advised throughout pregnancy. Pregnancy predisposes to candidiasis through elevated oestrogen, glycogen, and immune modulation. Teaching materials list candidiasis under curdly white/creamy discharge.

Migraine with aura is a recognised risk factor for ischaemic stroke, and combined oestrogen-containing contraceptives further increase this risk, making them contraindicated in this group under UK Medical Eligibility Criteria category 4. Progestogen-only methods, including the pill, implant, and intrauterine system, do not carry the same oestrogen-related vascular risk and remain appropriate options. This distinction is a common examination point in contraceptive counselling.
questions.question: A woman with migraine with aura wishes to start hormonal contraception. Which method is MOST appropriately contraindicated due to increased stroke risk?

questions.explanation: The FIGO prognostic scoring system incorporates factors including age, antecedent pregnancy, interval since index pregnancy, pretreatment hCG level, tumour size, site and number of metastases, and prior failed chemotherapy, together classifying patients as low or high risk to guide treatment intensity.
questions.question: The FIGO scoring system used to classify gestational trophoblastic neoplasia risk includes which of the following parameters?

questions.explanation: Unopposed oestrogen HRT increases endometrial carcinoma risk only in women with an intact uterus, as it stimulates unchecked endometrial proliferation without the balancing effect of progesterone. A woman who has undergone hysterectomy has no endometrium and therefore no risk of endometrial carcinoma from oestrogen-only HRT. Indeed, adding progestogen to HRT in a hysterectomized woman is unnecessary and may increase breast cancer risk.
questions.question: A post-menopausal woman asks about treatment with oestrogen-only HRT. She has had a hysterectomy. The risk of endometrial carcinoma from unopposed oestrogen does NOT apply to her because:
options: Post-menopausal women have lower oestrogen sensitivity
No uterus; no endometrium for malignant transformation
Post-menopausal oestrogen metabolism prevents endometrial stimulation
Oestrogen-only HRT uses natural oestrogens that are non-carcinogenic

questions.explanation: A high recto-vaginal fistula allows stool to bypass the voluntary anal sphincter complex, which is the primary continence mechanism, resulting in leakage that the patient cannot consciously control regardless of stool consistency. A low fistula near the anal verge, by contrast, may still allow some sphincteric control of continence. This distinction affects both symptom severity and repair planning.
questions.question: A patient with a high recto-vaginal fistula is noted to have worse faecal incontinence than a patient with a low fistula of similar size. What anatomical reason best explains why leakage from a high RVF is harder to control?
options: Bypasses the voluntary sphincter, causing leakage
Low fistulae are surrounded by more scar tissue
High fistulae only leak liquid stool, never solid stool
High fistulae always coexist with rectal prolapse
High fistulae are always larger in diameter
Antigens unique to one specific neoplasm
Both cancer cells and normal adult tissue
questions.explanation: Class 2 tumour markers are antigens expressed by many or most tumours of a specific histological type and by other histological types, but NOT expressed by normal adult tissue. Class 1 markers are unique to a specific neoplasm; Class 3 markers are expressed by both malignant and normal adult tissues.
questions.question: A tumour marker classified as Class 2 means it is expressed by:
A 38-year-old woman reports menstrual cycles occurring every 21 days with normal flow duration and volume. Using PALM-COEIN terminology, what is this bleeding pattern MOST correctly termed?
questions.explanation: The FIGO PALM-COEIN classification defines frequency separately from volume and regularity; cycles shorter than 24 days with normal flow are classified as frequent menstrual bleeding. Heavy bleeding refers to excessive volume, not frequency, while irregular bleeding describes variation in cycle length between cycles. Correct terminology guides appropriate targeted investigation.

options: Onset with heavy bleeding followed by painless cervical dilatation
Painless cervical dilatation with minimal bleeding or contractions
Gradual onset of labour-like contractions progressing over days
Fever and uterine tenderness preceding cervical opening
Sudden rupture of membranes with simultaneous contractions
questions.question: Second trimester spontaneous abortion from cervical incompetence typically presents with which characteristic pattern?
questions.explanation: Cervical incompetence classically presents with painless, silent cervical dilatation in the second trimester without preceding contractions or significant bleeding, distinguishing it from inevitable abortion (which involves pain and bleeding). The pregnant patient often notices the cervix is open only at routine examination or when presenting with pressure symptoms or bulging membranes. This silent progression is what makes it a distinct and clinically important diagnosis requiring prophylactic cerclage in future pregnancies.

DHEA (dihydroepiandrosterone) and its sulfate (DHEA-S) from the adrenal gland rise before any visible physical sign of puberty appears. In girls, DHEA-S reaches higher concentrations at the same bone age than in boys, and is responsible for adrenarche (pubic and axillary hair development). The exact neuroendocrine trigger for adrenarche remains incompletely understood but occurs independently of hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis activation.
options: A rise in oestradiol causing breast budding
A surge in FSH triggering follicular development
A surge in GnRH causing pulsatile gonadotrophin release
Elevation of DHEA-S from the adrenal gland
questions.question: The endocrinological event at puberty that is detected EARLIEST, before any visible physical sign, is:
The hCG doubling time during early viable intrauterine pregnancy is:
questions.explanation: In a normal viable intrauterine pregnancy, hCG rises exponentially with a doubling time of 1.3 to 2 days until 9–10 weeks of gestation. A 66% rise over 48 hours represents the lower limit of normal; slower rises suggest an ectopic pregnancy or non-viable intrauterine pregnancy, though 15% exceptions exist in each direction.

questions.question: When both a vesico-vaginal fistula and a recto-vaginal fistula coexist, which should be repaired first and why?
options: VVF first; simultaneous repair risks breakdown
RVF first, to avoid faecal contamination during VVF repair
Both should be repaired simultaneously to minimise anaesthetic risk
RVF first, as it is technically easier and allows safer VVF repair later
The larger fistula should always be repaired first
questions.explanation: When VVF and RVF coexist, VVF should be repaired first because borrowing tissues to fill in vaginal defects on both the anterior and posterior walls simultaneously produces tension favouring breakdown. If a 2nd attempt at VVF repair is needed, scarring from the posterior wall repair will interfere with access. The recommendation is to repair VVF first, then the rectal defect 3 weeks later if the anterior wall is soundly healed.

Successful tubal reanastomosis depends primarily on the length and quality of remaining healthy fallopian tube after removal of the damaged or occluded segment, since adequate tubal length is needed to restore normal function. Clip sterilisation typically damages less tubal tissue than methods such as cautery, often allowing better reversal outcomes, but the deciding factor remains available healthy tube length. Time since the original procedure and blood type do not directly determine surgical success.
options: Age of the sterilisation clips used
Number of years since the procedure
Length of remaining healthy tube available
Woman's blood type at the time
questions.question: A woman requests reversal of a previous tubal ligation performed five years ago using clip sterilisation. Which factor MOST strongly influences the likely success of surgical reversal?

questions.explanation: Poorly controlled gestational diabetes exposes the fetus to excess maternal glucose, stimulating fetal hyperinsulinaemia and increased fat deposition, leading to macrosomia, which in turn increases the risk of birth trauma, shoulder dystocia, and operative delivery. This differs from pre-existing (pre-gestational) diabetes with poor early control, which is more specifically linked to congenital structural anomalies from hyperglycaemia during organogenesis. Good glycaemic control throughout pregnancy reduces the risk of macrosomia and its associated complications.
options: Fetal growth restriction in every case
questions.question: A 24-year-old primigravida at 28 weeks is diagnosed with gestational diabetes on oral glucose tolerance testing. Which fetal complication is she at increased risk of if her glycaemic control remains poor?

questions.explanation: Women living with HIV who wish to conceive are advised to first achieve sustained viral suppression through effective antiretroviral therapy, which substantially reduces the risk of transmission to the partner during conception attempts and to the baby during pregnancy, delivery, and breastfeeding.
questions.question: A woman recently diagnosed with HIV should be counselled that pregnancy planning is MOST safely approached by:
options: Using only traditional fertility awareness methods without medical input
Discontinuing antiretroviral therapy once pregnancy is confirmed
Achieving viral suppression on antiretroviral therapy before attempting conception
Conceiving as soon as possible before starting any treatment
Avoiding pregnancy permanently regardless of treatment status

questions.explanation: Diabetes commonly causes erectile dysfunction through a combination of vascular endothelial damage and peripheral neuropathy affecting the nerves and blood vessels supplying erectile tissue, making organic vascular and neuropathic causes the most common mechanism rather than purely psychological factors.
questions.question: Erectile dysfunction in a man with well-controlled type 2 diabetes is MOST commonly attributable to which underlying mechanism?
options: Medication-induced effect only, unrelated to diabetes itself
Primary psychological anxiety unrelated to diabetes
Vascular and neuropathic damage to erectile tissue
Hormonal deficiency of testosterone in almost all cases
Structural abnormality of the penis present since birth

questions.explanation: Hysteroscopy allows direct visualisation of the endometrial cavity, enabling targeted biopsy of focal abnormalities such as polyps that might be missed by blind pipelle sampling, which relies on random tissue capture and can under-sample localised lesions.
questions.question: Hysteroscopy with directed biopsy is MOST useful over blind endometrial sampling because it allows:
options: Direct visualisation and targeted biopsy of focal endometrial lesions
Complete replacement of hysterectomy in all cases

questions.question: Cystometry is performed with subtracted abdominal pressure recording. What is the specific purpose of subtracting abdominal pressure from the total measured bladder pressure?
options: To measure urethral closure pressure directly
To isolate the true detrusor pressure component
questions.explanation: Subtracting rectal (abdominal) pressure from total intravesical pressure isolates the detrusor pressure component, allowing the clinician to distinguish pressure rises caused by involuntary detrusor contraction from those caused simply by raised intra-abdominal pressure such as straining. This differentiation is essential to correctly diagnose detrusor instability versus stress incontinence. It underpins accurate urodynamic diagnosis.

questions.question: Which of the following structures is specifically assessed by rectovaginal examination that cannot be adequately palpated by bimanual vaginal examination alone?
questions.explanation: Rectovaginal examination allows the examiner to palpate the posterior uterine wall, rectovaginal septal masses, uterosacral and sacrococcygeal ligaments, and cul-de-sac masses that are inaccessible or poorly defined on standard bimanual examination. This is also mandatory in staging cervical cancer. The other structures listed are accessible without rectal examination.

questions.question: GnRH agonist pretreatment before myomectomy is used primarily to achieve which effect?
options: Reduction in fibroid size and vascularity
Permanent cure of fibroids without surgery
questions.explanation: GnRH agonists induce a hypo-oestrogenic state that shrinks fibroids and reduces their vascularity, facilitating easier surgical removal with less intraoperative blood loss. The effect is temporary, and fibroids typically regrow once treatment is stopped.

questions.question: Among all ART complications listed, multiple gestation is specifically highlighted. What is the PRIMARY strategy used in modern IVF practice to reduce the multiple gestation rate?
questions.explanation: Single embryo transfer (SET) is the primary strategy to reduce IVF-related multiple gestation, as transferring two or more embryos directly multiplies multiple pregnancy risk. With improved embryo selection (time-lapse imaging, PGT-A) and cryopreservation, cumulative pregnancy rates from SET approach those from double embryo transfer while dramatically reducing twin and higher-order multiple pregnancies. Many European countries have legislated for elective SET as standard practice.
options: Reducing gonadotropin doses to prevent multiple follicle development
Using GnRH antagonist protocols instead of long protocols
Single embryo transfer (SET) in good-prognosis patients
Transferring only blastocysts instead of cleavage-stage embryos

questions.question: Which of the following is a paraphilic disorder according to DSM-5?
questions.explanation: Pedophilic disorder (sexual attraction to prepubescent children causing distress or involving behavior) is classified as a paraphilic disorder in DSM-5. Homosexuality was removed from DSM in 1973; bisexuality, fantasy, and masturbation are not disorders. Paraphilic disorders are defined by intense, persistent atypical sexual interests that cause distress or harm to self or others.

Dyschezia in endometriosis results from implants in the rectovaginal septum and rectosigmoid colon, which during menstruation swell with haemorrhage and prostaglandin release, causing pain on defaecation. Deep infiltrating endometriosis (DIE) of the rectovaginal septum is the most common cause of cyclical bowel symptoms in endometriosis. MRI is the best imaging modality for mapping DIE before surgery.
questions.question: Endometriosis affecting the bowel causes cyclical dyschezia (painful defaecation). Which structure's infiltration causes this symptom?
A woman using the Billings Ovulation Method experiences unusual cervical mucus during a cycle in which she is taking antibiotics. She should:
options: Discontinue the Billings Method and use emergency contraception
Ignore the mucus changes as antibiotics routinely cause false mucus signals
Record the unusual mucus as a drug effect and consider the day infertile
Apply the Billings rules strictly — if uncertain, treat the day as potentially fertile and abstain
Switch to BBT-only observation for that cycle
questions.explanation: The Billings Ovulation Method principle of 'when in doubt, leave it out' (treat uncertain days as fertile) is the fundamental safety rule. Any unusual or confusing mucus pattern — whether from antibiotics, illness, stress, or hormonal changes — should default to treating that day as potentially fertile. This conservative approach maximizes effectiveness. Women are taught to note any unusual patterns and consult their NFP teacher for interpretation guidance.

questions.question: A 28-year-old presents with 6 months of infertility. In gynaecological history, the MOST informative single question to ask is:
options: What contraceptive did you use before?
Is there a family history of twins?
questions.explanation: Determining whether the patient has regular, ovulatory cycles is fundamental in infertility assessment, as anovulation is one of the most common and treatable causes. Ovulation symptoms (mid-cycle pain, cervical mucus changes, premenstrual symptoms) and cycle regularity guide the initial diagnostic pathway. Other questions are relevant but secondary in establishing aetiology.

questions.question: Among barrier contraceptive methods, which has the LOWEST perfect-use failure rate?
questions.explanation: Among barrier methods, the male latex condom has the lowest perfect-use failure rate of approximately 2 per 100 women per year. The diaphragm with spermicide has a perfect-use rate of approximately 6%. The cervical cap in nulliparous women is approximately 9%; the female condom approximately 5%; spermicide alone ~18% (highest). Correct and consistent condom use achieves the best outcomes among barrier methods.

questions.question: The Bartholin's glands are contained in which compartment of the perineum?
questions.explanation: The superficial compartment (superficial perineal pouch) lies between the subcutaneous tissues and the perineal membrane. It contains the clitoris (crura and vestibular bulb), Bartholin's gland, bulbospongiosus, ischiocavernosus, and superficial transverse perineal muscle. Bartholin's gland is anatomically a component of this pouch.

questions.question: Which of the following presentations MOST suggests that an IUD has been expelled without the patient's knowledge?
options: Increased vaginal discharge and fever 2 weeks after insertion
Patient cannot feel the IUD threads and has onset of unintended pregnancy
Patient reports feeling 'threads' deeper than before
Severe cramping immediately after insertion lasting 30 minutes
questions.explanation: Unrecognized IUD expulsion most commonly presents as unintended pregnancy in a woman who believed she was protected. Silent expulsion may also be detected when a patient reports she can no longer palpate the threads on self-examination (though absent threads may also indicate upward thread migration). The first sign of expulsion is often a missed period or positive pregnancy test. Inability to feel threads plus pregnancy is the classic presentation.

Regular use of vaginal dilators after pelvic radiotherapy helps maintain vaginal calibre and elasticity by preventing fibrotic narrowing, reducing the risk of stenosis that can otherwise significantly impair sexual function and future gynaecological examination.
options: Avoidance of all vaginal examination indefinitely
Early resumption of unprotected intercourse alone without dilators
questions.question: Radiotherapy-induced vaginal stenosis following treatment for cervical or vaginal cancer is MOST appropriately prevented by:

questions.explanation: WHO recommends progestogen-only pills (POP) be started from Day 21 postpartum (3 weeks) in breastfeeding women to minimize any theoretical effect of progestogen exposure on the breastfed neonate's immature liver during the first weeks of life. Starting earlier (Day 1 or 2) is recommended only in non-breastfeeding women or in special circumstances. Combined pills are inappropriate due to estrogen's lactation suppression.
options: Combined oral contraceptive started at 3 weeks postpartum
Etonogestrel implant inserted on Day 1 postpartum
Progestogen-only pill started on Day 21 postpartum
questions.question: Which progestogen-only preparation is MOST appropriate for immediate postnatal use in a breastfeeding woman who delivers at 34 weeks' gestation?

options: Suppression of LH secretion from the pituitary
Anti-androgenic binding at testicular androgen receptors
Blocking epididymal sperm maturation through bacterial overgrowth inhibition
Causing retrograde ejaculation through sympathetic nerve damage
Spermatotoxicity through oxidative stress in germ cells
questions.question: Nitrofurantoin is listed among drugs causing male infertility. A 32-year-old man has been on long-term nitrofurantoin for recurrent urinary tract infections. By which mechanism does nitrofurantoin impair male fertility?
questions.explanation: Nitrofurantoin impairs spermatogenesis through oxidative stress mechanisms — its reactive metabolites generate free radicals that damage DNA and mitochondria in developing germ cells. This is reversible upon stopping the drug. As part of the infertility history, clinicians should specifically enquire about nitrofurantoin, sulphasalazine, and cimetidine use, as these represent important reversible iatrogenic causes of male factor infertility.

options: Antepartum haemorrhage causing chronic uteroplacental insufficiency
Excessive use of prophylactic oxytocin suppressing prolactin
Postpartum pituitary necrosis from hypovolemic shock
Uterine atony causing cortisol deficiency affecting the hypothalamus
Placental abruption damaging the hypothalamic-portal circulation
questions.explanation: Sheehan's syndrome results from postpartum pituitary necrosis caused by severe hypovolemic shock during or after delivery, most commonly from postpartum haemorrhage. The pituitary is particularly vulnerable at term due to its enlarged vascular state. Loss of pituitary gonadotrophs causes hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, resulting in amenorrhoea, inability to lactate, and generalized hypopituitarism.
questions.question: Sheehan's syndrome is a pituitary cause of infertility. A woman presents with amenorrhoea and inability to lactate following a postpartum haemorrhage. What is the pathophysiological mechanism?

questions.explanation: Urethral catheterisation is routinely performed postoperatively after prolapse repair to prevent urinary retention and to rest the bladder. The bladder may be temporarily dysfunctional following pelvic floor repair, especially anterior colporrhaphy. Additional post-operative measures include vaginal packing to reduce bleeding and antibiotics as necessary.
questions.question: Following surgery for prolapse, which immediate complication is prevented by urethral catheterisation?

questions.explanation: Elevated prolactin suppresses pulsatile GnRH release from the hypothalamus, which in turn reduces pituitary FSH and LH secretion, impairing normal follicular development and ovulation. This is why hyperprolactinaemia is a recognised and treatable cause of anovulatory infertility, often accompanied by galactorrhoea and amenorrhoea. Treatment with a dopamine agonist typically restores normal ovulatory cycles.
questions.question: A 32-year-old woman presents with anovulatory infertility and is found to have a markedly elevated serum prolactin level. Which mechanism explains how hyperprolactinaemia causes anovulation?
options: Prolactin suppresses hypothalamic GnRH pulsatility, reducing FSH and LH secretion
Prolactin causes premature luteinization of every follicle
Prolactin has no effect on the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis
Immediate IUS removal as amenorrhoea indicates device failure
First exclude pregnancy, then reassure if negative as LNG-IUS-induced amenorrhoea is expected and safe
Prescribe combined OCP cyclically to induce withdrawal bleeds
Order urgent pelvic MRI to assess endometrial response
Start progesterone supplementation to prevent endometrial hyperplasia
questions.explanation: LNG-IUS-induced amenorrhoea is expected in approximately 20–30% of users by year 1, increasing to 50% by year 5, due to progressive endometrial atrophy from local levonorgestrel exposure. Before attributing amenorrhoea to the IUS, pregnancy must always be excluded with a urine or serum hCG test. If negative, amenorrhoea is a recognised beneficial side effect and can be positively framed for women who welcome it. No hormonal supplementation is needed.
questions.question: Amenorrhoea in a woman using the levonorgestrel IUS (Mirena) should prompt which initial clinical action?

questions.explanation: Genuine stress incontinence (GSI) presents with involuntary urine loss with coughing, sneezing, laughing, or lifting. Physical signs include coincidental downswing of the bladder neck with leakage in the standing position. Importantly, approximately 50% of women with GSI have associated prolapse of the vagina. This frequent coexistence means both conditions often need to be addressed surgically at the same time.
questions.question: A woman presents with involuntary urine loss associated with an unexpected, sudden rise in abdominal pressure when she sneezes. On examination, the downswing of the bladder neck with urinary leakage is noted. What additional finding would be present in approximately half of such patients?

questions.explanation: HIV transmission risk per act is highest with receptive anal intercourse (fragile rectal epithelium) combined with acute HIV infection (when viral load is at its peak — often 100–1,000 times higher than in chronic infection). Antiretroviral therapy effectively reduces viral load to undetectable levels, achieving U=U (Undetectable = Untransmittable). Oral sex carries negligible transmission risk without oral ulcers or bleeding.
options: Insertive vaginal intercourse with a chronically infected partner on antiretroviral therapy
Oral sex between two adults with no visible oral ulcers
Insertive vaginal intercourse with an asymptomatic partner
Receptive anal intercourse with an acutely HIV-infected partner during seroconversion illness
Mutual masturbation without exchange of blood or semen
questions.question: HIV transmission efficiency (probability of transmission per act of unprotected intercourse) is HIGHEST in which scenario?
Vaginal clear cell adenocarcinoma in young women has been historically linked to in-utero exposure to:
questions.explanation: In-utero exposure to diethylstilboestrol, a synthetic oestrogen once used to prevent miscarriage, is strongly associated with clear cell adenocarcinoma of the vagina and cervix in young women exposed as fetuses, a link established through cohort studies decades later.

questions.question: Which specific investigation for pelvic organ prolapse provides 'detailed pictures of structures inside the pelvic area'?
questions.explanation: Computed tomography (CT) scan produces detailed pictures of structures inside the pelvic area and is listed among the preoperative investigations before surgical correction of prolapse. IVP shows the urinary tract (kidneys, ureters, bladder), cystoscopy shows the bladder interior, and urodynamic studies assess bladder function. CT provides cross-sectional anatomical detail of pelvic structures, lymph nodes, and any associated masses.

options: Cyst with mild discomfort at 16 weeks
Acute pain suggesting torsion or haemorrhage
Cyst discovered incidentally at dating scan
questions.question: Which of the following is an indication for IMMEDIATE surgical intervention in a pregnant woman with an ovarian cyst?
questions.explanation: Acute pain suggesting torsion or haemorrhage is an absolute indication for immediate surgical intervention in a pregnant woman with an ovarian cyst. The operation should be covered with tocolytics and performed in a centre with intensive neonatal care facilities. No urgent operation should be postponed solely because of pregnancy.

questions.question: Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV) is listed as a cause of which type of fistula?
questions.explanation: Recto-vaginal fistula causes include: tissue necrosis following obstructed labour, incompletely repaired 3rd degree perineal tear, rectal injury during pelvic procedures, radiation therapy for cervical carcinoma, and LGV (lymphogranuloma venereum). LGV is a sexually transmitted infection caused by Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1, L2, L3, which causes destructive granulomatous inflammation of the anorectum and perirectal tissues.

questions.question: Diagnostic laparoscopy has specific absolute contraindications. Which of the following represents an ABSOLUTE (not relative) contraindication to laparoscopy?
options: Previous abdominal surgery with suspected adhesions
questions.explanation: Intestinal obstruction is an absolute contraindication to laparoscopy because gas-filled distended bowel loops make safe trocar insertion impossible and dramatically increase the risk of bowel perforation during Veress needle and trocar placement. Additionally, the pneumoperitoneum further distends already compromised bowel and impairs diaphragmatic function. The other options are relative contraindications that may be managed with appropriate precautions and technique.

questions.question: Menometrorrhagia describes uterine bleeding that is:
options: Irregular frequency, duration, and excessive amount
Regular but prolonged in duration only
questions.explanation: Menometrorrhagia combines the features of menorrhagia (excessive flow) and metrorrhagia (irregular intermenstrual bleeding), resulting in bleeding that is totally irregular in frequency, excessive in amount, and prolonged in duration. Causes include conditions such as early abortion, hydatidiform mole, choriocarcinoma, ectopic pregnancy, and perimenopausal anovulatory cycles. It represents the most chaotic bleeding pattern and should always prompt thorough investigation.

options: Stimulating GnRH from the hypothalamus to suppress FSH
Binding androgen/progesterone receptors, displacing testosterone from SHBG, inhibiting steroidogenesis
Directly suppressing ovarian granulosa cell oestradiol production via LH receptor blockade
questions.explanation: Danazol (an isoxazole derivative of 17-alpha-ethinyltestosterone) produces amenorrhoea by multiple mechanisms: it binds to androgen, progesterone, and glucocorticoid receptors; displaces testosterone from SHBG, increasing free testosterone; prevents midcycle FSH and LH surges without significantly suppressing basal levels; and inhibits enzymes involved in steroidogenesis. The resulting low-oestrogen, androgen-dominant environment prevents endometrial growth, producing amenorrhoea.
questions.question: Danazol in DUB produces a low-oestrogen environment by which mechanism?
TATS (Tumour Associated Trypsin Inhibitor) has been found in cyst fluids of which type of ovarian cancer and complements which other marker?
questions.explanation: TATS (Tumour Associated Trypsin Inhibitor) has been found in veins, serum, and cyst fluids of mucinous carcinoma. It complements CA-125 as a clinical monitoring tool for serous carcinoma, providing additive information when the two markers are used together.

options: Give the injection immediately with no further assessment
Assume pregnancy has definitely occurred without testing
Delay the injection for another full year automatically
Refuse the injection permanently regardless of findings
Exclude pregnancy before giving the next injection
questions.question: A woman returns for her DMPA injection 16 weeks after her last dose, beyond the recommended grace period. The MOST appropriate action is:
questions.explanation: When a woman presents significantly beyond the recommended interval for her repeat DMPA injection, pregnancy should be reasonably excluded before the next dose is administered, since ovarian suppression may have waned, allowing a window during which conception could theoretically have occurred.

questions.question: Before elective repair of a rectovaginal fistula, repair should be deferred for how long after the causative labour or previous repair attempt?
questions.explanation: Before repair of a rectovaginal fistula, repair should be deferred for 2 months after the causative labour or the previous attempt at repair. This allows oedema to resolve, infection to subside, and tissues to return to normal vascularity and pliability. For ischaemic necrosis fistulae (such as those from obstructed labour), delay of 2-3 months is recommended until the effects of trauma and superadded infection have completely subsided.

questions.question: Which hormone is PRIMARILY responsible for the adolescent growth spurt, working synergistically with gonadal steroids?
questions.explanation: Growth hormone, in synergy with gonadal steroids (oestrogen in females, testosterone in males), is primarily responsible for the adolescent growth spurt. Growth hormone stimulates hepatic IGF-1 production, which drives longitudinal bone growth. Oestrogen initially stimulates growth hormone secretion and bone formation, then drives epiphyseal fusion which terminates the growth spurt.

Psammoma bodies, which are laminated calcified concretions, are a characteristic histological feature of serous ovarian tumours, both benign and malignant, and can also be seen in serous tumours of the peritoneum and fallopian tube.
questions.question: A histological finding of psammoma bodies within an ovarian tumour is MOST characteristic of which subtype?

questions.explanation: Dermoid cysts are the commonest ovarian tumours in young women, with a median age of approximately 30 years. They are bilateral in about 10–11% of cases and are rarely larger than 15 cm in diameter. They arise from totipotential germ cells and contain ectodermal derivatives.
questions.question: Dermoid cysts (mature cystic teratomas) are MOST common in which age group and are bilateral in approximately:

questions.explanation: Short stature in Turner's syndrome results from haploinsufficiency of genes located on the sex chromosomes — specifically the SHOX gene — that are normally present on both sex chromosomes and contribute to skeletal growth. The absence of the second sex chromosome (whether X or Y) removes one copy of these height-determining genes, resulting in short stature independent of gonadal failure. This is why growth hormone therapy is used, as it partially compensates.
questions.question: In Turner's syndrome (45,XO), short stature is caused by:
options: Growth hormone deficiency from pituitary dysfunction
Absent growth genes on X chromosome
Delayed bone age from oestrogen deficiency
Nutritional deficiency associated with cardiac defects

questions.explanation: Prophylactic antibiotics for gynaecological surgery are selected to cover the likely contaminating organisms from vaginal and skin flora, including gram-negative enteric organisms and anaerobes, reducing the risk of surgical site infection and pelvic abscess formation.
questions.question: The MOST appropriate perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis choice for elective gynaecological surgery typically targets which organism group?
options: Gram-negative and anaerobic vaginal and skin flora

questions.explanation: Tuberculosis of the cervix is very rare and is secondary to infection in the fallopian tubes and uterus (the primary genital TB sites), following coitus (rare route). Features are hyperplastic or ulcerative lesions. Investigation requires microscopy and biopsy. Treatment is anti-TB drugs. This contrasts with pulmonary TB where haematogenous spread to other organs is the usual mechanism.
options: Haematogenous spread from any primary site
questions.question: Cervical tuberculosis is described as very rare and typically secondary to infection from which primary sites?
FSH and LH levels are specifically measured in DUB evaluation to help diagnose which two conditions?
questions.explanation: Plasma FSH and LH levels in DUB investigations are specifically used to diagnose two conditions: elevated FSH and LH (particularly FSH > 40 IU/L with low oestradiol) confirms menopause or premature ovarian failure; and an elevated LH:FSH ratio (greater than 2:1 or 3:1) with mildly elevated LH suggests polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) — a common cause of anovulatory DUB. Both conditions require specific management approaches beyond standard DUB therapy.
options: Coagulation disorders and Von Willebrand disease

questions.explanation: Day 21 plasma progesterone (measured 7 days after expected ovulation in a 28-day cycle) is used to diagnose corpus luteum insufficiency — a low progesterone level (less than 10–16 nmol/L depending on laboratory threshold) indicates inadequate corpus luteum function. This is associated with irregular ripening of the endometrium, premenstrual spotting, and shortened cycles. It is one of the specific investigations listed for DUB alongside FSH, LH, prolactin, and thyroid function tests.
questions.question: Day 21 plasma progesterone measurement is used to diagnose which specific DUB pathology?
In primary repair of a 3rd degree perineal tear, the rectal wall defect is closed in layers that evert the raw edges towards the lumen of the rectum. Which technique is used for the anal sphincter?
questions.explanation: In primary repair of 3rd degree tear: the rectal wall defect is closed layer by layer, everting raw edges towards the rectum lumen. The torn ends of the retracted external anal sphincter are identified with tissue forceps and carefully united in front of the reconstructed anal canal with interrupted sutures. The posterior vaginal wall is repaired to the fourchette, and the perineal body is reconstructed by drawing the levator ani between the rectal and vaginal repair lines.
options: No suture as it heals spontaneously
Ligation and division of sphincter ends

questions.explanation: Filshie clips and Fallope rings (silicone bands) are mechanical occlusion devices applied laparoscopically to the fallopian tubes without using electrical energy, eliminating the risk of thermal bowel injury associated with diathermy methods. Filshie clips have a high success rate (failure rate <0.3 per 100 women-years) with the advantage of minimal tube destruction, potentially allowing reversal. They are preferred over diathermy where reversal may be considered.
questions.question: Laparoscopic sterilization is a therapeutic indication for laparoscopy. Which method of laparoscopic sterilization involves mechanical occlusion of the fallopian tubes without electrical current?
Ovarian enlargement in a woman on fertility drugs is MOST likely due to:
questions.explanation: Follicular cysts are often associated with fertility drugs such as clomiphene and HMG, which cause ovarian hyperstimulation and can result in multiple large follicular cysts. These are physiological in nature and are typically reversible when the medication is discontinued.

options: Ovarian cysts, functional ovarian cysts, ovarian cancer
Liver adenoma and focal nodular hyperplasia
Breast cancer in BRCA1 mutation carriers
questions.explanation: COC use is associated with a significant reduction in ovarian cancer risk (approximately 50% reduction with 5+ years use, persisting decades after discontinuation), reduced functional ovarian cysts (due to ovulation suppression), and reduced risk of endometrial cancer. These non-contraceptive benefits are well-established and can factor into prescribing decisions for women with family history of ovarian cancer. These benefits must be weighed against the small increased VTE, stroke, and cervical cancer risks.
questions.question: Combined oral contraceptive pills are associated with a REDUCED risk of which of the following conditions?

questions.explanation: Approximately 5–10% of infertile couples have no recognizable cause identified despite comprehensive investigation, classified as unexplained infertility. This group may have subtle defects in gamete interaction, fertilization, or implantation not detectable by standard tests. Empirical treatments including ovarian stimulation, intrauterine insemination, and IVF are offered, with IVF providing both diagnostic and therapeutic benefit.
questions.question: According to the teaching materials, what proportion of apparently infertile couples have NO recognizable cause identified on full investigation?

questions.explanation: An ideal tumour marker should be specific for the condition, sensitive, and detectable even in pre-malignant stages—NOT only at advanced stages. It should be present in proportion to the amount of malignant tissue and have an assay method that is cheap and easy. No currently available tumour marker meets all these criteria.
questions.question: An ideal tumour marker should possess all of the following characteristics EXCEPT:

questions.explanation: Hypothyroidism causes menorrhagia via two major pathways: first, hypothyroidism suppresses the hypothalamus, causing anovulatory cycles with unopposed oestrogen stimulation of the endometrium; second, it impairs hepatic synthesis of coagulation factors (particularly Factor VIII) and reduces fibrinolytic activity, creating a bleeding tendency. Elevated TRH also stimulates prolactin (causing hyperprolactinaemia), which may contribute to menstrual irregularity. Treatment of hypothyroidism often resolves menorrhagia.
questions.question: The diagnostic rule 'consider hypothyroidism' in DUB is clinically relevant because hypothyroidism can cause menorrhagia through which mechanism?
options: Direct stimulation of endometrial prostaglandin production
Excess TRH stimulating prolactin which causes amenorrhoea
TSH receptor activation in the endometrium causing hyperplasia
Hypothalamic suppression causing anovulation and impaired hepatic coagulation
Reduced FSH from pituitary compression by thyroid enlargement

questions.explanation: Kegel exercises involve repeated voluntary contraction and relaxation of the pelvic floor muscles, improving strength and control, which can benefit conditions such as stress urinary incontinence and, with appropriate guidance, certain aspects of sexual function and pelvic floor awareness.
questions.question: Kegel exercises, often recommended in the management of certain sexual and pelvic floor disorders, primarily aim to:
options: Replace the need for psychosexual therapy entirely
Strengthen and improve control of the pelvic floor muscles
The child can conceive and carry a pregnancy
Ovulation prevents short stature in these children
It confirms a benign constitutional cause of precocious puberty
It means treatment is unnecessary as cycles will normalize
questions.explanation: True (complete) precocious puberty involves full activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis including ovulation. This means the child is biologically capable of conception, making pregnancy a real clinical risk even at very young ages. This psychosocial and medical reality underscores the urgency of treatment to suppress ovulation, menstruation, and fertility while the child matures emotionally and cognitively.
questions.question: Complete (true) precocious puberty involves ovulation. This is clinically significant because:
Female sterilization by tubal ligation is MOST accurately described in counselling as:
options: Fully reversible with guaranteed return of fertility
A permanent method that should be considered irreversible
A temporary method lasting approximately five years
Reversible only in women under twenty years old
Easily reversible with a simple outpatient procedure
questions.explanation: Although tubal reanastomosis is technically possible in some cases, sterilization should always be counselled as a permanent procedure, since reversal surgery has variable and often low success rates and is not widely accessible, so patients must be certain of their decision before proceeding.

options: Daily washout through the distal colostomy loop
questions.explanation: In preoperative management with a colostomy before RVF repair, oral antibiotics are specifically stated to be NOT necessary. Management instead includes daily washout for discharging the colon and rectum through the distal loop of the colostomy, and no restriction on food intake. Post-operatively, a dye test (instilling dye into the distal loop with a clean swab in the vagina) confirms successful repair before colostomy closure. SUBTOPIC 7: VESICO-VAGINAL FISTULA, MICTURITION AND URINARY TRACT MANAGEMENT
questions.question: In the preoperative management with a colostomy before RVF repair, which of the following is specifically stated as NOT necessary?
